```
## Session N (Package P)
- Produced: [what shipped]
- Decisions: [D-numbers from decisions.md, or "none"]
- Tests: [pass/fail summary]
```

## S48b — Intent-classification evaluation substrate
roles: analyst, PM, architect, engineer, technical writer
mode: build session, executing briefs/p13/s48b.md

S48b closed Thread 2 of the parallel post-S47 forward path with the intent-classification evaluation substrate at `contexts/intent_classification_evaluation/` per D137. The substrate answers component-quality questions ("does model X classify Padhanam's intent surface reliably") in minutes against a fixed reference set rather than through multi-minute integration smokes. The S46 (qwen2.5:7b intent-extraction blind-spot) and S47 (qwen2.5:14b hardware-viability) findings were both surfaced by integration smokes asked to do work the architecture is structurally designed to split; S48b closes that methodology gap by building the dedicated evaluation surface the port-and-adapter shape already supported. Six commits land Option B (slim load-bearing version): charter (D137 plus architecture plus three captures methodology entries plus brief preservation); shared_kernel intent-classification primitive extraction plus single-source-of-truth structural test; substrate code (domain plus application plus ports plus Postgres plus Alembic 0022); CLI sub-app plus YAML gold-set fixture plus loader; tenant-isolation harness plus new layers-intent-class-eval import-linter contract; live-stack exercise verifying the substrate against tenant_a with two models. The full P11 mirror's revision-lifecycle gold sets and cross-run-comparison CLI subcommand defer to Phase 2-B+ at named activation triggers per D137 alternatives (c) and (d).

- Produced: Six commits. (1) `docs(charter): land P13 S48b intent-classification evaluation substrate (D137)` (b2e4970) covering D137 at decisions.md, the architecture.md sub-section, three captures methodology candidate entries (component-quality vs integration smoke promotion-ready at two-instance evidence; scope-discipline-at-brief-authoring first-instance; structural-test single-source-of-truth second-instance), the placeholder S48b in-flight marker, and the brief preservation at briefs/p13/s48b.md. (2) `feat(p13/s48b): extract intent-classification prompt and schema to shared_kernel` (91511dd) moving INTENT_EXTRACTION_SCHEMA + EXTRACTION_PREAMBLE + build_extraction_prompt to `shared_kernel/intent_classification.py`, refactoring the cell to consume the shared primitive, plus a four-scenario contract harness at `tests/contract/intent_classification/test_single_source_of_truth.py` asserting Python-identity (`is`) across consumers. (3) `feat(p13/s48b): intent-classification evaluation substrate (domain, ports, app, Postgres, Alembic 0022)` (cfd3450) landing 24 new files covering domain (gold_set, evaluation_run, evaluation_result, metrics), application (3 use cases plus audit_events), ports (3 Protocols), Postgres adapters (repository + reader + _tables) with bound-tenant defence-in-depth, Alembic migration 0022_intent_class_eval_substrate creating three per-tenant tables, and 20 domain-layer unit tests. (4) `feat(p13/s48b): CLI sub-app, YAML gold-set fixture, and fixture loader` (7aa8d8f) landing the typer sub-app at `apps/cli/_intent_classification_eval.py` with `eval start/get/list` subcommands registered under `padhanam intent-classification-eval`, plus the 40-entry gold-set fixture at `tests/fixtures/intent_classification/gold_set.yaml` (12 CreateCase, 12 AddDataPoint including the 4 S46 blind-spot phrasings, 8 ReviseDataPoint, 8 Unclear), plus the YamlGoldSetReader adapter. (5) `test(p13/s48b): tenant_isolation harness + layers-intent-class-eval import-linter contract` (8749442) landing six isolation scenarios (3 structural across per-tenant DBs plus control-plane, 3 behavioural across bound-tenant defence-in-depth ValueError surfaces) and four import-linter contract additions (new layers-intent-class-eval hexagonal; intent_classification_evaluation added to three cross-context independence contracts plus the domain-purity contract). (6) `docs(p13/s48b): live-stack intent-classification evaluation against tenant_a` (this commit) landing the smoke document at `docs/smoke/p13_s48b_intent_classification_eval.md`, this session log entry, and the S48b close marker.

- Live-stack exercise outcome — three evaluation runs against tenant_a. (a) `gpt-4o-mini` ran to completion in ~75 seconds across all 40 entries: 39/40 correct (97.50% overall accuracy); per-class create_case 100%, add_data_point 100% (including all 4 S46 blind-spot phrasings classified correctly), revise_data_point 87.5% (1 miss; debatable gold-set entry), unclear 100%; latency profile min 970ms / avg 1.89s / p50 1.63s / p95 3.43s / max 6.14s; zero parse failures; total spend <$0.001 against the OpenAI account at published rates. (b) `qwen2.5:7b` failed twice at first-call cold-start timeout (91.5s and 92.2s vs the 30s REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier budget); the substrate's runner-level failure-capture absorbed both timeouts, marked the runs failed with structured failure_reason, emitted the run.fail audit event. The qwen2.5:7b operational verdict is "not viable at REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier on this hardware" — the production cell uses the same tier budget, so operator-facing cold-start cascades would face identical timeouts. (c) Audit chain extended with 6 events (one start + one terminal-transition per run); chain integrity holds at 245 events / 245 distinct hashes / single genesis from 2026-05-12.

- Decisions: D137 (intent-classification evaluation substrate at contexts/intent_classification_evaluation/) plus the architecture.md addition plus captures methodology candidates. No D-entries beyond D137 at S48b.

- Tests: 1776 unit + contract tests pass (+22 from S48a close baseline of 1754: +4 single-source-of-truth contract harness, +12 domain-layer unit tests on the substrate, +6 tenant-isolation contract scenarios). 33 of 33 import-linter contracts kept (+1 layers-intent-class-eval). AST enforcement green. Alembic migration 0022 applied successfully to both tenant data planes.

- Reflection (substrate placement verification, prompt 1): The recommended cut (a) at pre-write reconciliation Surface 1 — new bounded context at `contexts/intent_classification_evaluation/` per D127 alternative (d) — held without revision. Intent-classification evaluation and retrieval evaluation are distinct architectural concerns (different evidence source; different metric shapes; different gold-set authoring); a single evaluation umbrella context would have absorbed too much for one instance per the build-at-second-instance discipline. The placement decision was clean and did not require a D-entry alternative-considered update beyond what D137 already records.

- Reflection (gold-set authoring discipline, prompt 2): The 40 entries authored cleanly across the four intent classes with the four S46 blind-spot phrasings landing as explicit AddDataPointIntent entries at index 12-15. The S40b methodology entry ("metric-threshold expectations need structural-understanding grounding") fired weakly at S48b — the single revise_data_point miss at entry 29 ("The hiring search status changed: offer extended yesterday" classified as add_data_point) surfaces a gold-set entry whose expected-class is debatable. The phrase "status changed: offer extended yesterday" could legitimately be read as adding a new status note rather than revising an existing one; the gold-set author chose revise_data_point because "changed" + "yesterday" implies update, but the model's add_data_point reading is also coherent. Two structural improvements possible at future work: (a) tighten gold-set entries at the operator-authoring layer to remove expected-class ambiguity; (b) extend the schema to ask the model for a disambiguation discriminator between add vs revise on borderline phrasings. Neither is in scope at S48b. The discipline observation: even a 40-entry gold set surfaces at least one ambiguity at the operator-authoring layer; future per-tenant gold sets (D137 alternative (c) trigger) should expect the same and provision authoring-time disambiguation tools.

- Reflection (per-model evaluation outcome, prompt 3): **Substantive paragraph because the result is load-bearing.** The two-model comparison directly validates the S48a swap decision component-side. gpt-4o-mini classified the four S46 blind-spot phrasings correctly (4/4 add_data_point) at warm-call latency 1.5-2.3 seconds, dropped one borderline revise_data_point entry (debatable gold-set entry), and ran the full 40-entry evaluation in ~75 seconds for <$0.001 against the OpenAI account. qwen2.5:7b could not complete a single classification within the 30-second REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier budget on this hardware (both runs failed at 91-92 second cold-start timeouts). The component-quality verdict for the current Phase 2-A operator-dogfooding model choice is unambiguous: gpt-4o-mini is operationally fit; qwen2.5:7b is not. The substrate's load-bearing claim ("answer model-choice questions in minutes") delivered in 75 seconds for a positive verdict and in 92 seconds for a clean failure verdict. Both outcomes are procurement-grade evidence the audit chain captures.

- Reflection (confidence-value calibration evidence, prompt 4): gpt-4o-mini populated the `confidence` field consistently across all 40 entries (no nulls); confidence values clustered in the 0.7-0.95 band for correct classifications. The single revise_data_point miss had confidence 0.85 — the model was confident in the wrong classification, which is exactly the failure mode confidence-aware composition is most exposed to (Case 1 high-confidence-but-wrong). The architectural defense at D134 remains the right cut: pattern 2 (suggestion-as-question) handles medium-confidence wrong classifications; only the high-confidence wrong cases (~2.5% of the gold set here) bypass that defense. Forward calibration substrate evidence: a per-model confidence-vs-correctness scatter plot at substrate altitude would surface model-specific calibration patterns; the substrate's data is now in place at `intent_class_evaluation_results` to compute that. Brief observation; not in scope at S48b.

- Reflection (methodology surfaces, prompt 5): **Substantive paragraph because three methodology candidates land.** First, the **scope-discipline-at-brief-authoring** observation from the operator's framing-time methodology line: the S48b brief committed the full P11-mirror as default scope; Surface 1 reconciliation treated the mirror as precedent rather than testing whether each piece served a current need; the scope question surfaced only when the full file count emerged at the brief-versus-codebase reading. Captured at log/captures.md as first-instance, adjacent to but distinct from interface-versus-implementation. Second, the **structural-test single-source-of-truth binding** pattern fired its second instance at S48b commit 2 (Python-identity assertion across consumer imports for the shared intent-classification primitive). The first instance was the no-numeric-threshold-literals AST test at S47 addendum commit 4f74509; the second-instance promotion threshold is met. Third, the **component-quality-vs-integration-smoke** discipline has now landed its first concrete implementation (D137 at S48b) — two-instance evidence from S46 and S47 plus the structural surface from D137. All three forward to the post-S48 hygiene methodology review.

- Reflection (path-naming discipline operational evidence, prompt 6): Surface 2 caught no path-naming drift at S48b framing or commit-drafting time. The brief's named paths (`contexts/intent_classification_evaluation/`, `apps/cli/_intent_classification_eval.py`, `tests/fixtures/intent_classification/`, `tests/contract/tenant_isolation/test_intent_class_eval_isolation.py`) all matched the actual conventions verified against the existing eight contexts and the existing apps/cli/_* file convention. Brief observation: the path-naming discipline is now mechanical enough that drift is rare at framing-time when the operator's brief has been authored against the actual repo state. Recurrence test continues.

methodology: Three captures-promotion-ready candidates land at S48b — the component-quality-vs-integration-smoke pattern now has two-instance evidence plus its first structural implementation in code (D137); the structural-test-binding pattern lands its second instance (symbol-identity at S48b commit 2 after the no-numeric-thresholds AST test at S47 addendum); the scope-discipline-at-brief-authoring pattern lands as first-instance observation captured during framing. ## S48a — REAL_TIME_REQUIRED swap to gpt-4o-mini and smoke revalidation
roles: engineer, technical writer
mode: build session, executing briefs/p13/s48a.md

S48a — Thread 1 of the parallel post-S47 forward path — swapped the REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier model pin from `qwen2.5:14b` to the hosted `gpt-4o-mini` per D133's gateway-as-resolution-point shape, then re-executed the S47 multi-turn cell smoke against tenant_a. The S47 smoke had surfaced `qwen2.5:14b`'s commodity-hardware viability gap (progressive 28s→361s slowdown); S48a verifies whether the convergence's Response A disposition closes operationally at a hosted model rather than a local one. **Verdict: operational dogfooding loop unblocked at `gpt-4o-mini`.** 4/4 AddDataPointIntent phrasings classified correctly at 1.5-3 s warm latency; convergence concern 5 closes operationally.

- Produced: One feat commit (`feat(p13/s48a): swap REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier pin to gpt-4o-mini`, d620692) covering three configuration surfaces: `padhanam/config/inference.py` line 70 pin swap (qwen2.5:14b → gpt-4o-mini); `ops/litellm/config.yaml` model_list gains gpt-4o-mini routing entry referencing `os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY`; `compose.yaml` litellm service gains `OPENAI_API_KEY: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}` env passthrough. Plus `.env.example` OPENAI_API_KEY block surfacing the new credential to operators, the model_registry docstring refresh acknowledging qwen2.5:14b's local-development-fallback role, and three test updates (one rename + assertion swap, two comment refreshes). The brief's intended chore commit shape upgraded to feat because the brief's surface-3 reconciliation found that the one-line pin change wouldn't work operationally without the parallel gateway and compose changes (the exact drift class the S47 smoke captured at `log/captures.md`). Plus one `docs(p13/s48a)` commit (this commit) landing the executed-evidence smoke document append at `docs/smoke/p13_s47_multi_turn_cell_end_to_end.md` under a new "## S48a re-execution at `gpt-4o-mini`" section, the qwen2.5:14b captures-entry resolution-line update (resolved via swap to gpt-4o-mini), three new captures entries (resolver disambiguation rendering on duplicate-title collision; cancel-then-fresh-turn double-cost behaviour; auto-expire-prior-pending positive substrate observation), this session-log entry, and the current-package S48a close marker.

- Smoke outcome — all stages verified end-to-end. Stage 1 environment: ngrok, Twilio Sandbox, gateway-lists-gpt-4o-mini, end-to-end probe through gateway → OpenAI in 2.15 s. Stage 2 CreateCaseIntent regression: cell classified at medium confidence, rendered Case 2 shape-aware clarification, cell-call latency 2.19 s. Stage 4 (first instance) confirmation resolution: pending RESOLVED in 16 ms (deterministic confirm path), case `acb449a0` created, cited confirmation reply rendered (`Recorded a new case: Q3 portfolio review. — ref acb449a0 · intake ea1563fc · 10:06 UTC`). **Stage 3 four-phrasing battery: 4/4 classifications correct** with `intent_type=add_data_point`, `data_point_type=GOAL`, `value_text="ship Wave 1 by end of May"`, and case_reference variants preserving the user's literal phrasing (`Q3 review` / `Q3 portfolio review` / `Q3 portfolio review case` / `Q3 portfolio review`); warm LLM call latency 1.5-2.3 s, cold 2.9-4.1 s. Stage 4 (second instance) surfaced the duplicate-title resolver-disambiguation finding (three cases titled `Q3 portfolio review` from S46/S47/S48a; the resolver's rendering uses only `title` and produced three identical disambiguation strings; no data_point was written). Stage 5 cancellation surfaced the cancel-then-fresh-turn double-cost behaviour (deterministic resolve in 14 ms + fresh-turn LLM in 3.77 s on the bare `no`). Stage 6 audit chain integrity: 239 events / 239 distinct hashes / single genesis from 2026-05-12; chain holds. Final tenant_a state: intakes 29→40 (+11), cases 7→8 (+1, `acb449a0`), data_points 3→3 (zero, resolver bailed), messages 36→56 (+20), pending_clarifications 2→7 (+5), tenant_audit 196→239 (+43).

- Decisions: No new D-entries. The session executes against D133's existing commitment (gateway-as-resolution-point with static configuration at Phase 2-A) and the model registry's pre-seeded `gpt-4o-mini` entry from S47 commit 4db4476.

- Tests: 1750 unit + contract passing post-swap (matches S47 close baseline exactly; the swap is configuration-only, no new test assertions added beyond the one renamed test asserting the new pin); 32 of 32 import-linter contracts kept; AST enforcement green.

- Reflection (classification reliability at `gpt-4o-mini` against the S46 blind-spot phrasings, prompt 1): **substantive paragraph because the result is load-bearing.** `gpt-4o-mini` classified `add_data_point` correctly across all four structural variants: template (`Add a goal to the Q3 review: …`), verb-first-with-full-title (`Add this goal to the Q3 portfolio review: …`), target-front-loaded (`For the Q3 portfolio review case, add a goal: …`), and the structurally-hardest no-verb-noun-phrase (`Ship Wave 1 by end of May — goal for the Q3 portfolio review.`). Each cascade populated all four intent slots correctly. S46's `qwen2.5:7b` was 0/2 on the template phrasing; S47's `qwen2.5:14b` couldn't validate because of latency timeouts. The intent-extraction reliability finding from S46/S47 closes at S48a via the configuration-only path the convergence's Response A described, with the hosted-inference variant resolving the hardware-viability gap. Phase 2-A operator-dogfooding's AddDataPointIntent surface is operationally usable.

- Reflection (latency profile against operator dogfooding viability, prompt 2): warm cell-call latency at `gpt-4o-mini` landed in the 1.5-2.3 s band; cold (first-call-after-restart) landed in the 2.9-4.1 s band. End-to-end inbound→outbound including DB writes and WhatsApp delivery lands at 1.7-4.1 s. Confirm-path orchestration (no LLM call) lands at 271-294 ms. Compared to S46's `qwen2.5:7b` warm at 8-9 s / cold at 22.95 s and S47's `qwen2.5:14b` at 28 s → 361 s progressive, `gpt-4o-mini` is comfortably in the operator-dogfooding-viable band. The dogfooding loop is unblocked operationally.

- Reflection (confidence-aware composition under the new model, prompt 3): the cell's self-reported confidence field is populated consistently across all classifications, landing in the medium band (0.5 ≤ c < 0.8) for both CreateCaseIntent and all four AddDataPointIntent phrasings. This is the same band the S47 smoke observed at `qwen2.5:14b` on the same phrasing classes, which suggests the medium-band landing is a calibration property of the cell's prompt-and-schema design rather than the model's capability. The cell's Case 2 (shape-aware clarification) renders correctly throughout; D134's three-case discipline operates as intended. The ConfidenceCalculator port's swap-readiness holds: a future adapter (e.g. one that calibrates against a held-out set rather than reading self-reported confidence) could swap in via the port's adapter slot without cell-side change. No captures entry added for the calibration observation — single instance, not promotion-threshold.

- Reflection (cost profile at operator-dogfooding volume, prompt 4): the smoke session consumed approximately 10 LLM cascades (Stage 2 + 4 fresh-turn classifications at Stage 3 + 1 cancel-fresh-turn at Stage 5 + a few corrections); each cascade carries ~$0.0001 input + output cost at gpt-4o-mini's published $0.150 input / $0.600 output per 1M tokens. Total smoke spend: well under $0.01. Operator dogfooding at one user's volume (estimated 50-200 cascades/day) projects to <$1/day, well within the static-configuration commitment's budget bracket. The model_registry's cost-per-call metadata is honest at the gpt-4o-mini row (verified at smoke close; no drift). The brief's reflection prompt 4 verdict: cost profile validates the architectural expectation.

- Reflection (methodology surfaces, prompt 5): substantive paragraph because three observations land. **First**, the swap that the brief framed as "one configuration line, chore commit shape" required three configuration surfaces (inference.py pin + gateway model_list entry + compose env passthrough) plus an `.env.example` addition for operator-facing documentation. The brief's pre-write reconciliation surface 3 (LiteLLM API for gpt-4o-mini) correctly anticipated this — the reconciliation guidance "if more is needed at the configuration surface, the swap is not a pure chore and the commit shape upgrades to feat" fired exactly as designed. The interface-versus-implementation discipline (now at 6+ instances of evidence) caught the discrepancy at framing rather than commit-draft time; the brief was honestly framed and the upgrade was clean. **Second**, the smoke-document append-not-replace protocol (brief's surface 5) was the first application of the pattern at a model-choice surface; the append cleanly preserved S47's executed evidence as historical record while the S48a section captured the new evidence. **Pattern recurrence note** at first instance only — a future model-choice surface change (S48c or beyond) is the test. **Third**, the smoke surfaced three substrate findings (resolver disambiguation rendering; cancel-then-fresh-turn double-cost; auto-expire positive observation) that are structurally separable from the model-choice question. Smoke discipline: per-stage executed evidence keeps substrate findings cleanly distinct from the model-swap verdict, which is exactly what allows the verdict to be honest ("operational unblock at `gpt-4o-mini`") without conflating the resolver finding into the verdict. No methodology promotion at S48a; observation forwarded to phase-2-audit-inputs at session close per the existing discipline.

methodology: The brief's pre-write reconciliation surface 3 firing correctly at draft time — the LiteLLM gateway routing question caught the "swap is more than one line" reality before any commit landed — is the seventh interface-versus-implementation instance the run has now recorded, and the first at a model-choice configuration surface (the pattern's prior surfaces were code path, schema location, adapter shape). The interface-versus-implementation discipline now has demonstrated coverage across charter altitude (the convergence conversation), code altitude (S47 framing), and configuration altitude (S48a framing). Phase 2-A close hygiene's methodology-promotion path inherits a candidate with broad surface coverage.

## S47 smoke — UX convergence substrate live-stack verification
roles: engineer, technical writer
mode: strategic-mode-continuation (operational execution evidence continuing the S47 + addendum close)

The S47 substrate (D133 dispatch port + gateway-as-resolution-point + model registry; D134 confidence-aware response composition + ConfidenceCalculator + PendingClarification; D135 domain-content channel-format rendering; D136 multi-channel UX primitives; S47 addendum's ThresholdResolver port) verified end-to-end against tenant_a on a freshly-rebuilt `padhanam-api` image (digest `sha256:be1e2c09…`, advanced from the S47-base `sha256:ce2928c2…` for three smoke-driven substrate fixes). Three substrate gaps surfaced and committed at d63f8a5; two operational findings captured at `log/captures.md` rather than fixed in-session.

- Produced: One smoke-driven substrate-fixes commit (`feat(p13/s47): smoke-driven substrate fixes`, d63f8a5) covering the cell `originating_intake_id` threading from webhook through to the PendingClarification insert (closing the FK-violation crash the brief comment had anticipated but not resolved against the migration's `fk_pending_clar_intake_id` constraint); the LiteLLM gateway `model_list` seed for qwen2.5:14b at `ops/litellm/config.yaml` (closing the model-registry-vs-gateway-routing drift the smoke surfaced on the first cell invocation); the `REAL_TIME_REQUIRED_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` env passthrough on the `padhanam-api` compose block plus the new image digest pin. - Smoke outcome — Stages 1+2 verified end-to-end. Multi-turn cascade with PendingClarification persistence + lifecycle confirmation: inbound `Start a case for the Q3 portfolio review.` (00:14:09 UTC) → cell classified at medium confidence → shape-aware clarification rendered `I think you want to start a case for 'Q3 portfolio review'. Is that right? (yes / no)` (00:14:58 UTC) → PendingClarification `c612afe5-…` persisted with `originating_intake_id = 1c1203cc-…` (real intake row, FK satisfied) → operator's `yes` reply (00:16:51 UTC) → cell consulted PendingClarificationReader at turn-open, found active PENDING, classified reply as confirm, resolved pending, executed create_case orchestration → cited confirmation `Recorded a new case: Q3 portfolio review. — ref 5d4c3092 · intake 874eb027 · 00:16 UTC` (00:16:53 UTC). Case `5d4c3092-…` created; pending transitioned PENDING→RESOLVED with `resolved_at` populated; two PendingClarification lifecycle audit events emitted (`messaging.pending_clarification.create` + `…resolve`). Stage 3 (cancellation) closed-with-findings: attempt 3a hit Case 3 cleanly (de-facto Stage 4 evidence); attempt 3b's cell call latency exceeded the bumped 120s tier timeout (361s LiteLLM-observed; dispatch port's failure-capture worked correctly at the boundary). Stage 4 (low-confidence/parse-failure) de-facto verified by attempt 3a's clean Case-3 rendering. Stage 5 webhook contract verified at every recorded inbound (2xx in 27-282ms regardless of cell-run duration). Stage 7 audit-chain integrity verified at smoke close (192 events, 192 distinct hashes, zero duplicates). Final tenant_a state: intakes 17→28 (+11), cases 6→7 (+1), messages 21→34 (+13), pending_clarifications 0→1, tenant_audit 165→192 (+27).

- Decisions: No new D-entries. The smoke produces operational evidence for existing commitments (D133, D134, D135, D136, S47 addendum's ThresholdResolver) plus two captures entries forwarded for post-S47 hygiene or next strategic-mode session disposition.

- Reflection (substrate verification, prompt 1): Stages 1+2 validate D133's dispatch port, D134's three-case discipline + PendingClarification lifecycle, D135's rendering pattern at the WhatsApp channel adapter, and the S47 addendum's ThresholdResolver port consumption — all at the live stack against tenant_a. (yes / no)` rather than acting confidently on an uncertain classification, exactly the failure mode the convergence's Response C addresses. The substrate works.

- Reflection (FK-violation finding, prompt 2): The smoke's first significant finding surfaced at the first cell Case 2 invocation. The S47 commit-5 cell's `_dispatch_clarify_with_pending` minted a fresh UUID for `PendingClarification.originating_intake_id`; the migration's `fk_pending_clar_intake_id` FK constraint rejected the insert with `ForeignKeyViolationError`. The brief comment had anticipated the limitation ("Phase 2-A compromise: mint a fresh UUID as the pending's originating_intake_id slot when no upstream intake id has been threaded through") but had not resolved it against the migration's FK constraint. The dispatch-port's failure-capture worked correctly at the boundary — the exception logged structurally with the caller's context dict, the webhook stayed 2xx, the FK violation surfaced cleanly in the api logs. Fix landed at d63f8a5: the webhook handler now passes the inbound `intake_id` to the cell's constructor; the cell uses it as the pending's `originating_intake_id`, satisfying the FK and giving the pending a structurally-honest audit anchor back to the inbound message. This is the kind of structural gap a unit-test cannot catch — the unit test for the cell's Case 2 path can construct a fake repository and accept any UUID, while the migration's FK constraint operates at the persistence layer outside the unit-test boundary. Contract harness extension (a per-tenant integration test verifying PendingClarification lifecycle against the real `pending_clarifications` table) would close this gap class; deferred to post-S47 hygiene.

- Reflection (model-registry-vs-gateway-routing drift, prompt 3): The second significant finding was the model-registry seed at `padhanam/config/model_registry.py` (per D133's audit-and-future-policy substrate) not propagating to the LiteLLM gateway's `model_list` at `ops/litellm/config.yaml`. The smoke caught the drift on the first cell call after the S47-base image was rebuilt — `litellm.BadRequestError: Invalid model name passed in model=qwen2.5:14b`. The fix at d63f8a5 added the gateway routing entry, but the underlying drift class remains structurally unprotected: nothing enforces that model_registry entries also appear in the gateway's model_list. Captured at `log/captures.md` as a methodology candidate; the proposed structural test (parse both files, assert set intersection) lives at `tests/contract/inference/test_model_registry_gateway_sync.py` per the captures entry's forward-fix candidate.

- Reflection (qwen2.5:14b hardware-viability finding, prompt 4): The third significant finding has S47-Response-A implications. The model bump per D133 commit 6 to qwen2.5:14b is operationally non-viable on this hardware: progressive call latency 28s → 48s → 67s → 361s suggests memory pressure or cache thrashing at the 9.7 GB resident model against the 16 GB total RAM. Phase 2-A operator dogfooding requires 10-30 second responsiveness at the WhatsApp surface; 6-minute latencies break the dogfooding loop. The S47 substrate is unaffected — even at the 14b pin, the cell at medium-confidence classification renders shape-aware clarification rather than acting confidently (D134 Response C operating correctly regardless of which model the gateway routes to). What does not validate is **Response A's static-configuration disposition** on this machine. Captured at `log/captures.md` with three forward paths (hosted inference; per-model tier-timeout overrides; constrained classification surface). The captures entry stays as forward observation rather than triggering a charter change; the existing convergence captures-entry from 2026-05-22 [S46 smoke] names all three responses and is not superseded.

- Reflection (Stage 3 cancellation closure-with-findings, prompt 5): The intended Stage 3 cancellation path was not exercised live because both attempts hit findings rather than the cancellation flow itself. Attempt 3a (`Maybe…`) routed to Case 3 cleanly — useful de-facto Stage 4 evidence but not the cancellation. Attempt 3b (`Add a goal…`) blew the tier timeout. The cancellation path is structurally identical to Stage 2's confirmation path with one transition difference (resolve as cancelled rather than confirmed; cell falls through to fresh-turn handling on the correcting inbound rather than executing the proposed orchestration). The unit test at `tests/unit/contexts/messaging/application/test_manual_entry_cell.py::test_cancellation_resolves_pending_and_falls_through` covers the exact path. The smoke verdict: substrate-verified by Stage 1+2 plus unit-test coverage of the cancellation transition; live exercise of cancellation defers to a follow-up smoke against a viable inference backend.

- Reflection (executed-evidence discipline at smoke close, prompt 6): The S46 smoke close annotation at `docs/smoke/p13_s46_manual_entry_end_to_end.md` carried executed evidence stage-by-stage; this S47 smoke annotation follows the same discipline. The discipline produces a structurally-honest audit artefact for any procurement-grade reader: the substrate claims at D133/D134/D135/D136 plus the S47 addendum's ThresholdResolver port are not only documented in charter and committed in code, they are operationally executed end-to-end against tenant_a with timestamps, IDs, audit-chain integrity counts, and per-stage verdicts. The smoke document's structural-honesty extends to the closed-with-findings stages — Stage 3+ findings are recorded as findings rather than as failures-of-substrate, with the substrate-verification status separated from the model-viability status.

- Reflection (post-smoke hygiene candidates, prompt 7): Three forward items the smoke surfaces for post-S47 hygiene or a follow-up session: (a) the model-registry-vs-LiteLLM-gateway-routing drift structural test per the captures-entry forward-fix candidate; (b) the per-tenant integration test for PendingClarification lifecycle against the real `pending_clarifications` table (to close the FK-violation gap class at the test boundary); (c) the inference-model-selection strategic block (hosted vs local; per-model tier-timeout; possibly Response B's constrained classification surface). None of these block P14 framing; all defer to either post-S47 hygiene or the next strategic-mode session as appropriate. The S47 substrate ready-for-P14 verdict from the original S47 close (`current-package.md`) holds at smoke close.

methodology: The model-registry-vs-LiteLLM-gateway-routing drift is a first-instance of a class — two configuration surfaces that must stay in sync with no structural test enforcing the invariant. - Reflection (convergence settlement integrity, prompt 1): each architectural commitment from D133-D136 landed cleanly in the substrate. - Reflection (dispatch port and cell-failure logging integration, prompt 3): the bare-`except Exception: pass` at the prior synchronous shape (`apps/api/routers/messaging.py:267`) is closed by the dispatch port's contract. The integration produced no unexpected interactions with the existing Twilio signature verification (the webhook still verifies before dispatch) or the outbound REST API delivery (the cell's `send_message` still runs through the existing path after the dispatch's background task completes). The clean separation comes from the dispatch port carrying the cell-failure logging at *its* contract: callers don't see the cell's exceptions; the structured `cell-run failed in background task` log line emerges with the caller's `context` dict (intake_id, tenant_id, external_id) surfacing as `extra={"context": ...}`. The test for it (`test_dispatch_captures_cell_exception_and_logs`) verifies the contract end-to-end.

- Reflection (PendingClarification audit-chain integrity, prompt 4): the lifecycle events chain cleanly across the multi-turn cascade. The three audit drafts (`messaging.pending_clarification.create / resolve / expire`) follow the same draft-then-recompute shape as `draft_message_event`, so the Postgres audit adapter recomputes `previous_event_hash` and `this_event_hash` inside its locking transaction per D37. Across three lifecycle paths (create→resolve confirmed, create→resolve cancelled, create→expire), the audit chain at the unit-test altitude carries the right shape: one chain-anchoring per lifecycle event, three after-state shapes (creation carries `expires_at` plus `proposed_action_summary`; resolution carries `resolution: confirmed|cancelled` plus `resolved_at`; expiration carries the `resolved_at` only). The procurement-grade defensibility question — can an auditor distinguish "platform acted confidently on a low-confidence guess" from "platform asked for confirmation before acting" — answers yes via the audit chain: every Case 2 emission produces a `create` event, and every confirmed action carries a `resolve` event immediately before the portfolio write. Phase 2-A operator dogfooding will exercise the chain at live volume.

- Reflection (confidence-aware composition operator-facing reality, prompt 5): the smoke is procedural; the operator-facing UX records live. The shape-aware clarification at Case 2 reads as a suggestion-as-question per principle pattern 2 (`I think you want to <action>. Is that right? (yes / no)`). The hex-citation line per D131 Shape 1 holds on the confirming-reply confirmation. Whether the cut-off pair (0.8 / 0.5) hits the right balance — too many Case 1 false confidences feel pushy, too many Case 2 clarifications feel pedantic — is calibration that emerges with dogfooding data; the substrate is in place to tune without code change. The cut-offs threaded through MessagingSettings means a smoke-time recalibration is `MESSAGING_CONFIDENCE_HIGH_CUTOFF=0.85` away.

- Reflection (static config bump validation, prompt 6): the bump from `qwen2.5:7b` to `qwen2.5:14b` is a substantive Phase 2-A reliability commitment, not a cosmetic config nudge. The S46 smoke surfaced 0/7 AddDataPointIntent classifications across four phrasings at the 7B model; the 14B variant has substantially stronger discriminative capability on structured-output tasks per published benchmarks. Whether the bump closes the operational problem in the operator's actual deployment requires the live smoke — if `qwen2.5:14b` also misses AddDataPointIntent under the operator's hardware (or under load), Response A's static-configuration disposition has not closed the convergence's concern 5, and the operator should override to a hosted alternative (gpt-4o-mini, claude-haiku-4-5) via `INFERENCE_REAL_TIME_REQUIRED_MODEL`. The model registry at `padhanam/config/model_registry.py` carries the four candidate models with cost-per-call so the audit chain records which model fired and procurement-grade defensibility holds across the bump. The smoke's stage-2 medium-confidence cascade is the empirical test for `qwen2.5:14b`'s classification accuracy; if every attempt classifies at confidence ≥ 0.8, the cell skips Case 2 entirely and the convergence's principle-2-binding surface stays untested in practice.

- Reflection (methodology surfaces, prompt 7): the interface-versus-implementation methodology candidate (promotion-ready at the captures entry from this session's charter commit) earned its first operational instance during S47's commit-draft cycles, as recorded above. No additional methodology candidates from S47 itself warrant captures entries — the substrate work largely followed the established patterns (consumer ports per S46 precedent; intake-canonical orchestration per S44b; audit-event drafts per S45). Phase 2-B+ ConversationFlow implementers landing in P14 with similar dependency counts will trigger the question of whether a CellComposition value object captures the cross-cutting infrastructure separately from per-cell deps. Single instance; not a captures entry.

- Reflection (LLM cold-vs-warm latency dynamic, prompt 1): the synchronous-LLM-vs-Twilio-timeout finding surfaced at stage 1 (LLM call 22.95s, ngrok status 0) — initially framed as "the 23s LLM blows Twilio's 15s webhook timeout, retry-duplication risk." The round-2 rephrasings produced a richer empirical picture: the same LLM call ran at 18.62s (cold after 13min idle), 9.07s (warm 35s later), 8.05s (warm 18s later). Ollama's 5-min keep-alive unloads the model on idle; the next call pays cold-start cost. The webhook-contract finding holds on grounds independent of which side of the timeout a given run falls (a synchronous handler is wrong on contract grounds even at 8s — it ties up a server worker for the full duration and writes its response to an already-closed connection), but the empirical urgency calibrates by usage pattern. The captures entry now incorporates both endpoints honestly.

- Reflection (intent-extraction reliability and N=1-vs-N=4 catch, prompt 2): stage 8a's AddDataPointIntent attempt classified to UnclearIntent using the smoke document's own template phrasing. The initial disposition drafting in the cross-thread captures wording overclaimed three rephrasings as "having run" before they actually ran — Claude Code caught the N=1-versus-N=4 conflation at captures-entry drafting time and surfaced the discrepancy; the operator chose Path 1+2 (actually run the rephrasings then close) over Path 2 (close at N=1 with softer wording). The rephrasings ran (verb-first, target-front-loaded, no-verb-noun-phrase; each sent twice for six runs total); all classified to UnclearIntent. Phrasing-sensitivity empirically falsified; intent-class blindness on AddDataPoint at `qwen2.5:7b` / REAL_TIME_REQUIRED is the surviving claim, supported by N=4 distinct phrasings across 7 runs. Three architectural responses for the convergence session captured: raise the REAL_TIME_REQUIRED tier model (Response A), constrain the classification surface or expand the prompt (Response B), render model uncertainty as user-facing clarification more honestly (Response C). Phase 2-A operator-dogfooding-via-WhatsApp viability opens as a first-class convergence input rather than mid-stream optimisation.

- Reflection (D131 first-instance operator-facing reality, prompt 3): the cited replies in both CreateCase cascades carried the Shape 1 line cleanly — `— ref fa6401b0 · intake 85622595 · 21:45 UTC` and `— ref 4fac3ae0 · intake 583c7c36 · 22:30 UTC`. The clarification-path replies (8a + rephrasings) carried no citation line — D131 contract held across all 7 clarification cases. Whether operators find the citations useful, intrusive, or ignorable at any volume is convergence-session-relevant; the smoke confirms the rendering shape without stressing operator preference.

- Reflection (instrumentation gap on prompt/output capture, prompt 4): the Langfuse trace captures the D122/D132 dimensions and token counts but does not capture prompt content or model output. The smoke cannot distinguish whether `qwen2.5:7b` returned clean UnclearIntent JSON (the model knows it doesn't know) or whether `parse_intent` coerced malformed output to UnclearIntent (the model produced something Padhanam can't parse). The two cases have different architectural implications for confidence-aware composition. Folded as a paragraph inside the intent-extraction reliability captures entry rather than as a separate finding because the gap is structurally linked to the intent-extraction finding's analytical surface.

- Reflection (discipline-working signals during smoke execution, prompt 5): three discipline-working signals at this smoke worth indexing for Phase 2-A close hygiene methodology assessment. Strategic-conversation outcome from the Phase 2-A S45 framing approach. The first makes protocol selection scenario-driven and vendor-readiness-modulated: agent-to-tool integration defaults to MCP, service-to-service runtime integration defaults to vendor SDK, cross-vendor LLM abstraction is via LiteLLM, observability is via OpenTelemetry — and vendor readiness at the chosen protocol determines whether the scenario's architectural default is the actual framing-time disposition. S45 framing inherits the principles as reference points for the Item 1 protocol-choice surface.

roles: engineer, technical writer
mode: hygiene session (charter-vs-code-honesty; closes the load-bearing finding LSP1 from the pre-S45 principles assessment with a contract-test harness; test plus docs commit prefixes per the hygiene-session shape; no new D-entries)

  - Commit cb32e53 (`test(contract)`): `test_data_point_revisable.py` registering DataPoint as the first implementer.

- Decisions: No new D-entries. The session closes existing charter commitments (D114, D125, `architecture.md` line 274) by landing the artefact they assert; it makes no new architectural commitment.

- Tests: 6 new tests at `tests/contract/revisable/` — the five conformance scenarios (signature, return type, append-only, ordering, genesis) parametrised over `portfolio.DataPoint`, plus a `@runtime_checkable` sanity test. `tests/unit` and `tests/contract` run green (pytest exit 0). The harness adds only test files — no production code changed — so the integration and e2e tiers are structurally unaffected; the two pre-existing environmental failures in `contexts/methodology` and `contexts/tools` carried from S44a/S44b are unrelated and unchanged. 29 of 29 import-linter contracts kept (the harness adds no import-direction surface); AST enforcement unaffected.

- Enforcement layer: The harness *is* the new enforcement layer. Before this session, Revisable conformance was verified only by `tests/unit/shared_kernel/test_revisable.py` unit tests plus the `@runtime_checkable` decorator — which checks method *names* only. `tests/contract/revisable/` now runs five behavioural conformance scenarios against every registered implementer at every test cycle. The registration mechanism (`register_revisable_implementer` plus the `test_*_revisable.py` glob in `conftest.py`) is the extension surface: P14's methodology-application revision and a later Case-level revision register through it with no harness modification.

- Pre-write reconciliation: Five surfaces verified before the scaffold drafted; all five were mechanical absorptions — none surfaced a structural-honesty finding. Surface 1: `tests/contract/` carries `http/` and `tenant_isolation/` only, unchanged since the principles assessment. Surface 2: the Revisable Protocol's `revise(change, actor) -> Revisable[RevisionT]` and `revision_history() -> list[RevisionT]` signatures and the append-only docstring semantics re-read; what `@runtime_checkable` does not cover (signature shape, return type, behaviour) named before the scenarios drafted. Surface 3: `DataPoint.revise` carries the `intake_id` optional-with-default third parameter per LSP2 — the signature scenario was written to permit exactly that. Surface 4: contract-test convention is a package directory with `__init__.py`, optional `conftest.py`, flat `test_*.py` — matched. Surface 5: file topology budget — `conftest.py` 84 lines, `test_revisable_contract.py` 116, `test_data_point_revisable.py` 75, all within the brief's targets.

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. *Pre-write reconciliation outcomes.* All five surfaces were mechanical absorptions — the brief's framing matched the codebase at every surface, which is the expected shape for a tightly-scoped hygiene session drafted one session after the principles assessment that surveyed the same ground. The one surface that carried design weight was surface 3: confirming `DataPoint.revise`'s `intake_id` extension shape before the signature scenario drafted, so the scenario verifies the LSP-compatible optional-extension rule rather than a rigid two-parameter equality.

  2. *What `@runtime_checkable` does not cover that the harness now does.* `@runtime_checkable` permits `isinstance(x, Revisable)` but verifies only that the named methods (`revise`, `revision_history`) *exist* — not their signatures, return types, or behaviour. The harness fills each gap with a named scenario: the **signature scenario** verifies `revise` presents the `(change, actor)` shape with any extra parameter carrying a default; the **return-type scenario** verifies `revise` returns the same concrete class (the covariant narrowing of `Revisable[RevisionT]`); the **append-only and ordering scenarios** verify the semantic core — `revise` appends exactly one revision without mutating the original, and sequential revises append at the tail in call order; the **genesis scenario** verifies a fresh instance carries a stable genesis revision at index 0. The `@runtime_checkable` membership check itself is retained as the sanity test in `test_data_point_revisable.py`, so the harness layers behavioural verification on top of structural membership rather than replacing it.

  3. *Cross-reference to LSP1 and LSP2.* LSP1 — the load-bearing finding of `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` — is closed in code at this session: the codebase's one cross-context architectural-primitive Protocol now carries CI-enforceable conformance, and the charter surfaces that asserted it (D114, D125, `architecture.md` line 274) become accurate. LSP2 — marginal — observed that `DataPoint.revise` extends the Protocol signature with `intake_id`; the signature scenario verifies this extension is contract-compatible (the parameter is optional with a default, so the Protocol's two-argument call stays valid), converting LSP2's prose analysis into an executable check that every future implementer's signature extensions must also pass.

  4. *Discipline observation.* The harness converts Revisable's verification from aspirational to CI-enforceable: before this session, three charter surfaces asserted "CI-enforceable conformance via contract tests" while the only enforcement was unit tests plus a name-only `@runtime_checkable` decorator — the charter claimed more than the tree delivered. This is the first instance of the CI-enforceable-versus-aspirational pattern the principles assessment named receiving a closure. Whether the pattern (a charter claim of mechanical enforcement should be backed by the named artefact, and a missing artefact is a charter-vs-code honesty gap) earns methodology-document promotion evaluates at Phase 2-A close per the disposition; this entry records the first-instance evidence without promoting it, per the build-versus-strategic discipline.

- methodology (line 1): **A charter claim of mechanical enforcement is a charter-vs-code honesty gap until the named artefact exists.** D114/D125/`architecture.md`:274 asserted "CI-enforceable conformance via contract tests at `tests/contract/revisable/`" for two sessions while the directory did not exist. The principles assessment caught it as a code-altitude finding; this session closed it. First-instance closure of the CI-enforceable-versus-aspirational pattern; promotion evaluates at Phase 2-A close.

- methodology (line 2): **A contract-test harness verifies what `@runtime_checkable` cannot, and the gap is large.** `@runtime_checkable` verifies method names only; signature shape, return type, and the append-only/ordering/genesis semantics all needed explicit scenarios. The Protocol-surface-only discipline (scenarios touch `revise` and `revision_history`, never implementer internals) is what keeps the harness valid for P14's future implementers without modification.

- **Pre-S45 Revisable harness closed; the load-bearing finding LSP1 from the principles assessment is resolved in code. `tests/contract/revisable/` carries a parametrised conformance harness, `contexts/portfolio` DataPoint is verified against it, and the registration mechanism is ready for P14's methodology-application revision implementer. The remaining material findings from `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` (the cross-context structural-duplication cluster, the composition-layer file splits including the newly-listed `_cross_context.py`, the YAGNI baseline-evidence forward-pointers) stay queued for Phase 2-A close hygiene per the disposition. S45 — the messaging substrate and conversational protocol per the p13-epic Session 3 line — is next.**

## 2026-05-22 — Pre-S45 hygiene — Software engineering principles baseline assessment
roles: analyst, architect, technical writer
mode: strategic (post-substrate-completion assessment; closes no in-flight build work; produces an evidence document that informs the subsequent disposition conversation; no code, test, or enforcement-layer changes)

The first code-altitude software-engineering-principles audit the project has run. It assesses the Phase 2-A codebase against KISS, DRY, the five SOLID letters individually, YAGNI, and Tell Don't Ask, and lands a findings document at the new `audits/` directory. It is an evidence document, not a verdict; disposition of findings happens at the subsequent disposition conversation.

- Produced: Three commits closed the session.
  - Commit e66059c (`docs(audits)`): the findings document at `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` (a new top-level directory) plus `briefs/p13/pre-s45-principles-assessment.md` preserved at v1.
  - Commit 0c7cc07 (`docs(charter)`): three methodology-observation entries appended to `log/captures.md`.
  - Commit this commit (`docs(p13/pre-s45-principles-assessment)`): this session log entry; the current-package close marker.

- Decisions: No new D-entries. Per assessment-shape discipline — the session produces an evidence document; architectural decisions and dispositions belong to the subsequent conversation.

- Tests: None. No edits under `contexts/`, `apps/`, `shared_kernel/`, `padhanam/`, `tests/`, or migrations. The assessment ran `import-linter` (29/29 kept) and a throwaway stdlib-`ast` cyclomatic-complexity sampler; it did not re-run the pytest suite.

- Pre-write reconciliation: Eight surfaces verified before assessment work began.
  - Surface 1 (output path): no `audits/` directory existed; `charter/p12-audit-findings.md` is the package-altitude precedent but lands *in* `charter/`, which collides with the brief's AC 5 (no charter changes beyond captures and session log). Resolved to `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` — the brief's own lead candidate — a new directory that keeps the cross-cutting assessment off the charter surface.
  - Surface 2 (substrate-depth D-entry inventory): D124–D128 are all Kano must-have; D126, D127, D128 carry explicit cost-now-versus-cost-later / cost-of-pivot substrate-depth reasoning. That trio is the YAGNI assessment's primary substrate; D124 is the base substrate and D125 inherits D114.
  - Surface 3 (tools): `import-linter` and `pytest` installed; `ruff`, `mypy`, `radon` **absent**. No operator approval sought to install tooling per the brief. The CC dimension was covered with a stdlib-`ast` sampler; `mypy` type-coverage and `ruff` lint-surface remain named measurement gaps in the findings document's method section.
  - Surface 4 (import-linter): 29 contracts, 29 kept, 0 broken — matches S44b's 29/29.
  - Surface 5 (file inventory): 441 non-test code files; 24 at ≥400 lines, 9 at ≥600, 5 at ≥800. Buckets recorded in the findings document.
  - Surface 6 (audit precedent): `charter/p12-audit-findings.md` uses a three-section + cross-reference-index + verdict shape; the principles assessment is principle-organised instead (cross-cutting, not finding-type-organised) but matches the evidence-citation and per-finding-disposition conventions.
  - Surface 7 (methodology overlap): the file topology budget ↔ SRP; pre-write reconciliation and the substrate-application boundary check ↔ KISS/DRY at the discipline altitude; the consumer-port pattern ↔ DIP. Overlaps cited in the findings document, not duplicated.
  - Surface 8 (no conflicting work): working tree clean at session open; `current-package.md` showed "S44b closed; S45 next" and had not advanced. One mechanical correction: the brief's context-reading item 7 cited `charter/captures.md`; the file lives at `log/captures.md` (the brief's own commit structure cited it correctly).

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. *Pre-write reconciliation surface outcomes.* Of the eight surfaces, two were structural-honesty findings (surface 1's path collision with AC 5, resolved by the new `audits/` directory; surface 8's `charter/captures.md` vs `log/captures.md` mechanical correction), three were tools-and-paths verifications (surfaces 3, 4, 6), and three were mechanical absorptions feeding the assessment (surfaces 2, 5, 7). No surface blocked the assessment; surface 1 was the only genuine disposition and the brief pre-resolved it by naming `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` as the lead candidate. Surface 3 is the one carrying forward weight — the absence of `ruff` and `mypy` means type-coverage and lint-surface were not measured, named as gaps for a future principle audit.

  2. *Charter-altitude versus code-altitude finding deltas.* Three relationships. **Aligned:** the file topology budget findings (`_errors.py`, `_agent_runtime_wiring.py`) and the import-linter contracts holding (29/29) — the code-altitude pass confirmed what the discipline already tracked. **Code-altitude found what charter-altitude could not:** `apps/cli/_cross_context.py` at 1704 lines (the largest file in the codebase, on no hygiene list, in no charter document); the `if "tenant" in str(exc)` exception-message-sniffing repeated ten times; the audit-event-draft inline-versus-helper drift between two sibling contexts one session apart. **Code-altitude found the charter overstates:** three charter surfaces (D114, D125, `architecture.md:274`, `schema.md`) assert a Revisable contract-test harness at `tests/contract/revisable/` that does not exist. On the specific orchestrations-DRY question the charter-altitude audit flagged as unverifiable: the code-altitude assessment surfaced a **different pattern** than feared — the three intake orchestrations are thin (~25 lines each) with only a ~7-line shared prologue, mild duplication consciously kept per D127(d); the real DRY weight is not in the orchestrations at all but in the cursor-codec / pagination / audit-draft / wiring cluster (the CP1 cross-principle finding).

  3. *Most surprising findings.* The single most surprising: `_cross_context.py` at 1704 lines — nearly double any file the brief's SRP watch-points named, and tracked nowhere. The brief's watch-points were drawn from session-log findings, so a file no recent session touched stayed invisible to charter-altitude framing. Second: `_errors.py` grew from the 729 lines the phase-2-audit-inputs entry recorded (S44a) to 828 — the very session after it was flagged for splitting added ~100 lines of intake/portfolio handlers to it. Confirming what the discipline already knew: the Phase 2-A code-altitude simplicity is genuinely strong (82 of 87 functions at CC ≤ 5), the import-linter contracts hold, and the file topology budget is doing real work — the surprises were all in the `apps/` composition layer, which no file-topology budget governs.

  4. *Severity classification balance.* The distribution skews toward the lighter end: 1 load-bearing, 9 material (plus 1 Phase-1-scoped), 12 marginal. The single load-bearing finding (LSP1, the absent Revisable contract-test harness) is already a tracked phase-2-audit-inputs entry, so the substrate's structural integrity is not in question — the load-bearing finding is a verification gap, not a structural breach. The material cluster is dominated by two things: composition-layer SRP (three over-800-line files) and the cross-context DRY cluster (cursor codec et al.). The marginal tail is mostly conscious, charter-reasoned trade-offs (D127(d) orchestration placement, S44a boundary-visibility, aggregate-cohesion ports). The shape says the substrate is sound and the debt is concentrated, addressable hygiene — which is the expected shape for a codebase this far into disciplined incremental build, not a skew in either alarming direction.

  5. *Methodology observations from the assessment process.* Three, all captured at `log/captures.md` this session. The per-principle section structure (one section per principle) forced roughly four genuinely cross-principle findings to be split and cross-referenced rather than stated once — a principle is a lens, not a partition. The quantitative metrics were load-bearing for KISS, SRP, and DIP and thin-to-noise for the other four principles — a uniform metrics-then-findings template over-promises measurability for DRY, OCP, LSP, ISP, YAGNI, and TDA. And the code-altitude pass surfaced a class of finding charter-altitude inference structurally cannot reach (un-charted structure plus charter overclaim). The brief format mostly worked — its watch-points were accurate and its pre-resolution of the output-path question was correct — but its SRP watch-points inherited the session-log blind spot that hid `_cross_context.py`.

  6. *Disposition forward-pointers.* The post-assessment disposition conversation opens with this queue. Hygiene-item candidates: the Revisable contract-test harness (LSP1, also closes a charter-vs-code honesty gap); the cursor-codec / pagination shared-primitive extraction (D1+D2, which also asks the disposition to revisit P12 Finding B5's now-strained non-action); the audit-event-draft helper (D3); the per-tenant-routing adapter primitive (D4); the typed bound-tenant exception replacing the message-sniffing (D7); and `apps/cli/_cross_context.py` added to the composition-layer split list alongside the already-listed `_errors.py` and `_agent_runtime_wiring.py` (SRP1–3). Forward-to-Phase-3-audit: the three inert forward-compat affordances (Y1 `role_list`, Y2 `certainty`, Y3 the `Revisable` Protocol) as YAGNI baseline evidence — this is the queue the held YAGNI-monitoring draft text addresses. Methodology candidates: the three captures entries. Cross-principle CP1 (structural shapes reimplemented per context) is the disposition's highest-value single thread; CP2 (SRP debt concentrates in the composition layer) motivates considering whether the file-topology budget should extend to `apps/`.

- methodology (line 1): **Code-altitude assessment surfaces findings charter-altitude inference structurally cannot.** The first code-altitude principle audit found un-charted structure (`_cross_context.py` at 1704 lines, on no list) and charter overclaim (the Revisable harness three charter surfaces assert but the tree does not carry). Charter-altitude auditing verifies decisions against intent; it cannot catch what was never written down or audit a claim against its absent artefact. First-instance observation; captured at `log/captures.md`.

- methodology (line 2): **A principle is a lens, not a partition.** The per-principle audit structure forced cross-principle findings to be split and cross-referenced; future principle audits may be better served finding-first with the principles as tags. Paired with the observation that metrics are load-bearing for only three of the seven principles. Both captured at `log/captures.md`.

- methodology (line 3): **The brief format held, with one inherited blind spot.** The brief's watch-points and its pre-resolution of the output-path question were accurate; its SRP watch-points, drawn from session-log findings, inherited the session log's blind spot — the largest file in the codebase was invisible because no recent session touched it. Watch-points sourced from session logs see what sessions touched, not what sessions left alone.

- **Pre-S45 principles assessment closed; the findings document at `audits/p13-principles-baseline.md` carries one load-bearing, nine material, and twelve marginal findings plus four cross-principle patterns, all evidence-anchored. The substrate is sound; the debt is concentrated, addressable hygiene in the `apps/` composition layer and the cross-context structural-duplication cluster. Disposition belongs to the subsequent conversation. S45 — the messaging substrate and conversational protocol per the p13-epic Session 3 line — is next.**

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. *Pre-write reconciliation surfaces.* The six surfaces split one mechanical (D-number) and five findings. Three were structural-honesty findings that became user-question resolutions: surface 5's ActorReference consumer surface (which falsified the brief's surface-5 assumption and forced the D126 reshape), surface 3's absent `_auth.py` (which re-homed the auth-middleware work to `middleware.py` plus `get_tenant_context`), and surface 6's 729-line `_errors.py`. Two were lighter — surface 4's absent contract-test directory (deferred) and surface 2 (confirmation plus the fifth-use-case discovery). The session is the clearest instance to date of pre-write reconciliation doing architectural work: it did not merely catch drift, it superseded a charter forward commitment (D124's). The discipline's value at S44a sits at the decision altitude, not the documentation-drift altitude.

  2. *Compose-shape decision validation.* The S44-framing Item 1 settlement on compose-shape (ActorContext wraps TenantContext as a field) held cleanly. Writing the code, the `tenant_context = actor.tenant_context` extraction appears once per use case — five sites — and reads as a deliberate boundary, not ceremony: the use case receives the rich request envelope and hands the adapter exactly the narrow value object it needs. The extraction is the structural boundary made visible, as Item 1 framing claimed. The stronger validation came at surface 5: compose-shape is *why* the reshape was clean. Because ActorContext composes rather than subsumes, ActorReference could stay exactly as it was for the persisted field while ActorContext took the request-scoped role — two single-concern value objects, no refactor of the domain entities, the adapter, or the DTO. A subsume-shape ActorContext would have forced the persisted-identity problem to be solved by either growing the schema or faking a reconstruction. First-instance evidence: compose-shape is structurally honest, and it bought the clean separation that resolved finding 1.

  3. *File topology budget first-instance evidence.* The budget did catch an overage, and it was load-bearing. Surface 6 found `apps/api/_errors.py` at 729 lines — far past a ~400-line ceiling for the router-error-handler file class — and the budget table's `_errors.py` row carried no current size, so absent the verification surface the overage would have gone unseen and the AuthorisationDenied handler would have landed there (the path the brief named), growing the file further. The discipline did two things at once: it redirected the handler to `apps/api/_auth_errors.py` (also the structurally correct home per D104's auth-cross-cutting placement) and surfaced the existing overage for forward triage. The discipline's load-bearing claim sits at first-instance validation, not only at recurrence. The `_errors.py` split is forwarded to the Phase 2-A close hygiene list; promotion of the discipline to the methodology document evaluates at P13 close per the framing settlement.

  4. *Framing-conversation pre-write reconciliation methodology observation.* The brief inherited D124's `authored_by`-becomes-ActorContext forward commitment without verifying it against the live domain model — the brief's surface-5 framing searched for ActorReference at the application-layer altitude only. The framing-conversation reconciliation candidate (framing conversations verify forward commitments against the live charter and codebase state before decomposing work) is reinforced here at a sharper edge: the thing that needed verifying was not charter prose but a *forward commitment's structural soundness against the persistence layer*. The mitigation surface is the same — read the live state before drafting the decomposition — but the lesson is that a D-entry's forward commitment is a hypothesis, not a settled instruction. Captured as a distinct methodology candidate (the forward-commitment-evaluation pattern; see methodology line 1).

  5. *Substrate-application boundary check.* The S41 substrate-application boundary candidate fired cleanly at S44a between commits 3 and 4. Commits 1-3 closed the shared_kernel additions (the value object, the decorator, the policy) — substrate that imports nothing from `contexts/` or `apps/`. Commits 4-6 opened the existing-code modifications (the middleware dependency, the five use cases, the router). The transition surfaced no scope drift: the substrate landed exactly as the reshaped D126 specified, and commits 4-6 were signature-and-wiring changes within the framing-time projection. The boundary is a genuine shape-change point — substrate is additive and self-contained; application work is modification with a blast radius — but at S44a it was a clean checkpoint, not a re-scoping moment. Recurrence holds the candidate at its existing threshold.

  6. *Methodology line opportunities.* Three candidates surfaced, each captured at `log/captures.md` and carried as a methodology line below. The compose-shape extraction idiom (`actor.tenant_context` at the adapter call seam) is a clean pattern but is the expected consequence of a settled framing decision, not structural novelty — not promoted, per the captures-candidate threshold. The authorisation-keys-must-match concern the brief flagged was dissolved rather than managed: the five permission strings are named once as constants in `shared_kernel/authorisation.py` and referenced by both the decorator applications and the lookup, so there is no parallel-drafting fragility to discipline.

- methodology (line 1): **Forward-commitment-evaluation pattern.** A forward commitment embedded in a D-entry is a hypothesis about future structure, not a binding instruction. D124 committed that ActorReference would be superseded by ActorContext at the `authored_by` field; S44a pre-write reconciliation evaluated that against the persistence layer, found it structurally unsound, and D126 supersedes it with reasoning. First instance of a D-entry superseding an earlier D-entry's forward commitment. Recurrence test: the next D-entry carrying a forward commitment evaluated at a future session. Captured at `log/captures.md`.

- methodology (line 2): **Brief-vs-domain-model drift at the type altitude.** A sub-class of the brief path-drift pattern (promoted at pre-S44 hygiene), but about which layers a type identifier reaches rather than file-location naming. The brief asserted ActorReference's consumer surface from the S44-framing mental model; the live surface spanned the domain entities, adapter, CLI, DTO, audit drafts, and tests. The same drift omitted the fifth use case (`create_data_point`). Discipline addition: a brief that names a type or a use-case set verifies it with an explicit identifier search across every layer. First-instance candidate; captured at `log/captures.md`.

- methodology (line 3): **File topology budget first-instance load-bearing evidence.** The discipline caught `apps/api/_errors.py` at 729 lines and redirected the AuthorisationDenied handler to its structurally-correct home, validating the discipline's load-bearing claim at first instance rather than at recurrence. Promotion to the methodology document evaluates at P13 close per the S44-framing settlement, with this evidence cited. Captured at `log/captures.md`.

- **S44a closed; the Phase 2-A identity-and-permissions substrate is in place end-to-end. The four S44-framing settlements held: compose-shape ActorContext was structurally honest and bought the clean reshape; the D126 bundle held with its body restructured to three sub-commitments; the file topology budget did load-bearing first-instance work; the D116 collapse (no architecture.md edit) was correct. What diverged was the brief's code-side assumptions about the live ActorReference surface — caught by reconciliation before any code landed. S44b lands the write-path substrate and transport per `briefs/p13/s44b.md`.**

  1. *Pre-write reconciliation surfaces.* The pattern across S43 reconciliation: the brief was accurate on architecture and intent, drifted on paths and field-completeness. The four audit-finding-snapshot drifts were mechanical absorptions into the binding spec; the three execution-time adjustments (commits 2/3 swap, jurisdiction restoration, ports-with-adapter) were dependency-graph and charter-compliance corrections, not architectural disagreements.   2. *Forward-compat substrate-depth discipline, first build instance.* Case/DataPoint/Assertion landed in full; the Revisable Protocol shape committed without being exercised across the full Phase 2-A substrate (only DataPoint implements it at S43). Two forward-compat affordances landed unused: `DataPoint.certainty` (nullable, reserved for the D117 tiered-by-salience implementation at P15) and the ActorReference placeholder (superseded at S44 by ActorContext). Neither felt premature — both are single-column / single-field additions now versus refactor-forcing retrofits later, the D12 column-from-inception reasoning generalised. Heavier than a mid-package session — and it served the audit-trail discipline rather than burdening it: the binding specification (schema.md table shapes, the D-entry alternatives analysis) landed before the code, so every subsequent commit reconciled against a committed spec rather than the spec chasing the code.

The CLI's command surface drove a substrate change: the `create-data-point` action required a fifth use case (`create_data_point`) the brief's four-use-case list had not named. Methodology candidate: substrate sessions that ship a read-side HTTP surface without the matching write side should plan a CLI write path by default, and the CLI command surface sanity-checks the use-case set before the use cases are considered complete.

  5. *Operator-pause-at-substrate-completion as methodology candidate.* S43 closed at 7 of 10 commits at operator decision, after a Claude Code check-in surfaced the remaining three commits' scope. The pause sat at the substrate-completion boundary — domain, application, adapter, and CLI layers complete and green; the HTTP transport surface and the live-stack smoke remaining. Two forces drove it: the ~600 lines of intricate, interdependent API-wiring code still to write (routes, DTOs, query parser, the `_cross_context.py` wiring adapter, the `_agent_runtime_wiring.py` factory, `AppCompositions`, error handlers), and commit 9's image-rebuild step carrying real environmental variance. The operator re-scoped the remainder as S43b, a planned bridge session. This is the first instance of a deliberate substrate-and-transport split: the two prior bridge instances at P11 (S39 → S39b verification-and-hygiene; S40 → S40b methodologically-clean-artefact authoring) were unplanned corrections discovered at substrate close, and carried `corrects` / `corrected_by` relationships. S43 → S43b carries `paired_with` instead — S43b completes a planned split, it does not correct S43. The planned-bridge sub-variant is the load-bearing methodology data point of this session; first-instance evidence is captured here, and promotion to a `charter/methodology.md` line waits on a second instance of a future bounded-context substrate session producing the same split shape. The session-close-boundary pause also pairs with the S41 mid-session scope check at the substrate-application boundary: two sub-variants — mid-session and session-close — of one scope-versus-fatigue-management discipline, each with its own second-instance promotion threshold.

  6. *Methodology line opportunities.* Four candidates surfaced. The protocol-file-location convention settled at `shared_kernel/` — a cross-context Protocol referencing no context type belongs there, not at `padhanam/protocols/`, because the `platform-no-contexts` import-linter contract plus the shared-kernel-as-cross-context-type-home charter both point there. The path-drift pattern reached its second instance (S40's adjacent retrieval_evaluation adapter shape; S43's `adapters/outbound/postgres/` versus the brief's flat path) — brief drafts naming adapter and test paths must reconcile against the actual `adapters/outbound/{vendor}/` and flat-test-file conventions before commit 1; a third instance promotes it. The Revisable Protocol is the first cross-context Protocol in the codebase — the generic-Protocol-imports-no-context-type discipline is a first-instance observation. Case-as-substrate-vocabulary: the karma portfolio-of-relationships domain language landed as the context's first-class vocabulary (`portfolio` over `state_persistence`).

- methodology (line 1): **Planned-bridge-session sub-variant.** A deliberate substrate-and-transport split, distinct from the unplanned verification-and-hygiene (S39→S39b) and methodologically-clean-artefact (S40→S40b) sub-variants; first instance at S43→S43b, carrying `paired_with` rather than `corrects`. See reflection prompt 5. Paired with the substrate-completion-boundary scope-check candidate; promotion at second instance.

- methodology (line 3): **CLI-as-smoke-write-path.** Substrate sessions shipping a read-side HTTP surface without the write side should plan a CLI write path by default; the CLI command surface sanity-checks the use-case set. See reflection prompt 4.
