The email-wiring doubles integration tests pass. Three known docker-dependent environmental failures carry forward, not in scope, not introduced.

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. **The measurement (required) — PENDING, and honestly so.** The load-bearing deliverable of this session is the measured message count and full-pull floor, and **it could not be taken**: only google-calendar is connected in Nango; there is no google-mail connection, and the agent is `gmail.readonly`-scoped at most — it cannot OAuth-provision a mailbox. So the measurement is operator-gated behind the google-mail Nango provisioning step (the same gate calendar had at the Nango provisioning session). Consequently the two decisions that depend on it — the email sync-mechanism graduation (incremental, gated on volume) and the refresh-before-answer strategy (D150 Option A vs background-sync-then-serve, gated on the floor) — **remain open and must be decided from the operator-run smoke before S56b**. What reconnaissance predicts, to be confirmed live: at ~1,000–6,000 messages / 30 days, the two-call N+1 (list + thousands of batched gets + chunk + embed over Ollama) likely puts the full-pull floor in the multi-second-to-minutes range, which would (a) justify incremental sooner than calendar and (b) kill always-refresh-in-turn in favour of background-sync-then-serve. The substrate is built full-pull-only with the dormant history anchor exactly so that decision lands against the real number, not the estimate.

  2. **Chunk-store divergence — boundary held.** Body chunking is the largest divergence from calendar, and the injected-tools boundary stayed clean because the reconciliation drew the line correctly: the **embedder is inherited as a port** (`EmailChunkEmbeddingPort` → the apps bridge → ingestion's batch `ChunkEmbedderPort.embed`), while the **chunker is email-local** (`chunk_email`), because ingestion's chunking is not a standalone tool — it is welded into the format parsers and their `Source` coupling. Email did not pull itself into ingestion's pipeline: it owns its `email_chunks` store, calls the embedder through a thin consumer port, and never imports ingestion internals (the `layers-email` contract + the cross-context contracts hold). The temptation that would have breached the boundary — constructing a synthetic ingestion `Source` to reuse `plain_text_parser` — was declined; a 30-line local chunker is the honest cost of the clean boundary.

  3. **Set-diff deletion.** Unit-proven (`test_set_diff_tombstones_removed_message`: a stored live in-window message absent from the pull tombstones). The live confirmation (trash a Gmail message, re-pull) is operator-gated behind both the google-mail provisioning and a `gmail.readonly` agent that cannot trash; folded into the smoke Stage 3. One window-scope edge case noted for the live run: the set-diff scope is `received_at >= now - window_days`, so a message whose `received_at` is near the window boundary could oscillate in/out across pulls at the edge — benign (it re-upserts when back in window) but worth watching at the smoke.

  4. **S55b-2 baked confirmation.** Carried into this session per plan; the baked-image rebuild (retiring the S55b-2 synced-source residue and baking S56a) is part of the smoke's provisioning gate. Recorded in the smoke; executed at the operator's smoke run (the rebuild is deterministic but bundled with the provisioning gate the measurement needs).

methodology: Two pre-write reconciliation corrections (historyId anchor source; chunker-is-not-a-tool) both came from reconciling the strategic reconnaissance against exact code/vendor shapes at build time — the reconnaissance got the *shape* right (two-call, set-diff, incremental gotcha) but two *mechanics* needed the build-time check, which is the division of labour the reconnaissance-then-build split is meant to produce: strategy surfaces the gotchas, the build pins the signatures. The measurement being operator-gated is the honest limit of an agent-run substrate session against a vendor that requires interactive OAuth — the same shape as calendar, handled the same way (build the substrate, gate the live number on operator provisioning).

- Close verdict: the email data substrate is built end to end — two-call adapter, encrypted store + email-local chunk store, full-pull-only sync with set-diff deletion, body chunking via the inherited embedder + email-local chunker, the dormant history anchor — per D151, mirroring calendar with the reconnaissance divergences. 2125 unit+contract tests green from clean bytecode, 39 import-linter contracts kept (+layers-email), migration 0027 applied to both tenant DBs. **The load-bearing measurement is pending the operator's google-mail Nango provisioning + smoke run; the email sync-mechanism and refresh-strategy decisions are made from it before S56b opens.**

## 2026-06-03 — [S56b] Email conversation surface + five-way dispatch (S56 close)
roles: architect, engineer, technical writer
mode: build session (second of the S56 split, mirroring S55b). HEAD at open: `80e6740` (S56a wiring-proof close tip). Builds the email conversation surface and integrates it as the fifth MetaClassifier route, mirroring the calendar conversation surface (D138/D139/D140/D150) with the email-specific divergences from D151/D152.

The surface mirrors calendar's cell shape: a five-intent classifier (find_by_date_range, find_from_sender, find_by_subject, find_recent, unclear_email), refresh-before-answer through a port (D152 Option A), CitedResponse + resolution-ambiguity (find_by_subject is the ambiguity carrier), and five-way dispatch routing. The load-bearing divergence from calendar is **cite-directly, no snapshot** (D151: email content is immutable, so the citation references the live row rather than freezing an encrypted after_state snapshot — the inverse of D148 option b).

- Two operator holds, both honoured:
  - **The Option-A wiring is the load-bearing boundary.** The cell reaches the substrate *only* through `EmailRefreshPort`; it imports no `sync_email`. Background-sync-vs-incremental stays a pure wiring swap behind the port (D152). Verified live in the smoke (both refresh branches fire through the port) and structurally (the cell module imports the port, not the application use case).
  - **The smoke is a wiring-proof again.** Five-way routing live + refresh fires on both branches + cite-directly renders — proven. Volume-path proof and binding sync/refresh latency measurement stay open by design, gated on a representative inbox at dogfooding (the `tenant_a` mailbox is n=1 and unrepresentative; no sync/refresh architecture is decided on it).

- Produced (seven commits; charter ahead of code):
  - **Commit 1 (`950e5f8`)** `docs(charter): D152 ...` — D152 (email refresh Option A; background-sync/incremental deferred, measurement-gated; the cell-never-reaches-past-the-port clause) + the closed-union extensions (cell/routing) + current-package/p15-epic/architecture.
  - **Commit 2 (`fc6354c`)** `feat(email_conversation): cell + intent + query + response + cite-directly + resolution-ambiguity` — the EmailIntent union + parser, the query builder (window/sender/subject-resolution/recent), EmailConversationResponse (CitedResponse, "email" citation discriminator), the cell (mirroring calendar; cite-directly, no snapshot), `layers-email-conversation` (40 kept); 14 cell/intent/query/response unit tests.
  - **Commit 3 (`e1b2972`)** `feat(email_conversation): refresh port wired to Option A full-pull-in-turn` — EmailRefreshPort + EmailRefreshError, the `_maybe_refresh` timeout/fallback, the apps EmailRefreshAdapter over `sync_email`; 3 refresh fallback/timeout/success unit tests.
  - **Commit 4 (`7ea7795`)** `feat(messaging): MetaClassifier five-way routing to email_conversation` — CellIdentifier.EMAIL_CONVERSATION, the schema enum + routing-prompt body (option 5, read-only + disambiguation guidance), the dispatch lexicon, the rule-based email branch (before the generic mirror read-verbs), the eval-runner surface primitive, and `_run_email_conversation_cell` + `_resolve_email_connection_id` + runner registration in the API; the four-way→five-way routing conformance widening; rule-based + LLM email-routing unit tests.
  - **Commit 5 (`c1654f0`)** `test(p15/s56b): email-conversation + five-way routing gold sets` — the email-conversation intent gold set (20 entries) + the five-way routing gold set (30 entries, with two new ambiguous email/calendar-band entries); loader tests.
  - **Commit 6 (`69f88a1`)** `test(p15/s56b): register email_conversation in ConversationFlow conformance` — the email registration module (auto-discovered), CitedResponse-conformance payload-key entry, resolution-ambiguity duplicate-subject fixture; all conformance scenarios green with five implementers.
  - **Commit 7 (`<this commit>`)** `docs(p15/s56b): email dispatch smoke (executed) + session log + S56b/S56 close` — the procedural dispatch smoke (executed live), this entry, the current-package S56b/S56 close markers, p15-epic S56-complete.

- Decisions: D152 (`charter/decisions.md`, Commit 1). No methodology.md write (build mode, D47).

Three known docker-dependent environmental failures carry forward, not in scope, not introduced.

- Smoke (executed live 2026-06-03, `docs/smoke/p15_s56b_email_dispatch.md`):
  - **Stage 1 (five-way routing) — PASS.** The live LLM meta-classifier routed both email phrasings to `email_conversation` at 0.90.
  - **Stage 2 (no-regression) — PASS.** manual_entry / audit / mirror / calendar all routed correctly at 0.90 alongside the fifth route.
  - **Stage 3a (refresh fallback) — PASS.** The email cell, built with the live structured-output port + the real `tenant_a` store + the real D152 refresh adapter, fell back to the cached store on a default-timeout refresh, cited 1 email directly, and carried the staleness note.
  - **Stage 3b (refresh success) — PASS.** With a 120s timeout the refresh completed in-turn (no staleness note). Both Option-A branches proven live; the cell reached the substrate solely through the port.

- Reflection: The cell mirrored calendar cleanly because the two-threshold abstractions (CitedResponse, resolution-ambiguity, the ConversationFlow harness, the per-surface eval primitive, the five-way routing conformance) were already structurally guaranteed by the calendar instance — the second instance landed by extension, not by new abstraction, which is the discipline working as intended. The one real divergence — cite-directly vs the D148 snapshot — fell out of the data property (email content immutable) and required no new machinery, only the *absence* of the snapshot hook the calendar cell carries. The refresh-port boundary held under the live smoke: the same timeout-fallback the calendar cell uses produced the graceful cached-store answer when the live Gmail pull was slow, which is exactly the degradation the operator's "never reach past the port" hold protects.

methodology: The fifth surface added by pure extension across five routing/conformance seams (CellIdentifier, schema enum, dispatch lexicon, rule-based branch, eval primitive, routing conformance, CitedResponse map, resolution-ambiguity factory, ConversationFlow registration) with no new abstraction is the strongest evidence yet that the P14 conversational substrate's two-threshold abstractions were drawn at the right altitude — adding a surface is now a checklist, not a design. Not a promotion candidate (existing methodology applied correctly; no structural novelty, no 3x recurrence).

- Close verdict: the email conversation surface is built and integrated as the fifth MetaClassifier route, mirroring calendar with cite-directly as the sole load-bearing divergence (D151), refresh-before-answer behind a port (D152 Option A). 2155 unit+contract tests green from clean bytecode, 40 import-linter contracts kept (+layers-email-conversation), all ConversationFlow conformance scenarios green with five implementers. The live wiring-proof smoke is green (five-way routing, both refresh branches, cite-directly). **S56b closes; S56 closes; P15 continues.** Volume-path + binding sync/refresh measurement remain deferred to a representative inbox at dogfooding — where D152's background-sync-vs-incremental decision (a wiring swap behind the port) gets its number.

## 2026-06-03 — [S57] Threshold-briefing + P15 close
roles: architect, engineer, technical writer
mode: build session (the P15-closing session). HEAD at open: `1c2c9a9` (S56b close tip). Builds the proactive threshold-briefing arc on the S53/S54 broadcast machinery — ThresholdEvaluator + threshold-briefing as the two-stage chain — and closes P15. This is outbound broadcast, reusing BroadcastFlow + BroadcastDispatch, not the conversation/dispatch path.

- **Pre-write reconciliation caught the load-bearing wrong assumption before the charter commit.** The epic (line 35) and the S57 brief's D153 both asserted the evaluator "polls the audit chain for state-change matches." The reconciliation gate falsified it: `sync_calendar` writes only to the meetings store (upsert/tombstone) and emits **no** audit events, so calendar cancellations/moves are not in the chain (the only calendar audit events are the conversation cell's `meeting_citation` snapshots). And more fundamentally, **conflict/double-booking was never a state-*change* event** — it is a standing condition over the current set, a query. Surfaced and the operator chose **Design 1: evaluate over the calendar state store**, a single coherent model (both rules are state queries) over a hybrid that makes cancel/move into events but special-cases conflict — and one that avoids pulling an AuditPort into the calendar substrate at close. The brief's "the cancellation tombstone is in tenant_a's audit chain" was a conflation of the `meeting_citation` snapshot (a citation of the since-cancelled meeting) with a state-change record (which does not exist). This is the reconciliation-then-build front-loading working exactly as intended.

- Produced (seven commits + one test-fix follow-up; charter ahead of code):
  - **Commit 1 (`c7ce128`)** `docs(charter): D153 ... + D154 P15 close ...` — D153 (reworded to state-store evaluation, the narrow cancel+conflict set, THRESHOLD_CROSSED re-keyed on derived-state identity, the restraint discipline) + D154 (P15 close interpretation); epic line-35 correction; current-package/p15-epic close markers; architecture sub-section; deferred-decisions (audit-chain CDC); captures (reverse-Kano candidate).
  - **Commit 2 (`ead983c`)** `feat(broadcast): ThresholdEvaluator implementer + configured-rules schema` — `contexts/threshold_briefing/`: the rule schema (two must-haves active, deferred shapes supported), pure evaluation functions (cancel + conflict), RuleMatch, the evaluator (refresh→read state→evaluate→emit), the three consumer ports, `BroadcastTriggerType += SCHEDULED_EVALUATION`, `layers-threshold-briefing` (41 contracts); 13 unit tests.
  - **Commit 3 (`a6ac323`)** `feat(broadcast): threshold-briefing implementer` — the crossing read-model, the briefing response + render, composer + notifier ports, the implementer (compose, fall back to summary on LLM failure, render, send), the LiteLLM composer adapter; 6 unit tests.
  - **Commit 4 (`83acd08`)** `feat(broadcast): refresh-then-evaluate scheduled trigger + idempotency + wiring` — idempotency for SCHEDULED_EVALUATION (None) + THRESHOLD_CROSSED (crossing identity); BROADCAST_INITIATED after_state carries the crossing metadata (traceability); the four apps wiring adapters (state reader, lazy refresh, emitter-via-FireTrigger, notifier); main.py registers both implementers (the three-implementer set complete); tests.
  - **Commit 5 (`cd3ef47`)** `test(contract): BroadcastFlow three-implementer conformance + threshold rule eval` — registers both implementers with the harness; the rule-eval conformance (two-stage hand-off, restraint no-cross); three-implementer completeness (close criterion 1).
  - **Commit follow-up (`f2365c7`)** `fix(test): update BroadcastTriggerType count for SCHEDULED_EVALUATION` — the shared_kernel value-set test asserted the old count of 5 (a verification miss in Commit 2: the enum addition was checked against the threshold subset but not this test).
  - **Commit 6-fix (`8fa8203`)** `fix(broadcast): stabilise cancellation crossing identity + lower-bound window` — the two live-smoke findings (below), fixed in the threshold context, with D153 + architecture corrected and the deeper calendar fixes deferred.
  - **Commit 7 (`<this commit>`)** `docs(p15/s57): threshold-briefing smoke + P15 close + session log` — the executed smoke, this entry, the P15 close verdict.

- Decisions: D153, D154 (`charter/decisions.md`). No methodology.md write (build mode, D47).

- Tests: close run **2190 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed** (tests/unit + tests/contract, clean bytecode; +35 over the S56b 2155 baseline) plus the post-fix threshold/idempotency/conformance subset green; import-linter **41/41 kept** (+`layers-threshold-briefing`); AST enforcement green (9). Three known docker-dependent environmental failures carry forward, not in scope, not introduced.

- Smoke (executed live 2026-06-03, `docs/smoke/p15_s57_threshold_briefing.md`): a wiring-proof of the two-stage chain over live tenant_a state. Stage A (refresh-then-evaluate) — PASS: the evaluator refreshed calendar, read the state store, emitted one stable-identity cancellation crossing. Stage B (two-stage hand-off) — PASS: metadata round-tripped, the briefing fired, the LLM composer errored and the **fallback-to-summary** path fired and rendered (the resilience guarantee proven; happy-path compose not separately confirmed this run). Stage C (no-cross / restraint) — PASS: the conflict rule over the live confirmed set (no overlaps) emitted zero. The proactive end-to-end fire (operator cancellation → WhatsApp) and idempotency re-fire stay operator-gated.

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. **Restraint in practice (required).** The no-cross case held live (Stage C: conflict rule over the real confirmed set → zero crossings) and structurally (`test_evaluate_no_cross`, `test_evaluator_emits_nothing_on_no_cross`). The reverse-category discipline is observable in how narrow the active set is — two rules, with the schema explicitly enumerating five deferred shapes it declines to enable (`PHASE_2A_ACTIVE_RULE_TYPES` is a strict subset of `ThresholdRuleType`), and `evaluate` structurally skips any rule outside the active set so restraint is enforced, not assumed. The live run sharpened the point: the `cancelled_at`-churn finding was a *reverse-Kano-in-the-mechanism* bug — a naive idempotency key would have re-briefed the same cancellation every scan, the precise noise that collapses a proactive surface's value. Restraint is not only which rules fire but that each crossing fires *once*. **The captures observation is worth promoting to methodology at the P15 audit** — "restraint against the reverse category on any platform-initiated surface" generalises beyond this one surface, and the live finding adds a second face (restraint applies to firing *frequency* and *content*, not only rule selection); held as a candidate per the 3x-or-structural-novelty bar.
  2. **Proactivity.** Confirmed live: the scheduled trigger fired the evaluation and the briefing **without a conversation turn** (Stage A/B driven from a `SCHEDULED_EVALUATION` trigger, no inbound). This is the property that distinguishes refresh-then-evaluate from the conversation cell's in-turn freshness (D150) — the briefing surfaces a change the user never asked about.
  3. **ThresholdEvaluator as a BroadcastFlow implementer — it fit, with a noted strain.** The evaluator satisfies BroadcastFlow cleanly (it has `fire`, returns a BroadcastResponse, registers under a trigger type), but the fit is slightly forced: its `fire` does not send a user-facing message — it emits a downstream trigger. The two-stage chain (SCHEDULED_EVALUATION → evaluator → THRESHOLD_CROSSED → briefing) reuses BroadcastDispatch for both a non-user-facing scan and a user-facing send, which is economical but means "BroadcastFlow" now covers two semantically different things (compose-and-send vs. evaluate-and-emit). Worth flagging for the P15 audit: if a third evaluator-shaped implementer appears, a distinct `Evaluator`/`Scan` abstraction alongside BroadcastFlow may be the second-instance threshold.
  4. **P15 close honesty.** The nine criteria are met as written (Stage 4 walk). The email debts are mapped to the dogfooding gate **in the close verdict itself** (D154, criterion 7 recorded wiring-proven-not-volume-proven, criterion 9 as dogfooding-*ready*), not obscured — the close states the gap and where it resolves.

methodology: The session's load-bearing lesson is that the **live smoke caught a class of bug the stubbed tests structurally could not** — the `cancelled_at` churn is a *runtime substrate behaviour* (the tombstone resets the timestamp on every sync), invisible to tests that stub the store, and it would have shipped a re-brief-every-scan defect. This is the S4 Langfuse lesson recurring in a new form (CLI/unit green while the real-substrate behaviour differs) and reinforces the browser/live-verification discipline for any acceptance criterion that depends on real substrate state, not only UI. The reconciliation gate caught the *static* wrong assumption (audit-chain polling) before the charter commit; the live smoke caught the *dynamic* one (cancelled_at churn) before close — two different gates, two different classes of error, both load-bearing.

- Close verdict: the proactive threshold-briefing arc is built and integrated as the two-stage chain on the broadcast machinery, evaluating over the calendar state store per D153 (the reconciled model), with the narrow cancel+conflict must-have set under the restraint-against-reverse-Kano discipline. 2190 unit+contract tests green from clean bytecode, 41 import-linter contracts kept (+`layers-threshold-briefing`), AST green; the three-implementer BroadcastFlow set is complete. The live wiring-proof is green (refresh-then-evaluate, two-stage hand-off with proven fallback, restraint), and surfaced + fixed two real substrate-behaviour findings. **P15 closes at S57 (D154)**: all nine close criteria met, the email volume debts + the calendar meeting-moved threshold mapped to the Phase 2-A dogfooding gate. **The next strategic-mode steps are the P15 audit (drift-finding; the reverse-Kano + BroadcastFlow-strain candidates triaged there) and the Phase 2-A dogfooding gate (one week of real use + senior-leader-ICP validation).** P16 follows the gate.

## 2026-06-03 — [P15-audit-residue] Corrective: THRESHOLD_CROSSED idempotency + audit residue sweep
roles: engineer, technical writer
mode: corrective build session (no new S-number, matching the S55a-fix precedent). HEAD at open: `781ffa1` (the P15-audit charter hygiene-sweep tip). Remediates the code residue the P15 audit surfaced (`docs/audit/p15-audit-evidence.md`) plus the latent `idempotency.py` fallback bug; the charter-only half (D155 + the hygiene sweep) landed first at `1d64d28`/`781ffa1`. Classification **corrective**: it fixes shipped stale residue and a latent re-introduction of a fixed bug, booked honestly into the CFR ledger.

- **Pre-write reconciliation — the fallback decision was delete-vs-fix and was reconciled against current code, not guessed.** Traced the THRESHOLD_CROSSED metadata path from emitter through FireTrigger to `resolve_idempotency_key`. Two producers reach the resolver: (1) the in-process emitter `apps/api/_threshold_briefing_wiring.py:182-187` always sets `crossing_identity` via `RuleMatch.to_trigger_metadata`; (2) **the HTTP trigger endpoint `apps/api/routers/triggers.py:62,152-157`** accepts `FireTriggerRequest.trigger_type` over the *full* `BroadcastTriggerType` enum (THRESHOLD_CROSSED included) with a caller-supplied open `metadata` dict that need not carry `crossing_identity`. Because producer (2) makes the fallback genuinely reachable, deleting it would crash a structurally-permitted request → **reconstruct, not delete**: the fallback now mirrors `RuleMatch.crossing_identity()` (cancellation `rule_id:google_event_id`; conflict `rule_id` + sorted pair), never embedding `cancelled_at`. (Grep evidence: `resolve_idempotency_key` callers = `fire_trigger.py:98` + the `triggers.py` import; the only THRESHOLD_CROSSED TriggerContext constructors are the wiring emitter and the HTTP router.)

- Produced (charter ahead of code, four commits):
  - **Commit 1 (`829582e`)** `docs(charter): captures — D153 residue-propagation + latent-fallback lesson` — the [P15-audit-residue] capture: the correction-sweep-checklist candidate and the dead-or-defensive-path latent-bug observation, with the reconciliation finding recorded.
  - **Commit 2 (`be829bc`)** `fix(p15/audit): stabilise THRESHOLD_CROSSED idempotency off cancelled_at` — `idempotency.py` fallback reconstructs the stable identity (no `cancelled_at`); docstrings corrected; `test_idempotency.py` gains an SSOT-conformance test binding the resolved key to `RuleMatch.crossing_identity()` (incl. a churned-`cancelled_at`-re-keys-the-same assertion) and a reconstruction test, and the two fixtures that baked in the `cancelled_at`-bearing shape are corrected.
  - **Commit 3 (`99c8920`)** `docs(p15/audit): sweep matched_audit_event_id + email-future docstring residue` — `broadcast_flow.py` + `test_broadcast_flow.py` (off `matched_audit_event_id`), `conversation_flow.py` (four-type union names `email`), `sync_calendar.py`/`sync_email.py` (the D155 no-audit-events note).
  - **Commit 4 (`<this commit>`)** `docs(p15/audit): session log + close` — this entry.

- Tests: `make lint` from cleared bytecode → import-linter **41/41 kept**, AST enforcement green (9); `tests/unit tests/contract` from cleared bytecode → **exit 0** (the py3.14/pytest non-TTY quirk suppresses the final tally line, but exit 0 confirms zero failures; the `test_idempotency.py` subset shows 13 green incl. the new SSOT-conformance + reconstruction tests). The three known docker-dependent live-infra failures in the full tier carry forward unchanged, not in scope, not introduced.

- Reflection prompts answered:

  1. **The correction-sweep lesson.** D153 reached the code SSOT (`rule_match.py`) and the rewritten prose but not five secondary surfaces, surfacing only at a dedicated audit. This is **distinct from pre-write reconciliation**: reconciliation guards the *new* code against a wrong assumption before writing; a correction sweep guards the *old* shape's *removal* after a correcting decision lands. Its checkable tell is concrete — before closing any session whose deliverable is a correction, grep the old shape's identifier (here `matched_audit_event_id`, `cancelled_at`-in-identity) across `contexts apps shared_kernel tests charter`. Promotion is **held, not taken**: D149 was the first reconciliation correction, D153 the second; the candidate meets the bar at a third instance leaving similar residue, or on structural-novelty grounds at the Phase 2-A close audit (strategic mode owns the promotion per D47). Recorded as a captures candidate, not promoted here.

  2. **The latent-fallback finding.** The fallback was **defensive, not dead** (the HTTP path reaches it), which makes the bug worse than a dead branch: it is a live-reachable path the green suite *actively asserted in its buggy form* (`test_threshold_crossed_falls_back_to_composite_when_identity_absent` checked the `cancelled_at`-bearing key). So the suite did not merely miss the bug — it locked it in. This is the **same face** as the stale-bytecode enforcement masking and the S57 tombstone churn: each is a green that does not exercise the real path (stale `.pyc` → contract never actually run; stubbed store → runtime churn never seen; a fixture asserting the wrong shape → the corrected shape never demanded). All three are instances of the **live-substrate / real-path verification gate** candidate. The distinct sub-lesson here: a unit test can be *worse* than absent when its fixture encodes the bug as the expected value — so the corrective test now binds to the cross-context SSOT (`RuleMatch.crossing_identity()`) rather than to a hand-written expected string, which a future shape change would force to update in one place.

  3. **Corrective classification.** This is the **second `corrective` session** after the ChannelResolver corrective (the two-threshold-rule retraction). The CFR ledger now carries two corrective sessions; both originate in front-loaded-abstraction or correction-propagation drift caught by a later gate (reconciliation, audit) rather than by the green suite — a pattern worth the Phase 2-A close audit's attention when it reviews the corrective rate against the build rate.

methodology: The corrective work confirms a layered-gates picture the P15 arc has been drawing: the **reconciliation gate** catches static wrong assumptions before the write (S57: audit-chain polling), the **live smoke** catches runtime-substrate assumptions before close (S57: `cancelled_at` churn), and the **audit pass** catches correction-propagation residue after close (this session: five stale surfaces + the latent fallback). Each gate catches a class the prior one structurally cannot. The new candidate — a correction-sweep checklist — is the natural fourth, folding the audit's residue-finding back into the closing session that makes the correction, so the audit becomes a backstop rather than the primary catch. Held for strategic-mode promotion per D47.

- Close verdict: the THRESHOLD_CROSSED idempotency key carries no `cancelled_at` and no `matched_audit_event_id` on any path (the fallback reconstructs the stable identity, reachable via the HTTP endpoint), bound to the `RuleMatch` SSOT by a new unit test; the `matched_audit_event_id` / email-future docstring + fixture residue is swept from `shared_kernel` and the broadcast/conversation tests; the two sync entry points carry the D155 note. `make lint` 41/41 + AST green and unit+contract exit 0 from cleared bytecode. ## S58 — P16 opens: daily-driver first slice (prioritised-today surface + Commitment + Day)
roles: engineer, designer (the operator surface), technical writer (the smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S58 daily-driver-first-slice prompt

S58 opened P16 and shipped the first instance of the Phase 2 whole-life causal daily driver per D156/D157: a real operator-facing prioritised-today surface over existing read-surfaces plus a minimal user-authored `Commitment` with render-time staleness. The slice is the thinnest dogfoodable cut that shows the active-not-passive differentiator — an overdue commitment surfacing as a "behind on this" row — which is the Phase 2-A dogfooding deliverable the operator's abandoned standalone tracker (D156) is the evidence for. New `contexts/daily_driver/` (four-layer hexagonal, plain package mirroring portfolio), migration `0028_daily_driver_substrate`, the HTTP routes, and the served `/app` operator page. Five code commits plus the charter commit; 42 import-linter contracts kept; 2203 unit+contract tests pass from cleared bytecode.

- Produced: Six commits. (1) `docs(charter): D157 + P16 open — daily-driver first slice` (e648294) — D157 index + full entry, the P16-in-flight current-package marker with the reconciliation findings, the deferred-decisions "Cadence-with-staleness primitive (full)" entry. (2) `feat(p16/s58): minimal Commitment substrate + Day ordering + today-aggregation` (8b6cf77) — the full `contexts/daily_driver/` context (domain: Commitment + completion log, the minimal Day concept, the render-time staleness rule, `build_today_view`; ports: CommitmentRepository, DayRepository, the OpenCasesReader consumer port; application: create_commitment, log_commitment_completion, list_today, set_today_order, mark_item_done; Postgres adapters bound at construction), migration 0028 (three per-tenant tables, tenant_id + jurisdiction per D12, no status/overdue column), charter/schema.md (same commit as the migration), the import-linter `layers-daily-driver` + independence/purity registrations, the four daily_driver authorisations granted to ROLE_OPERATOR, plus domain/application/contract tests. (3) `feat(p16/s58): today's-items HTTP read aggregation + routes + wiring` (caea865) — the five routes, `_daily_driver_wiring.py` (per-request-tenant CommitmentRepositoryRouter / DayRepositoryRouter + the OpenCasesReaderAdapter composing portfolio list_cases OPEN-filtered, the D17 seam mirroring daily-briefing), main.py composition seams, the `/app` _PUBLIC_PATHS exemption, HTTP route tests. (4) `feat(p16/s58): daily-driver operator surface (served HTML) + open-into-cell` (5ae10a8) — the self-contained brand-styled vanilla-JS page at apps/api/static/daily_driver.html. (5)/(6) this docs commit — the procedural smoke at docs/smoke/p16_s58_daily_driver.md, this session-log entry, and the P16/S58 close marker.

- Decisions: D157 (the daily-driver first slice as a real apps-layer prioritised-today surface over existing read-surfaces plus a minimal user-authored Commitment with render-time staleness; first instance of D156's daily driver, minimal instance of the deferred cadence-with-staleness primitive). No D-entries beyond D157.

- Tests: 2203 unit+contract tests pass from cleared bytecode (+30 over the pre-session baseline: 7 staleness + 4 commitment-domain + 5 view-builder + 7 application + 4 HTTP-route + 4 tenant-isolation, minus none; two golden permission-set assertions updated for the four new daily_driver authorisations). 43 of 42 import-linter contracts kept (+1 `layers-daily-driver`). AST/enforcement green (9 passed). The live browser verification (AC5/AC6/AC7) is **operator-gated** at the procedural smoke — the build environment cannot reach docker, Caddy, or a browser (the S45/S55a/S56b procedural-then-executed precedent).

- Reflection (the reconciliation outcome, prompt 1): **Substantive because it reshaped the slice.** Four findings, all recorded in current-package.md and D157. (F1) **No web surface existed at all** — apps/api was pure JSON, zero StaticFiles/HTML/React. The operator UI is genuinely net-new; rather than stand up a separate front-end toolchain (out of scope for a thin slice), the surface is one self-contained HTML page served from the API at the auth-exempt `/app` path, styled from the brand tokens. (F2) **Item sources:** OPEN Cases are real and HTTP-exposed (`list_cases`); Commitments are new this slice; **fired_triggers/briefings were named OUT** — `fired_triggers` has no reader and is low-content idempotency substrate, and `DailyBriefingReader` has no HTTP surface, so wiring either would add surface without showing anything the overdue commitment doesn't show better, and the prompt's own guidance is to name a non-listable source out rather than invent a store. The first list renders OPEN Cases + Commitments, which is honest and sufficient. (F3) **No conversation thread is persisted as a listable entity** — ConversationFlow is stateless per turn (D115); cells run via the messaging inbound webhook + MetaClassifier, not HTTP. (F4) **The consequential one — open-into-cell:** there is no HTTP "run a cell on item X" surface, so "open an item into its conversation cell" wires as open-the-cell-*context* — for a Case, the existing `GET /api/v1/portfolio/cases/{id}` (`get_case_detail`, the mirror-conversation read context, rendered as the side panel); for a Commitment, its detail panel. The live conversational-turn-over-HTTP path is named out of scope. The S4 Langfuse precedent held: building the surface against the *real* endpoints (not the design sketch) is what surfaced that open-into-cell had no live HTTP target — a sketch-built surface would have shipped a dead "open" button.

- Reflection (the felt-differentiator test, prompt 2): **Substantive paragraph — this is the question the whole pivot rests on.** At the code+test level the differentiator is structurally present and verified: `test_view_builder.test_overdue_commitment_is_behind_and_sorts_first` and `test_application.test_list_today_surfaces_overdue_first` both assert that an overdue Commitment computes to BEHIND and sorts to the top of the list, and `test_logging_completion_clears_overdue` asserts the completion loop flips it back to ON_TRACK. The surface renders BEHIND as a red pill with a "behind on this — N days over" detail at the top, and "✓ Did it" runs the completion-clears-overdue loop live. Whether it *reads* as the system noticing something went quiet — rather than as just another row — is the genuinely UI-level judgement, and that is honestly **operator-gated**: I cannot run the browser in this environment, so the felt-quality verdict is deferred to the operator's Stage-3 smoke run, where it is the explicit close question. My structural confidence is high (the overdue row is visually distinct, top-pinned, and carries an elapsed-time detail, which is the minimum for "noticing"); the felt confidence is the operator's to give. This is the right division: the code makes the differentiator *present and correct*; only dogfooding can make it *felt*.

- Reflection (compute-versus-persist, prompt 3): Compute-at-render held cleanly and nothing forced persisted status/overdue earlier than expected. The domain `staleness` functions take `now` as an injected parameter (the application layer mints `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`), keeping the domain pure and the overdue computation fully unit-testable without time mocking; `build_today_view` computes status and default priority entirely from the completion-log last-activity against the interval. The only state that persists is the user's per-day `position` and `done` mark in `day_item_states` — and even there, ordering and done are independent upserts (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on the one column each) so reordering never clobbers a done mark. One honest seam the compute-at-render choice surfaced: a freshly UI-created commitment is never overdue (last activity = creation = now), so demonstrating the BEHIND state at smoke time needs a backdated seed (the smoke's Stage 2 inserts one with `created_at = now - 30 days`) — that is a demo-seeding wrinkle, not a design pressure toward persistence. The day boundary is UTC for this slice (operator-timezone day boundaries are a named Phase 2-B refinement); that is the one place a future requirement (timezone-correct "today") will touch, and it is isolated to the application layer's `now.date()`.

- Did the slice land end-to-end at S58 or split to S59? **At the code+test level it landed end-to-end** — every layer is wired and green (substrate → read aggregation → HTTP routes → served surface → open-into-cell), and the surface is a real brand-styled page, not a harness. The one thing not closed in-session is the **live browser confirmation** of AC5/AC6/AC7, which is operator-gated by the no-docker build environment (the established procedural-then-executed precedent, not an S59 surface-polish split). No S59 is scheduled; if the operator's Stage-3 browser run surfaces a polish gap (felt-quality or interaction), that becomes the S59 scope and is recorded then.

methodology: The reconciliation-shapes-the-slice discipline earned its keep again — the load-bearing finding (open-into-cell has no live HTTP target; F4) was invisible from the design sketch and only emerged from reading the real read-surfaces, the S4 Langfuse pattern recurring at a UI boundary. Candidate (held, not promoted): "name the non-listable source out rather than invent a store for it" as an explicit thin-slice discipline — it kept fired_triggers/briefings out of the first list cleanly; one instance, watch for recurrence.

## [dogfood-setup] — Personal tenant, scoped wipe, pinned deploy (operational chore)
roles: engineer, technical writer (the runbook)
mode: chore/ops — no domain feature code

Provisioned the operator's dogfooding environment so the daily driver can run on real personal data, on a stable commit, advanced deliberately. A dedicated personal tenant on the database-per-tenant topology (D32), a guarded scoped wipe, a runbook, and a pinned stable tag. No domain code shipped. Personal tenant id: `00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000d001` ("d" = dogfood, neutral — encodes no real identity). Stable tag: `dogfood-stable`.

- Produced: Five commits. (1) `docs(charter): wipe-completeness requirement on personal-graph isolation` (813cd40) — extends the deferred "Personal causal-graph isolation and encryption posture" entry with the wipe-completeness requirement (Postgres drop today; grows to a Neo4j delete-by-tenant-property plus a Langfuse trace clear as personal data spreads). (2) `chore(dogfood): provision isolated personal tenant` (979b5a8) — `postgres-tenant-personal` container + volume + `POSTGRES_TENANT_PERSONAL_*` env passthrough in compose.yaml, synthetic creds in `.env.example`, `ops/dogfood_provision.py` (registers the tenant in the control plane with an encrypted connection config per D34, idempotent), and `make dogfood-provision`/`dogfood-token`/`dogfood-wipe` targets. (3) `chore(dogfood): scoped wipe command + guard` (d511066) — `ops/dogfood_wipe.sh`, three guard layers. (4) `docs(dogfood): personal-tenant dogfooding runbook` (af00ba4) — `docs/ops/dogfood-runbook.md`. (5) this session-log commit, plus the `dogfood-stable` tag.

- Reflection (provisioning reconciliation, prompt 1): Tenants are **dedicated Postgres containers** (`postgres-tenant-{a,b}`) on the database-per-tenant topology (D32), each with its own volume and `POSTGRES_TENANT_<LABEL>_*` env creds; the api container passes those through so ops scripts can build plaintext `TenantConnectionConfig`s at registration time. Registration is `ops/seed_tenants.py` calling `register_tenant(...)`, which stores the connection config **encrypted** in the control-plane registry (D34); `TenantPostgresSettings.for_tenant(label)` is **generic** (env prefix `POSTGRES_TENANT_<LABEL>_`, host default `postgres-tenant-<label>`), so a `personal` label needs no code change. Migration is `ops/migrate.py`, which **iterates every registered tenant** from the registry — so once the personal tenant is registered, `make migrate` migrates it through `0028`. The personal tenant therefore needed **a little new tooling, not much**: the compose service/volume/env passthrough (infra config), and a minimal `ops/dogfood_provision.py` (registration), kept separate from `seed_tenants.py` so the deterministic a/b test set stays clean. Two build-time wrinkles the live run surfaced: the running api predated the env passthrough (recreated it to pick up `POSTGRES_TENANT_PERSONAL_*`), and `make sync-code` does not copy `ops/` (copied it explicitly so the container saw the new provision script) — both ops-iteration artefacts, not design issues.

- Reflection (wipe today vs later, prompt 2): The wipe is a **single clean database drop today** — `DROP DATABASE` + `CREATE DATABASE` inside the `postgres-tenant-personal` container, then re-migrate. Verified live: the personal tenant went from 1 item to 0 while tenant_a stayed at 12 and the three daily-driver tables were re-created. Because the daily driver is **Postgres-only**, that single drop *is* a complete wipe right now. It will **not** stay complete: once personal data reaches Neo4j (the causal-decision-graph slice — a shared instance scoped by `tenant_id` property per D63, **not** a per-tenant database) a complete wipe also needs a **delete-by-tenant-property** Cypher, and once conversational cells capture prompts it needs a **Langfuse trace clear**. Both are named out of scope here and written into the deferred-decisions entry and the runbook, so the later slices inherit the requirement rather than rediscovering it. This is the wipe-completeness argument *for* resolving the personal-graph isolation decision toward a per-tenant/separate graph store: clean-wipeability is structurally harder to guarantee on a shared property-scoped store than on a database you can drop.

- Reflection (synthetic-seed-only boundary, prompt 3): The rule held without strain. All creds are synthetic (`tenant_personal`), the tenant id is a neutral deterministic placeholder, the live-seeded commitment was literally named "SYNTHETIC personal dogfood commitment", and `.env` (which would hold any real values) is gitignored. The one place the rule was *at risk* is conceptual, not actual: the entire point of this tenant is to hold the operator's **real** personal data during dogfooding — so the boundary that matters is "real data lives only in the running `postgres-tenant-personal` volume on the operator's machine, never in the repo, the seeds, the docs, or the synthetic test fixtures." The wipe exists partly to honour that boundary (a clean exit for real data), and the guard exists so honouring it can never collateral-damage the test tenants. `git grep` over the new artefacts found only image digests and the pre-existing synthetic `admin@padhanam.local` — no real identity.

- The guard (load-bearing): three independent layers in `ops/dogfood_wipe.sh` — (1) the container boundary (every destructive statement runs inside `postgres-tenant-personal` via `compose exec`, structurally unable to reach another instance), (2) a hardcoded target (an argument may only re-confirm `personal`, never redirect), (3) a refuse-list (aborts if the resolved service/db match a/b/control names, defending a tampered `.env`). All three verified: the wipe refuses `a`, refuses `tenant_b`, and refuses a tampered `POSTGRES_TENANT_PERSONAL_DB=tenant_a`.

methodology: A second face of the live-substrate lesson at the *ops* layer, sibling to the S58 browser-boundary instance — `make sync-code` silently omits `ops/`, so the provisioning script was absent in the container and `python -m ops.dogfood_provision` failed with a bare "No module named"; only running it live surfaced the gap (a green-by-omission, not a green-by-correctness). Minor, not promotion-worthy alone, but it rhymes with the live-substrate-verification-gate candidate: tooling that is never exercised against the real container lies about being wired. (Note recorded here rather than in captures — it is an ops-iteration artefact, not a recurring design pattern.)

## S59 — P16: live conversational-turn-over-HTTP cell surface (the conversation cell)
roles: engineer, architect (the stateless web-adapter seam), designer (the conversation drawer), technical writer (the smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S59 conversation-cell prompt

S59 turned the daily driver's open-into-cell from the S58 read-only context panel into a **live conversation over HTTP** (D158): `/app` opening a Case now runs the existing portfolio **mirror-conversation cell**'s `open` then `turn` over a new tenant-scoped surface, renders the cell's recommendation-shaped reply and its **source-typed citation chips** (the first web render of D131/D138), and accepts further turns. The web adapter is **stateless per turn** (D115): `ConversationState` threads through the client; the server holds no conversation state and adds no parallel state machine. This resolves the exact frustration the S58 view-only open named as the tiebreaker — correct view, could not continue the conversation. Four commits (charter-first); 2061 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode (0 failed; +10 conversation tests added this session); 42 import-linter contracts kept; 9 AST enforcement green.

- Produced: Four commits. (1) `docs(charter): D158 live conversational-turn-over-HTTP cell surface` (d54cae6) — D158 index + full entry, the S59 current-package sub-entry with the six reconciliation findings and the F2 persist-vs-scope decision, and the deferred-decisions "Cross-task conversational reference" entry. (2) `feat(p16/s59): http cell-turn surface wiring the Case cell + citation resolution` (710af38) — `apps/api/_conversation_cell_wiring.py` (the stateless adapter: `build_mirror_cell` mirroring `_run_mirror_conversation_cell`, `open_conversation`, `advance_conversation`, and `_resolve_citations` resolving `CellResponse` ids → `{type, label, ref}` via the same `mirror_portfolio_reader` the cell reads from), `apps/api/routers/_conversation_dto.py` (the slim client-threaded DTOs), `apps/api/routers/conversation.py` (the tenant-scoped `open`/`turn` router), and `main.py` registration. (3) `feat(p16/s59): /app live conversation drawer with citation chips` (2646a2f) — the conversation thread + composer + citation chips in `apps/api/static/daily_driver.html`, replacing the Case branch's read-only `GET /portfolio/cases/{id}`. (4) this docs commit — the procedural smoke at `docs/smoke/p16_s59_conversation_cell.md`, plus `test(p16/s59)` (3595f01, landed ahead of docs) covering the wiring + routes, this session-log entry, and the S59 close marker.

- Decisions: D158 (the open-into-cell becomes a live conversational turn over HTTP via a stateless web ConversationFlow adapter wiring the existing Case cell; first web render of D131 citation discipline). No D-entries beyond D158. One deferred-decisions entry added (Cross-task conversational reference, references D158/D17).

- Tests: 2061 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode, 0 failed (181 skipped — the standard DB-gated adapter tests in the no-docker build env). +10 this session: 6 wiring-level (`tests/unit/apps/api/test_conversation_cell.py` — open grounds + resolves citations with no raw UUID, missing-case→None, tenant_b cannot open tenant_a's case, drill-down threads via client cell_payload, no-prior-focus clarifies, ambiguous→clarification) + 4 route-level (`tests/unit/apps/api/routers/test_conversation.py` — open/turn DTO shape, 404, 422). The ConversationFlow conformance harness stays green (the cell is unchanged; the adapter is apps-layer wiring). 42 import-linter contracts kept (**no new contract** — the web adapter is the composition root, not a context). 9 AST enforcement green. The live browser verification (AC2/AC3/AC4) is **operator-gated** at `docs/smoke/p16_s59_conversation_cell.md` per the S45/S55a/S58 procedural-then-executed precedent.

- Reflection (*stateless-per-turn over HTTP, prompt 1): **Substantive — this is the load-bearing architectural call.** `ConversationState` lives in the *client* between turns. The cell's `cell_payload`/drill-down (D141) did force a persist-vs-thread decision, and I chose **thread, not persist**: the cell takes `prior_focus` at construction and emits the serialised focus in `state.payload["cell_payload"]`; the web turn DTO carries that `cell_payload` to the client, the next `turn` request returns it, and `advance_conversation` reconstructs `prior_focus` via the cell's own `extract_focus_from_cell_payload`. So drill-down/parent/siblings work **statelessly, kept in scope** — no `messages` row, no migration, no new table (F6). The messaging path persists `cell_payload` on the outbound Message because WhatsApp turns are one-shot with no client to hold state; the web client *is* that holder, so reusing the messaging message-persistence would have been a second, redundant state store. The web adapter stayed free of a parallel state machine: it constructs the existing cell and threads its existing state shape; it invents no lifecycle. The one honest nuance is that the cell's **PendingClarification** (medium-confidence + resolution-ambiguity) still persists server-side in the messaging DB — but that is the *cell's* existing user-scoped mechanism (D134, deliberately cross-channel), reused unchanged, not state the *adapter* holds. The precise claim is: the adapter holds no conversation state; the cell keeps its own clarification discipline; the drill-down focus rides the client. That division is what makes "stateless per turn" true without scoping drill-down out.

- Reflection (*citation web render — D131 first web instance, prompt 2): **Substantive.** Citation ids resolve to labels at the **adapter** layer, through the *same* `mirror_portfolio_reader` the cell already reads from, so there is no second read path and no risk of the render disagreeing with the cell: a `case` citation → `get_case_detail(...).case.title`; a `data_point` citation → `get_data_point(...)` value-text. Each becomes `{type, label, ref}` where `ref` is an 8-char short-hex, never the raw UUID — the tests assert no full UUID appears in `reply`, `label`, or `ref` (the cell_payload *does* carry the focus artefact_id, but that is an opaque client-threaded token, not surfaced). The honest gap is exactly the one D138 names: `cited_audit_events` stays **empty** for mirror (the response composes from current portfolio state, and the audit chain is reached transitively through cited IntakeRecords per D128), so the chips today are `case`/`data_point` only; the resolver carries the intake/audit branches defensively (short-hex labels) for a future implementer that populates them. The resolution shape is the **first web instance** of D131 render — it does not yet recur (WhatsApp render is channel-text, not chips), so per the captures-promotion threshold I did **not** open a candidate; if a second chip-rendering surface lands (the dashboard, a Slack card), the `{type, label, ref}` resolver-at-the-adapter shape is the thing to watch for promotion at the Phase 2-A close audit.

- Reflection (which cell answered the focus item, prompt 3): The Case **mirror-conversation cell** sufficed as-is — no cell change, no new domain code; the adapter constructs it exactly as the messaging dispatch does. The one wiring-surfaced shape: the cell's `open` returns an *empty* state (no opening message), so the web "opening turn" is a synthesised `turn` on `"show me {title}"` (title from the focus case_id via the reader). That is the cell's real resolution path (REAL_TIME_REQUIRED, D122) and grounds on the clicked Case at dogfooding scale (single-digit distinct titles); exact-id opening is a named refinement if titles collide. No Commitment-focus gap forced a new cell — a Commitment-specific cell is named out (D158) until dogfooding shows a Commitment needs conversation; the Case cell carries this cut. Carryover: none beyond that named-out item.

- Reflection (live-substrate verification, prompt 4): The fifth instance of the live-substrate lesson, and honestly **operator-gated, not executed in-build** — the build environment cannot reach docker/Caddy/a browser, and S59's whole deliverable is a browser round-trip plus a real LLM intent-extraction call. So what the sketch could not tell me, and what only the live run can, is named explicitly in the smoke (Stage 2 CLI wiring-proof + Stage 3 browser): whether the synthesised opening turn actually resolves the clicked Case (title-resolution at real scale), whether the LLM classifies follow-ups at high-enough confidence to avoid spurious clarifications, and whether the chips read as grounding rather than noise. The build-time confidence is structural (the wiring mirrors a proven dispatch; the threading is unit-tested both directions; citations resolve through the cell's own reader); the felt and live-LLM confidence is the operator's to give at Stage 3. This **does** strengthen the live-substrate-verification-gate candidate — it adds a face the S58 browser-boundary instance did not have: a surface whose correctness depends on a **live model call**, not just a UI-to-API contract, so green tests with stubbed structured-output cannot speak to whether the real classifier behaves. Recorded here (not promoted) per the candidate's pending status for the Phase 2-A close audit.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level; live browser verification (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC6-live) operator-gated** per the no-docker procedural-then-executed precedent. If the operator's Stage-3 run surfaces a gap (a sketch-built dead path, a title-resolution miss, a felt-quality issue), that is recorded as a forward correction the way the S58 open-into-cell bug was.

- Selection note (D158 correction, 2026-06-05): S59 was selected on the structural read-only dead-end (the D157 tiebreaker), not by dogfooding evidence, and lands ahead of the pending Phase 2-A week-of-use gate (D156). D158's reasoning clause was amended same-day to drop a "dogfooding confirmed the frustration" over-claim the timeline does not support (dogfood-setup provisioned and verified the personal tenant but never used the BEHIND surface; one day separated it from the S59 brief). The next move after Stage-3 is the dogfooding week, not S60 — building a third unproven surface ahead of the gate is the drift to watch.

methodology: Reconciliation-shapes-the-build held again — reading the *real* `_run_mirror_conversation_cell` (not the brief's framing) is what settled F2 cleanly: the messaging path persists `cell_payload` only because WhatsApp has no client state-holder, which is exactly the asymmetry that makes the web path's client-threading the honest minimal choice rather than a shortcut. No new methodology candidate; the live-substrate-verification-gate candidate gains a live-model-call face (above), still held for the Phase 2-A close audit.

## S60 — P16: calendar items in the Today surface + the Connections page (the dogfooding entry point)
roles: engineer, architect (the calendar consumer-port seam + the second-implementer HTTP-cell path), designer (the Today surface + Connections page to the settled design language), technical writer (the smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S60 prompt (briefs/p16/s60.md)

S60 makes the Today surface the whole-life driver D156 describes (D159): the operator's **real calendar** events render in one list alongside OPEN Cases and Commitments, typed by domain; the item drawer carries the S59 conversation cell via the **calendar-conversation implementer** over the same stateless HTTP-cell path; and an in-product **Connections page** (design-language §9) lets the operator connect Google Calendar one-tap, read-only. **This is the Phase 2-A dogfooding entry point** — the week-of-use restraint gate (D156) now runs against this surface, on real data. **The slice landed end-to-end at S60** (no S60b split); the live run (AC8) is operator-gated. Seven commits (charter-first); 2083 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode (0 failed; +22 over S59); 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — the calendar reader is a consumer-port seam); 9 AST enforcement green.

- Produced: Seven commits. (1) `docs(charter): D159 + P16/S60 marker` (7b4fd3a) — D159 index + full entry, the design-language §9 calendar-to-domain clause, the S60 current-package marker with the six Step-0 reconciliation findings corrected to reality, and the S60 brief (riding the charter-first commit, the S48b precedent). (2) `feat(p16/s60): calendar events in the Today list via a calendar consumer-port reader` (297d44a) — the `CalendarEventsReader` consumer port + `CalendarToday` projection, the `CalendarEventsReaderAdapter` composing the calendar `MeetingReader` + today-window filter (the D17 seam, mirroring `OpenCasesReader`), `build_today_view`'s calendar source + `ItemKind.CALENDAR`, the `resolve_calendar_domain` mapping + `CalendarSettings.calendar_domain_tag`. (3) `feat(p16/s60): calendar_conversation over the S59 HTTP-cell path` (4c303b6) — `build_calendar_cell` + reader-injected open/advance cores + infra wrappers in `_conversation_cell_wiring.py`, meeting-citation resolution, the router dispatch by `focus_kind`/`purpose`. (4) `feat(p16/s60): Today surface rebuilt to the design language` (c0d067b) — `daily_driver.html` rebuilt to `today-surface-mock.html` (domain surfaces, three-channel identity, status pills, legend, right-fixed drawer, theme + cue toggles, reduced-motion), the S59 conversation cell kept and extended to calendar items. (5) `feat(p16/s60): Connections page` (34f0343) — `connections.html` + the `GET /api/v1/connections` status route + `ConnectionsStatusReader` (design-language §9 + the app-shell Connected accounts view). (6) `test(p16/s60): calendar reader isolation, cell-path conformance, route tests` (d3467f8). (7) this docs commit — the smoke at `docs/smoke/p16_s60_today_calendar.md`, this session-log entry, the S60 close marker.

- Decisions: D159 (calendar-sourced items in the Today surface via a consumer-port reader; the calendar-conversation cell over the S59 HTTP-cell path; the in-product Connections page per §9; calendar-to-domain mapping as a per-tenant default fixed at connection time, per-calendar persistence deferred to the second-calendar threshold). One design-language §9 clause added (the calendar-to-domain mapping the §9 manage panel implied but did not specify). No deferred-decisions entries beyond what D159 names.

- Tests: 2083 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode, 0 failed (181 DB-gated skips, the no-docker profile, unchanged from S59). +22 this session: 13 daily-driver (the calendar-to-domain mapping; `build_today_view`'s calendar source — status, domain typing, time-ordering within band, rank between BEHIND and NEEDS_YOU; `list_today` composition with/without the reader); 7 conversation (4 wiring-core with a stub Meeting reader — opening grounds and cites by title, missing meeting → None, tenant isolation at the wiring boundary, advance answers from the store; 3 route-dispatch — CALENDAR / calendar_query routing, meeting-not-found 404); 6 apps wiring/route (calendar reader bound-tenant isolation red-team + today-window filter + domain-tag fallback; connections status DTO shape + 503). The ConversationFlow conformance harness stays green (the calendar cell is unchanged — the HTTP path is a second implementer of apps-layer wiring). 42 import-linter contracts kept (**no new contract** — the calendar reader is a consumer-port seam, not a context). 9 AST enforcement green. **AC8 (live events + a live gpt-4o-mini turn on a real event) is operator-gated** at the smoke per the S56a procedural-then-executed precedent.

- Reflection (calendar-to-domain mapping, prompt 1): The build settled the mapping as a **per-tenant default tag resolved at the read seam** (`CalendarSettings.calendar_domain_tag`, default `work`), surfaced read-only in the Connections manage panel; events inherit it via `resolve_calendar_domain`, which falls back to `work` for an unset or unknown tag so a calendar always types its events. **§9 needed a clause and got one** — the manage panel offered Work/Personal/Family and the Today mock typed items by domain, but §9 never said the calendar *holds* the tag and the events *inherit* it; that is now stated, with the explicit two-threshold note that per-calendar persisted tags and their management UI arrive when a second calendar with a distinct domain connects. The honest limitation this exposes: at single-personal-calendar scale **every calendar event gets one domain**, so the domain-typing the mock illustrates with a mixed work/personal/family day collapses to one surface colour on real single-calendar data — which is precisely what reflection 3 has to weigh.

- Reflection (reconciliation outcome, prompt 2): **The today-scoped calendar reader did not exist** — `contexts/calendar` had `MeetingReader.list_meetings` (newest-start, all) and `get_by_event_id`, no today filter — so I built the today-window filter in the daily-driver consumer-port adapter (composing `list_meetings`), not as a new calendar-context query method, keeping the D17 seam the single cross-context mechanism. **Extending the HTTP-cell path to `calendar_conversation` stayed a second-implementer change, not a parallel path**: the existing `OpenConversationRequest.focus_kind` already carried a discriminator (the router 422'd non-CASE), so the change was a `build_calendar_cell` + a `CALENDAR` open branch + a `meeting` citation resolver + dispatch by the client-threaded `purpose` — the calendar cell reuses the same `ConversationState`/`PendingClarification` mechanics, and the adapter holds no conversation state. One refactor the reconciliation forced for testability: the mirror path is unit-testable because its reader is injected via `MessagingComposition`, but the calendar cell's Meeting reader + refresh are built from per-tenant infrastructure — so I split each calendar open/advance into a **reader-injected core** (unit-tested with a stub Meeting reader) and a thin **infra wrapper** (exercised at the live smoke). One **forward finding worth naming**: the Today list reads the **cached** meeting store (the `CalendarEventsReader` does not refresh on list), unlike the calendar-conversation cell which refreshes-before-answer (D150); the store is seeded by the conversation refresh / threshold evaluator, and a refresh-on-list is a deferred refinement recorded in the smoke — if the dogfooding week shows the morning list reads stale, that is the first correction.

- Reflection (felt-quality on real data, prompt 3): **Operator-gated, so the honest first read is recorded at the live run, not asserted here** — the build environment has no calendar, no browser, no live model. What I can say structurally: the surface genuinely composes three sources into one domain-typed list with a conversational drawer on calendar items, which is the mechanism D156 calls for. What I *cannot* yet know, and what the live run must answer, is the felt question — and the build already surfaces the specific risk that makes it live-or-nothing: with a single connected calendar, **every event inherits one domain**, so the three-channel domain-typing that makes the mock read as "whole life at a glance" may, on real single-calendar data, read as a single-colour calendar agenda with Cases and Commitments stapled on — i.e. exactly "a calendar clone with extra rows." Whether the *active-surfacing* difference (the BEHIND commitment leading, the calendar events time-anchored beneath it, the at-risk Case needing you) reads as a driver rather than an agenda is the thing the operator feels in the first morning and not before. Recorded as pending the Stage-4 read; a gap there is a forward correction in the S58/S59 shape.

- Reflection (dogfooding entry point, prompt 4): **The week-of-use restraint gate (D156) now runs against this surface** — S60 is the artefact the gate has been waiting for, and the standing project note is updated to say so (S60 is the sanctioned entry point, not drift; the drift to watch has moved downstream to any *further* surface — S61 email-into-list, the week matrix, the dashboard, the journal, the Map/Flow views — drafted before the week returns a verdict). For calendar items specifically, "keeps earning its place" looks like: the morning list surfaces the meeting the operator would otherwise have missed or under-prepared for, and opening it into the cell to ask "what's the last thing we agreed" or "who's coming" earns the conversational drawer; "curdles into guilt" looks like the list filling with every recurring standup and personal block as undifferentiated rows the operator learns to scroll past — the reverse-Kano failure the threshold-briefing restraint (the S57 candidate) already named for proactive surfaces, here applied to a passive list that can still bury signal in volume. **Nothing in this slice pre-empts that verdict**: the mapping is deliberately minimal (one tag, no per-calendar machinery), email/Drive are connectable but not list-wired (so the list does not pre-fill with a second noisy source before calendar proves out), calendar items are read-through (no reorder/done semantics invented before use shows the need), and the refresh-on-list question is left open rather than answered by guess. The slice ships the minimum that makes a genuine week-of-use test possible, and leaves every expansion to what that week shows.

methodology: Reconciliation-shapes-the-build held a third consecutive session — the today-scoped reader's absence (F1) and the cell-path's existing `focus_kind` discriminator (F3) were both settled by reading the real code, not the brief's framing, and the testability refactor (reader-injected core vs infra wrapper) came directly from noticing the mirror path's reader is injected while the calendar path's is built. No new methodology candidate; the live-substrate-verification-gate candidate gains a third UI face (the Today surface's domain-typing felt-quality, AC3/reflection 3, only verifiable in a real browser on real single-calendar data), still held for the Phase 2-A close audit.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level; AC8 (live calendar events + a live gpt-4o-mini conversation turn on a real event) and the felt-quality read (reflection 3) operator-gated** per the no-docker procedural-then-executed precedent. The slice landed end-to-end at S60 — no S60b split. The next move is the **dogfooding week** against this surface, not a further surface.

(2) `feat(p16/s60b): real platform sign-in over a token-exchange seam` (ede60fd) — `LoginVerifier` port, `DevPassphraseLoginVerifier` (wired), `GoogleLoginVerifier` (operator-gated), `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `login.html`, the `/`+`/login`+`/api/v1/auth/login` public-path additions, +8 tests. (3) `feat(p16/s60b): app shell as the navigation frame` (b0f5434) — `daily_driver.html` rebuilt into the shell (rail + main + Today live inside + honest placeholders), login-gated. (4) `feat(p16/s60b): live calendar connect` (b91d115) — `CalendarConnectInitiator` port + `NangoCalendarConnectInitiator` (operator-gated) + `ConnectionStore` (callback writer, reuses `save_connection`, injectable first-sync), the initiate/callback routes, the Connections-page connect flow. (5) `test(p16/s60b): connect-callback + per-tenant connection isolation` (0371421) — red-team isolation on the stored connection + initiator gating + connect routes. (6) this docs commit — the smoke at `docs/smoke/p16_s60b_live_connect.md`, this entry, the close marker.

- Decisions: D160 (the live e2e loop — login token-exchange seam, the app shell, the connect-initiator port; closes the paste-token UX backdoor; vendor adapters operator-gated). No deferred-decisions entries.

- Tests: 2101 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode, 0 failed (181 DB-gated skips, unchanged). +18 this session: 8 auth (dev verifier accept/reject/tenant-override, Google operator-gated, backend selection; the login route issues a verifiable tenant-scoped token, 401, 503) + 8 connect (ConnectionStore bound-tenant red-team — stores the actor's tenant, two tenants each their own, first-sync failure does not lose the connection, missing ref raises; initiator gated/wired) + the connect-route tests (initiate 503/200, callback stores + reports sync). 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — the seams are apps-layer composition). 9 AST enforcement green. **AC7 (sign in, connect a real calendar, see live events, move/cancel a meeting and confirm the surface reflects it) is operator-gated** at the smoke.

- Reflection (reconciliation outcome, prompt 1): The Connect button was **display-only** (S60 — it toasted "connect via the Nango flow"); there was **no initiate route and no callback**. The auth path was **bearer-JWT only** (`issue_dev_token` HS256, CLI-minted; `verify_credential` decodes), with the middleware exempting only page bytes — **no OAuth login, no session, no login endpoint**, and the production Keycloak backend a **stub that raises** (D3/D23, never landed). tenant_a was connected at S56a via the **Nango self-hosted runbook** (OAuth in Nango's own flow) + a `save_connection` write — there is **no in-app connect-session code**. So Step 0 corrected the brief's central assumption ("wire the login surface to the existing auth machinery; wire Connect through the existing Nango integration"): the machinery for both is net-new, not present. `login-mock.html` mapped to nothing built. The reusable piece is the per-tenant `save_connection` write seam and `build_calendar_refresh_adapter` for the first pull; the Google OAuth client + Nango integration are app-level (reusable) but the **connect-session API** is a vendor contract to reconcile live.

- Reflection (the auth-exempt-to-real transition, prompt 2): What **closed** is the *UX* backdoor — the daily-driver page no longer prompts "paste a dev token"; it reads the JWT the login flow set in `localStorage` and redirects to `/login` when absent, and a 401 on any fetch clears the token and bounces to login. What **stays exempt** is exactly what must: the **page bytes** (`/`, `/login`, `/app`, `/connections` — a browser GET carries no bearer) and the **act of logging in** (`POST /api/v1/auth/login` — you cannot bearer-auth the request that issues the bearer). The **data routes stay bearer-authed throughout** — S60b did not loosen any data-route auth; it added a real way to *obtain* the token rather than minting it at the CLI and pasting it. The honest residue: the dev login is a passphrase, not Google sign-in; the real §9 one-tap is operator-gated (the `GoogleLoginVerifier` raises until its verifier + email→tenant resolver are wired), and production auth remains the D3/D23 Keycloak swap — S60b added a dev-mode login seam, not a new production backend.

- Reflection (e2e felt-quality on real data, prompt 3): **Operator-gated, so the honest first read is recorded at the live run.** What is structurally true: the loop is now sign-in → shell → Today-on-live-data → conversational drawer, with the unbuilt surfaces present as honest placeholders rather than absent — which is the difference between "a demo of one screen" and "a product with a frame." What only the live sitting can tell, and what the smoke asks for: whether signing in and connecting *your own* calendar reads as a product you would live in or as a demo wearing a shell. The specific risk this session's honesty surfaces: the two most "product-defining" moments — the Google one-tap and the in-app one-tap connect — are the two that are operator-gated, so the *first* live pass runs on a passphrase login and a runbook-assisted connect; the connect-session and Google adapters must be wired before the loop feels like the §9 one-tap it is designed to be. The felt verdict is the operator's at the live run; a gap is a forward correction in the S58/S59 shape.

- Reflection (the temporal verdict, prompt 4): **A fast positive is a green light to keep going, not the restraint verdict — and these are different in kind.** The whole-life read and the connect experience assess in a sitting: does the day cohere, does sign-in-and-connect feel like a product. The reverse-Kano restraint verdict — does the morning surface *keep earning its place across a week*, or curdle into guilt — is temporal and cannot be read on day one. A surface that delights on day one can be dead by day five: the calendar that felt like the whole-life driver on Monday is the source of guilt by Thursday if every recurring standup and personal block piles in undifferentiated and the operator learns to scroll past. So the day-one read S60b enables is necessary (a loop that fails the sitting never survives the week) but not sufficient (a loop that passes the sitting still has to earn the week). The explicit statement the brief asks for: **record the day-one read as a green-light-to-continue, never as the close gate; only elapsed days settle whether the surface keeps earning its place.** Nothing in S60b pre-empts that — every unbuilt surface stays a placeholder, defaulted out, built in the order the week informs, not before.

methodology: Step-0 reconciliation was the session's highest-leverage act — it turned a brief that read as "wiring" into an honest "net-new across vendor contracts" and, rather than overrunning silently (the brief's named failure mode) or fabricating vendor adapters (the S4/S55a-fix anti-pattern), the build shipped the seams with vendor adapters operator-gated. This is a **second instance** of the live-substrate-verification-gate's "don't assert vendor contracts from memory" applied *preemptively at design time* rather than caught at the smoke (S55a-fix was the reactive instance) — a candidate facet worth the Phase 2-A close audit: the gate is not only "verify against the live service" but "when you cannot, ship the seam operator-gated rather than the fabricated adapter." Held, not promoted.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level; the live e2e run (AC7) operator-gated**, with the Google-login and Nango-connect-initiate vendor adapters operator-gated by construction (reconcile-at-smoke). The loop landed end-to-end; no further split. The next move is the **dogfooding week** against this live loop, then the restraint verdict — not a further surface.
