## S60c — P16: real Google OIDC login wired behind the LoginVerifier port (the dogfooding-login unblock; identity foundation activated)
roles: engineer, architect (the credential-reshape reconciliation + the OIDC adapter behind the existing port), technical writer (the operator smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S60c prompt (briefs/p16/s60c.md)

S60c completes the S60b sign-in seam to a real Google provider (D161): the `GoogleLoginVerifier` raise becomes a live Google **OpenID Connect** login, the operator's `operator@example.com` resolves to the personal tenant, and the callback mints the JWT the data routes already require. **Gate-enabling, not a new value surface** — it is the dogfooding-login unblock and the first real provider of the deferred identity foundation, which D161 activates (lifting D52). **Step 0 was again the decisive deliverable**: it corrected the S60b seam's hidden assumption that the `credential` is a client-obtained Google ID token (one-tap/GIS). The operator's actual setup — an OAuth client with a redirect URI — is a server-side authorization-code flow, so the reconciliation reshaped the credential (`verify(credential=<authorization code>)`) and reused the port unchanged rather than building a parallel path. PyJWT (already pinned) does the ID-token verification, httpx (already pinned) the code exchange + JWKS fetch — no new dependency, no vendor SDK, an OIDC-generic adapter whose Google endpoints are config. Three commits after the charter-first: 2278 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode (+34 S60c tests); 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — the OIDC adapter is apps-layer composition); 9 AST enforcement green. **The flow is real and tested; the live sign-in (AC6) is operator-gated** behind the operator's OAuth-client pre-flight, reconciling Google's live token contract at the smoke (the S4/S55a-fix discipline).

- Produced: Four commits. (1) `docs(charter): D161 + P16/S60c marker` (99fa754) — D161 index + full entry, the D52 index annotation (identity-foundation-deferral clause lifted), the S60c marker with the Step 0 findings, the brief preserved at `briefs/p16/s60c.md`. (2) `feat(p16/s60c): GoogleLoginVerifier + initiate/callback routes + operator-email-to-tenant resolver` (4c8b455) — `GoogleOAuthSettings`; `GoogleOidcClient` (`authorization_url`, signed-state issue/verify, code exchange + ID-token verification via PyJWT against Google's JWKS); the reshaped `GoogleLoginVerifier` + `OperatorEmailTenantResolver`; the `GET /api/v1/auth/google/initiate` + `/callback` routes (callback ends in an HTML bridge writing the same `dd_token`); the two public-path additions; the main.py wiring; the login-page button. (3) `test(p16/s60c): verifier with mocked Google tokens, email-to-tenant resolution, callback route, isolation` (5bff5cd) — 34 tests, Google calls mocked via httpx.MockTransport. (4) this docs commit — the smoke at `docs/smoke/p16_s60c_google_login.md`, this entry, the close marker, the captures note.

- Decisions: D161 (Google OIDC as the first real identity provider behind the `LoginVerifier` port; lifts D52's identity-foundation deferral; Google first, Apple/Entra parallel follow-ons; login carries identity scopes only, data stays on the Nango path; connector breadth stays gated behind the restraint verdict). Kano: must-have. No deferred-decisions entries.

- Tests: 2278 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode; +34 this session — 24 OIDC-adapter (valid/expired/wrong-audience/unverified-email/issuer-mismatch ID tokens; token-endpoint rejection; missing id_token; operator-gated unconfigured client; authorization_url params; state round-trip + tamper/empty reject; build_google_oidc None-until-configured; resolver mapped-case-insensitive/unmapped→None; verifier code→scoped-identity/unmapped-reject/operator-gated) + 10 route (initiate redirects to Google; callback happy path mints a tenant-scoped session that verifies through the same backend; bad-state and oauth-error rejected without minting; unmapped email rejected without minting; per-tenant isolation across two emails→two tenants; initiate/callback 503 when operator-gated). 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract). 9 AST enforcement green. **One pre-existing failure unrelated to S60c** (`test_advance_calendar_turn_answers_from_the_store`, a wall-clock-coupled calendar-cell test that broke at the 2026-06-06 midnight rollover; reproduces on a clean tree with S60c stashed; logged at `log/captures.md` [S60c]) — **S60c adds 0 new failures.** **AC6 (live sign-in with `operator@example.com`, past the unverified-app warning, into the app shell as the personal tenant) is operator-gated** at the smoke.

- Reflection 1 — Reconciliation outcome. Google did **not** fit the S60b seam's assumed method. The seam assumed `verify(credential)` receives a Google **ID token** the client already obtained (the one-tap/GIS model, delegating to an injected one-line callback). The operator's OAuth-client-plus-redirect-URI setup is a **server-side authorization-code flow**: the credential the callback holds is an authorization **code**, not an ID token. Step 0 corrected this by *reshaping the credential, not the port* — `verify(credential=<code>)`, with `GoogleLoginVerifier` reshaped into the real OIDC adapter that exchanges the code and verifies the ID token internally. The port method signature is unchanged; the initiate/callback routes are thin HTTP wrappers; there is no second auth path. A second correction Step 0 surfaced: the callback is a browser redirect and cannot return JSON for the page JS to store, so it ends in an HTML **bridge page** that writes the same `dd_token` localStorage key the passphrase path uses — making the Google-minted session byte-identical to the passphrase-minted one at the bearer-authed data routes (no cookie infra, no middleware change). The S60b seam's `GoogleIdTokenVerifier` callback type was the obsolete residue of the old assumption and was removed.

- Reflection 2 — The identity-foundation activation. D161 **lifts D52's deferral** and commits exactly one thing: **Google OIDC login, behind the `LoginVerifier` port**, for the dogfooding stack. What stays deferred or parallel, so the next session does not treat the Google wiring as the whole foundation: **Apple sign-in, Microsoft Entra, SCIM provisioning, and enterprise SSO** are the parallel identity package, framed separately; the **production IdP** path is unchanged (D3/D23's Keycloak swap — Google here is the dogfooding-stack login adapter, not the production identity provider); **browser-session-bound OAuth state** (full CSRF binding) defers to the multi-user package — at single-operator allowlisted scale the email→tenant allowlist is the binding gate, an attacker's code resolves to an unmapped email and is rejected. The OIDC adapter is deliberately **provider-generic** (Google's endpoints are config), so Apple/Entra are a config + endpoint change against the same adapter shape, not a second SDK — that is the seed the activation plants.

- Reflection 3 — Login-versus-data separation. The login carries **identity scopes only** — `openid email profile` (set in `authorization_url`); it requests no `calendar.readonly`, no `gmail.readonly`, no Drive scope. Calendar and mail **data** remain entirely on the separate Nango path (D148): a different connector, a different consent, a different store. **The login working is not the same as the data flowing.** After S60c the operator can sign in as `operator@example.com` and land in the app shell as the personal tenant, but the **dogfooding Today surface is still empty of calendar events** until the operator-gated Nango connect (S60b's `CalendarConnectInitiator`, still reconcile-at-smoke) runs. Authenticating the user and connecting the user's data are two independent operator-gated steps; S60c closes only the first.

methodology: Step-0 reconciliation delivered its value at a **different layer** than S60b's. S60b's Step 0 corrected an *as-built* assumption (no OAuth login exists). S60c's Step 0 corrected a *seam-shape* assumption inside code the previous session itself built — the S60b seam encoded "the credential is an ID token," and only reading it against the operator's actual OAuth-client setup surfaced that the real flow is a code exchange. The lesson: a seam shipped operator-gated still carries an unverified shape assumption, and the session that activates it must reconcile the *seam's* assumption, not just the codebase's — pre-write reconciliation applies to one's own prior seams, not only to foreign code. Held as a facet of the live-substrate-verification-gate candidate (the seam's vendor-contract shape is itself a live-substrate assumption), not promoted on a single instance.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level; the live sign-in (AC6) operator-gated** by construction (Google's token contract reconciled at the smoke, the operator's OAuth-client pre-flight required). The identity foundation is activated (Google, behind the port); Apple/Entra/SCIM/SSO stay parallel. **The login working is not the data flowing** — Today stays empty until the Nango connect runs. The next move is unchanged: the **dogfooding week**, then the restraint verdict — not a further surface.

## S61 — P16: minimal expected-versus-observed loop on the Commitment primitive (the last pre-week build)
roles: engineer, architect (the record-vs-log placement call + the drop-candidate seam in build_today_view), PM (the minimal-vs-deferred line; the reverse-Kano friction judgement), technical writer (the smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S61 prompt (the brief in-context)

S61 builds the minimal expected-versus-observed loop per D162: the Commitment record gains a free-text **expected outcome** captured forward at creation, a free-text **observed outcome** + a coarse `outcome_status` (met/partial/missed/changed/dropped) captured after, the **gap** rendered side by side in the item drawer (a view-time comparison, not LLM-computed), and a **drop-candidate recommendation** (open + no progress in N days, a nudge, never an auto-drop). The differentiated value of the daily driver is the platform's observability-and-optimisation thesis turned on the operator — capture what was expected, observe what transpired, see the gap, act — and a tick collapses that to a binary; S61 is the minimal version of the real loop so the dogfooding week tests the thesis rather than tick-adequacy. **This is the last pre-week build — after S61 building stops and the dogfooding week starts.** Four commits after the charter-first: 2322 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode (+27 S61 tests; **0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock-coupled calendar test, `log/captures.md` [S60c]); 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — a daily_driver extension); 9 AST enforcement green. **AC8 (the live loop: capture an expectation, record what transpired, see the gap, get a drop nudge on a stale item) is operator-gated** at `docs/smoke/p16_s61_expected_observed.md` per the no-docker procedural-then-executed precedent.

- Produced: Five commits. (1) `docs(charter): D162 + P16/S61 marker` (57a8675) — D162 index + full entry, the S61 marker with the Step 0 findings. (2) `feat(p16/s61): expected and observed outcomes on the Commitment record` (0042931) — `OutcomeStatus` enum + four optional fields on `Commitment` (with the observed-requires-status invariant); migration 0029_commitment_outcome (ALTER `commitments`, +4 nullable columns + the status check); the `_tables.py` columns; the repository row-mapping + `expected_outcome` insert + the bound-tenant `record_observed_outcome` UPDATE…RETURNING; `create_commitment` accepts the expectation; the `record_observed_outcome` use case; the `DAILY_DRIVER_COMMITMENT_OBSERVE` permission; schema.md in the same commit. (3) `feat(p16/s61): gap view and drop-candidate recommendation` (ac006c2) — `is_drop_candidate`/`quiet_for_days` in staleness; the `TodayItem` outcome fields + `drop_candidate`; `_commitment_item` populating them + computing drop-candidacy off the derived `last_progress_at`; the `build_today_view` + `list_today` threading; `DailyDriverSettings.drop_candidate_quiet_days` (default 21); the DTO + `record-observed-outcome` route; the main.py config wiring; the surface (create-form expected field, drawer expected/observed gap grid + record form, the row + drawer drop nudge). (4) `test(p16/s61): outcome fields, status transitions, drop-candidate query, isolation` (9b000b1) — +27 tests across domain/staleness/view-builder/application/router/isolation, plus the two operator-permission-set tests updated for the new permission. (5) this docs commit — the smoke, this entry, the close marker.

- Decisions: D162 (the expected-versus-observed loop as a relational record now; graph causal edges + traversal, the LLM-computed gap, and the longitudinal optimisation named and deferred together behind the dogfooding verdict plus a gap-analysis eval substrate; expectations/observations free text; the drop candidate a relational query surfaced as a recommendation, never auto-deleted). Kano: performance. No deferred-decisions entries (the deferred layer is named inside D162).

- Tests: 2322 unit+contract pass from cleared bytecode (12 skipped); +27 this session — 5 domain (outcome defaults; expected captured; observed-requires-status; observed-with-status; status-without-text-allowed-for-drop), 2 staleness (quiet-for-days; drop-candidate inclusive boundary just-inside/just-outside N), 7 view-builder (outcome fields surfaced; flagged past N; not flagged when N unset; not flagged within N; recent observation resets the quiet window; dropped excluded; done excluded), 6 application (create captures expectation; record sets status + returns updated; record requires auth; record unknown→None; list flags quiet; dropping clears the flag), 6 router (create-with-expected round-trips; observed-outcome route; unknown→404; unknown status→422; today flags drop when configured; no flag when threshold unset), 1 isolation (observed-outcome write rejects cross-tenant). 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract). 9 AST enforcement green. **One pre-existing failure** (`test_advance_calendar_turn_answers_from_the_store`, the wall-clock-coupled calendar-cell test, `log/captures.md` [S60c]) — **S61 adds 0 new failures.** **AC8 (the live loop) is operator-gated** at the smoke.

- Reflection 1 — Reconciliation outcome. Step 0 made the load-bearing call that the observed outcome **extends the Commitment record, not the completion log**. The completion log (`commitment_completions`) is the cadence-tick history that clears render-time staleness; the expected/observed pair is about the commitment as a whole (one expectation, one observation, one status), orthogonal to the tick history — so it is record-level state (four columns on `commitments`), exactly as D162 framed it, and not a per-completion field. The second Step 0 correction: `last_progress_at` is **derived, not stored** — `list_with_activity` already yields `MAX(completed_at)` and `build_today_view` already derives a last-activity, so the only genuinely new progress signal is the observation, captured as one `observed_at` column; the drop-candidate progress signal is `max(created_at, last_completed_at, observed_at)`, composed at render. What this corrected about the surface: COMMITMENT is **not** a conversational focus (only CASE/CALENDAR open the cell), so the gap and the observed-capture land in the drawer's existing non-conversational COMMITMENT branch, not a new cell path.

- Reflection 2 — The minimal-versus-deferred line. Confirmed **not built**: the graph causal edges and traversal (why the gap happened, what it cascades to), the LLM-computed gap and longitudinal pattern detection, and the longitudinal recommendation-shaped optimisation. D162 names all three deferred **together** (edges without the traversal that reads them is premature substrate; LLM gap judgments need an eval floor) behind one activation trigger: the Phase 2-A dogfooding verdict **plus** a gap-analysis evaluation substrate (the D137 component-quality discipline — an LLM-derived gap judgment cannot ship untrusted). The gap at S61 is a **view-time comparison of two free-text fields**, nothing more. Stated plainly so the next session does not treat the relational loop as the whole thesis: S61 is the substrate the causal/optimisation layer will later read, not that layer.

- Reflection 3 — The friction test (the reverse-Kano question, now built). Capturing an expected outcome at creation is **structurally near-frictionless**: it is one optional free-text input on the existing New-commitment form ("What do you expect to come of it?"), and a commitment created without it is fully valid — the field never blocks the create. That was the deliberate design answer to the reverse-Kano risk the prior conversation surfaced: a heavy, mandatory, structured expected-capture would produce sparse pairs and a false-negative week (the operator stops creating commitments, or leaves the field empty, and the loop has nothing to compare). Free text + optional is the lightest honest form. But the *felt* friction — whether the prompt reads as a natural "what's this for?" moment or as an extra hoop that makes the operator hesitate — is exactly what the live smoke and the dogfooding week must judge, because structure cannot prove it. The honest risk that remains: optionality protects the create flow but does not guarantee the field gets filled, and an empty expected side makes the gap view degenerate (Observed against "none captured"). If the week shows expectations rarely captured, the loop is technically present but practically empty, and the response is a lighter prompt or a better moment to ask — **not** a mandatory field, which would trade the empty-pair failure for the abandoned-create failure. The reverse-Kano category governs the *capture* surface the way it governs the proactive-briefing surface ([S57] candidate): the lightest path that still yields a signal wins.

- Reflection 4 — The last-build line. **S61 is the last pre-week build. The dogfooding week starts next, on what S58→S61 produced — not a further surface.** The specific builds that will be tempting and must be resisted until the restraint verdict: (a) the **optimisation layer** — turning the gap pairs into longitudinal patterns and recommendation-shaped adjustments, which is the obvious "next" and is precisely what the week is meant to earn the right to build, gated on a gap-analysis eval substrate; (b) the **graph causal view** — wiring expectation→outcome edges into Neo4j and traversing them for cause/cascade, premature without the traversal that reads them; (c) **more connectors** — email-in-list, the to-do-app connector, any data-connector breadth, all explicitly behind the verdict (D156). The discipline the week tests is restraint: the morning surface must keep earning its place across a week of real use (does the gap view and the drop nudge stay useful, or curdle into noise/guilt) before any of (a)–(c) is justified. The dogfooding entry point has been live since S60; S61 makes the loop the week tests the *real* loop. Building more before the verdict is the drift to watch.

methodology: the reverse-Kano discipline that [S57] surfaced for *proactive* surfaces (signal-to-noise is the product; restraint over coverage) recurred here on a *capture* surface — the expected-outcome field — in a new form: the lightest capture that still yields a usable pair beats a richer mandatory one, because heavy capture fails by producing sparse/empty pairs rather than by interrupting. This is a second instance of "the reverse category governs the surface design," now on input rather than output; noted as a possible widening of the held [S57] candidate (from proactive-output surfaces to any surface where over-asking degrades the signal), not promoted on this instance.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level; the live loop (AC8) operator-gated** by construction (no-docker build env; the browser-boundary verification is the success criterion per the S58 lesson). No new context boundary, no new import-linter contract, no audit path added (the daily_driver context's S58 no-audit posture is matched). **S61 is the last pre-week build** — the next move is the **dogfooding week**, then the restraint verdict; the optimisation layer, the graph causal view, and connector breadth stay deferred behind it (D162, D156).

## S62 — P16: the goal taxonomy to charter + German as the first end-to-end causal goal (D163)
roles: architect (the typed graph capability vs Entity/Relationship call; the Lever-reference-node seam; the consumer-port + apps-bridge placement), analyst (the three-axis taxonomy formalisation), engineer (the wrapper Cypher, the read path, the surface), PM (the instance-one-shape-only restraint), technical writer (D163, the methodology section, the smoke)
mode: build session, executing the S62 prompt (the brief in-context)

S62 lands the whole-life goal taxonomy in the charter (D163: three axes — engine, target, control; three core shapes; two boundaries; one variant; one higher layer; three mechanics) and instances **German** as the first end-to-end causal goal — mode progressive, control self, subject self, with a CEFR level ladder toward fluency and a current target one level above where the operator sits (A2 → B1), its German-practice commitment connected as the lever. The daily driver shows, for German, the current target, the commitment-sourced progress, the qualitative gap, and a raise-or-hold recommendation; the target changes only on an explicit raise action, never automatically (D9). Every other mode, the control-and-influence semantics, the avoidance variant, the balance layer, and the exploratory phase are schema-present and uninstanced. Four commits after the charter-first: 2354 unit+contract pass (+~41 S62 tests; **0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock-coupled calendar test, `log/captures.md` [S60c], carried forward); 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — the daily-driver consumer-port + apps-bridge seam reuses D17); 9 AST enforcement green, including the neo4j-confined fence over the new goal-graph Cypher. **AC7/AC8 (German seeded in the live personal tenant + the browser surface) are operator-gated** at `docs/smoke/p16_s62_german_goal.md` (the build env cannot reach Postgres/Neo4j — the procedural-then-executed precedent).

- Step 0 reconciliation (recorded; where it differed from the prompt): **F1** — the "existing graph interface" is `GraphRepositoryPort` + the `TenantScopedNeo4jSession` wrapper (the single Cypher surface, fenced by the `neo4j-confined` contract **and** the AST test; Neo4j 5 Community, no APOC). The prompt's "behind the existing graph interface" needed a correction: the existing `Entity`/`Relationship` value objects **cannot** carry the lever edge's `mode` + ladder + current target (a `Relationship` holds only `relationship_type` + `source_chunk_id`; an `Entity` is keyed by `source_chunk_ids` a goal lacks), so the Outcome node + lever edge are a **new typed capability on the same wrapper**, not a reuse. **F2** — daily_driver may import neither neo4j nor ingestion, so it consumes the graph through a daily-driver `GoalGraphPort` + an apps-composition-root bridge to ingestion's new `OutcomeGraphPort` (the calendar/email `MeetingGraphIndexBridge` precedent). **F3** — commitments live **only in Postgres** (no graph node through S61); the lever-to-outcome edge attaches by reference via a thin `:Lever {commitment_id}` node, not a copy of the row. **F4** — no German commitment existed; seeded minimally. **F5** — the goal is a graph node and the lever reuses the `commitments` table, so **no Alembic migration**; the graph schema landed as `migrations/neo4j/0002_outcome_goal.cypher` via `ops/migrate_neo4j`. **F6/F7** — tenant+jurisdiction on every node/edge (D12/D63); D163 and S62 confirmed free.

- Produced: Five commits. (1) `docs(charter): add goal taxonomy (D163) and P16 goal layer` (1ff3734) — D163 index + full entry, the product-methodology goal-taxonomy section mirroring D163, the current-package goal-layer edit + Step 0 findings; deferred-decisions confirmed unchanged (quantitative inference + companion/health encryption posture stay deferred per D156). (2) `feat(graph): add Outcome node and lever-to-outcome edge with mode and qualitative target` (f1d69fc) — ingestion `OutcomeGraphPort` + `OutcomeGraphRecord`; wrapper Cypher + methods (`merge_outcome`, `merge_lever_for_outcome`, `set_lever_target`, `list_outcomes`); `Neo4jGraphRepository` implementing them; daily-driver `Goal` domain (`GoalMode`/`ControlAxis`/`Subject` enums, `LevelLadder`, `Goal`) + `GoalGraphPort`; `migrations/neo4j/0002_outcome_goal.cypher`; schema.md in the same commit. (3) `feat(daily-driver): seed German as the first progressive-cadence goal` (d8cc872) — `ops/seed_german_goal.py` (idempotent: the German-practice commitment in Postgres + the Outcome node + lever edge in the graph) + the `make seed-german` target. (4) `feat(daily-driver): surface target, progress, gap and a raise-or-hold recommendation for German` (d48ecf3) — `build_goal_reading` (pure); `list_goals` + `raise_goal_target` use cases; `DAILY_DRIVER_GOAL_READ`/`DAILY_DRIVER_GOAL_RAISE_TARGET` permissions; the apps `GoalGraphAdapter` bridge + `build_goal_graph`; `GET /goals` + `POST /goals/{id}/raise-target`; `GoalReadingDTO`; the `/app` Goals panel; main.py wiring; the smoke; tests. (5) this docs commit — this entry + close marker.

- Decisions: D163 (the whole-life goal taxonomy). Kano: performance. No deferred-decisions entries added (the uninstanced values are named-and-deferred inside D163; D156's quantitative-inference and companion/health deferrals confirmed untouched).

- Tests: 2354 unit+contract pass (12 skipped; 1 deselected — the pre-existing wall-clock calendar test). +~41 this session: 6 goal domain (ladder next/at-top/validation, progressive-requires-ladder, German constructable), 5 wrapper goal-graph (merge_outcome binds tenant, lever edge carries mode+ladder, set_lever_target returns/None, list_outcomes maps records), 7 goal_view (raise on on-track+met; hold when behind / not-met / not-yet-observed / at-top / missing-lever; non-progressive not read), 8 application+bridge (list_goals join+raise, auth boundary on both, raise one-level / at-top noop / unknown noop, bridge record→Goal mapping + raise delegation), 3 routes (/goals reading, raise-target one level, at-top 409), plus the two operator-permission-set tests updated for the new permissions. 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract); 9 AST enforcement green (neo4j confined over the new Cypher). **AC10:** the wall-clock-coupled calendar test (`test_advance_calendar_turn_answers_from_the_store`) is **carried forward red**, unchanged by S62; the clock-seam fix is named as its own small slice (out of scope, `log/captures.md` [S60c]).

- Acceptance criteria: AC1 charter commit precedes all code (✓, 1ff3734 first); AC2 product-methodology section consistent with D163 (✓); AC3 current-package goal layer (✓); AC4 Outcome node + lever edge, `mode` ∈ {homeostatic, progressive, sequence}, progressive carries ladder + current target (✓); AC5 tenant+jurisdiction on every node/edge (✓); AC6 no raw neo4j call outside the wrapper — AST + import-linter green (✓); AC7 German one Outcome node, progressive/self/self, ladder, connected to a German-practice commitment lever (✓ at the seed; live-apply operator-gated); AC8 surface shows target/progress/gap/raise-or-hold, target unchanged without explicit action (✓ code+test; browser operator-gated); AC9 no homeostatic/sequence/influence/avoidance/balance/exploratory behaviour wired — values schema-present only (✓); AC10 the calendar test carried forward red, clock-seam fix named (✓); AC11 this entry records Step 0 + the reflections (✓).

- Reflection 1 — Did a field resist? Yes: **`current_target_level` strained against living on the edge.** The brief put `mode` and the target on the lever-to-outcome edge, and `mode` sits there cleanly (it genuinely describes how the lever relates to the outcome). But the current target is the *goal's* present aim, a property of the Outcome, not of the lever relationship — at single-lever scale edge-placement is harmless, but the field "wanted to be" on the Outcome node, and if a goal ever had two levers the target would be duplicated or ambiguous across edges. I followed the brief (target on the edge) and noted the strain rather than silently relocating it. A second, milder strain: the **control axis** carries `SELF`/`OTHER` values to match the brief's "control self," but the axis is really *determine* vs *influence*; SELF/OTHER reads cleanly for the instanced case yet slightly conflates with the subject axis's own SELF/OTHER. Docstrings carry the mapping (control-SELF = the actor's levers determine); the influence-goal session is where that naming will be tested for real.

- Reflection 2 — Is the split clean? Mostly, with one honest seam. Commitment stays in Postgres as the lever, the Outcome is a graph node, and an edge connects them — as intended. The strain is that the edge cannot be a pure graph edge between two graph nodes, because the commitment has **no** graph node (F3). So the "lever-to-outcome edge" became a three-element path — a thin `:Lever {commitment_id}` reference node, a `LEVER_FOR` edge, the `:Outcome` — plus a Postgres join in the read path keyed on the same `commitment_id` (the daily-driver use case zips `GoalGraphPort.list_goals` against `CommitmentRepository.list_with_activity`). That means "this commitment is a lever" has two representations reconciled by id: the graph Lever node and the Postgres row. It is the cleanest available split given the standing rule that commitments are Postgres-only and the no-duplication rule, but it is a seam, not a single edge — and the place a future bug would hide is a Lever node whose `commitment_id` no longer resolves in Postgres (the read path holds for that: a missing lever yields a hold-with-note, not a crash).

- Reflection 3 — Qualitative target sufficient, or a pull toward numeric? There was a real, resisted pull. The raise-or-hold logic reads only coarse signals — cadence on-track plus the last `outcome_status == MET` → RAISE, else HOLD — and a single MET observation flips the recommendation to RAISE, which is arguably too eager. The honest fix my fingers reached for was a **count** ("met N weeks running before raising"), which is exactly the deferred quantitative inference (D156): the moment you count consecutive METs you have started building edge weights and thresholds. I held the line: the recommendation stays qualitative and deliberately thin, and the eagerness is a known limitation to judge in the dogfooding week, not a number to add now. The qualitative ladder + raise-or-hold is *sufficient to be honest* (it never fabricates a metric) but it is **thin**, and that thinness is the point — it is the substrate the deferred optimisation layer will later sharpen against an eval floor, not a stand-in for it.

- Reflection 4 — The strongest second instance. A **sequence goal** (unblock-or-drop) — "get a job" or "ship X." It is the cleanest two-threshold test: it exercises the `SEQUENCE` mode and the unblock-or-drop remedy while staying control-self / subject-self, so it changes exactly **one** axis (the engine/target shape) and adds exactly one remedy, reusing the Outcome/Lever/edge shape unchanged. The influence goal (M's Esperanto) is the more *interesting* instance because it exercises control=OTHER and the probabilistic gap, but it changes **two** axes at once (control and subject both move to OTHER) and needs probabilistic-gap semantics that do not exist — too much new surface for the instance that proves the abstraction generalises. A homeostatic re-establish goal is the mildest (nearest to progressive) and would mostly prove the mode dispatch. So: sequence first (one new mode, one new remedy, abstraction proven cheaply), then influence (the richer probabilistic gap) once the mode/remedy machinery has earned a second instance. This is the moment the taxonomy either holds or gets rebuilt; the sequence instance is the lowest-coupling way to find out.

methodology: the instance-one-shape-only discipline (build the full typed taxonomy but instance a single shape end-to-end, leave every other value schema-present and uninstanced) is the two-threshold rule applied to a *domain model* rather than to a vendor adapter — the same restraint that ships one adapter behind a port, now shipping one goal-shape behind a taxonomy. Worth watching whether the second instance (sequence) confirms the abstraction generalises with a one-axis change, which is the test the rule implicitly promises; if it needs a rebuild, the taxonomy was over-specified at S62.

- Live verification (forward correction, run at the operator's direction on the live stack, 2026-06-08). The build env could not reach Docker, but the operator's stack can; the smoke was run, not deferred. It caught a **real bug the green unit test hid**: `_MERGE_LEVER_FOR_OUTCOME`'s `ON CREATE SET` references `$created_at` on the `:Lever` node and the `LEVER_FOR` edge, but `merge_lever_for_outcome` never passed it — `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ParameterMissing` at write time. The mocked `session.run` does not validate Cypher parameters, so the unit test was green while the live write failed — the **S55a-fix MockTransport lesson recurring** (the fifth instance after S4 Langfuse, S55a calendar syncToken, S57 cancellation churn, S58 browser-boundary). Fix `5735d06` (`fix(p16/s62)`): pass `created_at`; the wrapper tests strengthened to assert **every `$placeholder` in the Cypher is supplied** (the class, not the instance); the api image rebuilt + digest-pinned (`make build-api`). Re-verified live after the fix: **seed idempotent** across two runs (Outcome + lever edge MERGE in place); the **graph shape exact** (`tenant=…d001, control=self, subject=self, mode=progressive, ladder=A1..C2, target=B1, lever=…620c01`); **`GET /goals`** reads the German card (target B1, commitment-sourced progress, qualitative gap, recommendation); **the principle held** — after a completion + a `met` observation the recommendation flipped to `raise` ("sustaining B1; ready to reach for B2") while `current_target` stayed **B1** (no auto-move), and only `POST /goals/{id}/raise-target` moved it to B2; **tenant_b returns `[]`** (isolation). The third check (felt-quality): the card reads as **more than a relabelled checkbox** at the surface — it states what it is aiming at (B1), reads progress off the lever rather than asking for a tick, and tells the operator whether to push or hold and why — but the **recommendation logic is thin in exactly the way Reflection 3 named**: a single `met` keeps recommending a raise up the ladder (it recommended raising to C1 immediately after B2), which would walk the target up too fast; the qualitative-sufficiency verdict is honest-but-eager, and the dogfooding week judges whether the eagerness curdles. AC7 and AC8 are now **live-verified**, not just code+test. Smoke artifacts left on the German lever: one completion tick (today) + a synthetic `met` observation ("solid week…"); the target was reset to B1, but the operator may want to clear that observation before dogfooding from a clean slate.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level, and live-verified on the operator's stack (AC7/AC8 pass; one live-caught bug fixed at `5735d06` and re-verified)**. No new context boundary, no new import-linter contract, no audit path added (the daily_driver S58 no-audit posture matched). Only the progressive shape is wired; all other taxonomy values are schema-present and uninstanced (AC9). **Next: instance the second goal — sequence, get-a-job (the operator's call, maximally unlike German, stresses the schema hardest); S63 carries the mode-and-target move to the Outcome node, the thin-reference-node decision, and the migration-discipline check, charter-first.**

## S63 — P16: schema corrections (D163 clarification) + get-a-job as the second goal, a sequence (D164, D165)
roles: architect (the edge→node placement clarification, the relationship-level step props, the multi-lever record reshape, the cross-store + migration-discipline decisions), engineer (the wrapper Cypher + aggregation, the chain remedy, the seed, the live smoke), analyst (the two-threshold generalisation test), PM (the instance-second-shape-only restraint; influence schema-present-only), technical writer (D163 clarification, D164, D165, the smoke, this entry)
mode: build session, executing the S63 prompt (the brief in-context)

S63 corrects the S62 schema per the **D163 clarification** — mode, the level ladder, and the current target move from the `LEVER_FOR` edge to the `:Outcome` node (a specification, not a reversal) — and instances **get-a-job** as the second end-to-end causal goal: mode **sequence**, control **influence** (`ControlAxis.OTHER` — the employer determines the terminal, the actor only influences), subject **self**, with a **terminal** target ("Offer accepted", state pending) rather than a ladder, and a chain of three lever steps that release toward it. The daily driver reads the shape: German keeps raise-or-hold; get-a-job gets unblock-or-drop over its chain. The remedy branches on mode with no shared path. control influence is a recorded field value only — no influence-specific logic (schema-present, uninstanced, the S62 discipline). **Docker was reachable this session, so the seed + the full data path were live-verified, not operator-gated** (the S62 forward-correction lesson). Four commits after the charter-first: 2363 unit+contract pass (**0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock-coupled calendar test, `log/captures.md` [S60c], carried forward); 42 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract); 9 AST enforcement green (neo4j-confined fence over the new sequence Cypher). Browser click-through is operator-gated at `docs/smoke/p16_s63_get_a_job.md` (no browser binary in the build env); the data path beneath it is fully live-verified.

- Step 0 reconciliation (recorded; where it differed from the prompt): **F1 (placement)** — confirmed `mode`/`ladder`/`current_target_level` sat on the `LEVER_FOR` edge `r` in the S62 wrapper (set by `_MERGE_LEVER_FOR_OUTCOME`, read by `_LIST_OUTCOMES`, written by `_SET_LEVER_TARGET`); the migration moves exactly those three edge→node, matching the prompt. **F2 (thin reference, D164)** — the `:Lever {tenant_id, commitment_id}` node carries only commitment_id + tenant + jurisdiction + created_at, no row copy; a first-class graph representation would duplicate Postgres-owned state and break single-source-of-truth, so **D164 ratifies the thin reference**. **F3 (migration discipline, D165)** — `ops/migrate_neo4j.py` (phase 3 of `make migrate`) is already sequenced lexicographically + idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` + `:_Migration` node), the same discipline as relational Alembic, so **D165 ratifies the mechanism**; the nuance is that 0002 lands only constraints, so the edge→node move is the first graph *data* migration (`0003_outcome_props_to_node.cypher`). **F4 (the sequence reshape — the real finding)** — the S62 schema modelled **one lever per outcome** (`OutcomeGraphRecord` with a single `commitment_id`, `Goal.lever_commitment_id` singular, `_LIST_OUTCOMES` one-row-per-outcome); a sequence needs many ordered, individually-stateful lever steps + a terminal, so S63 reshaped: terminal on the node, `step_order`/`step_state` on the edge (relationship-level, not goal-level), and multi-lever aggregation in the wrapper/record/bridge/`Goal`. **F5 (tenancy)** — D12/D63 hold on every node/edge (live audit: 0 bad). **F6 (index)** — D163 highest → D164/D165 free; S62 highest → S63. Confirmed.

- Produced: Five commits. (1) `docs(charter): clarify D163 placement, add cross-store (D164) and graph-migration (D165) decisions` — the D163 clarification (+ an in-build refinement: the edge legitimately carries relationship-level step props), D164 (ratifies the thin `:Lever`), D165 (ratifies the `ops/migrate_neo4j` mechanism), current-package S63 marker + Step 0. (3) `feat(daily-driver): seed get-a-job as the second goal, a sequence` — the sequence schema (terminal on node, step props on edge, multi-lever `OutcomeGraphRecord` + `LeverEdgeRecord` + wrapper aggregation; `Goal` gains `Terminal`/`LeverStep`/`StepState`/`TerminalState` + per-mode validation; bridge branches); `ops/seed_get_a_job.py` + `make seed-get-a-job`; schema.md; tests. - Acceptance criteria: AC1 D163 clarification + D164 + D165 logged, charter commit first (✓); AC2 `:Outcome` holds mode/ladder/target, edge does not — **live: edge mode=NULL, node mode=progressive/target=B1** (✓); AC3 German migrated in place, B1 before/after, no loss — **live-verified after `make migrate`, before any re-seed** (✓); AC4 get-a-job one Outcome, sequence/influence/self, terminal, chain of lever steps — **live: 3 steps ord 1/2/3 done/blocked/blocked** (✓); AC5 daily driver shows chain state + unblock-or-drop — **live `GET /goals`** (✓; browser operator-gated); AC6 remedy reads shape, branches on mode, no shared path — German raise-or-hold only, get-a-job unblock-or-drop only (✓); AC7 control influence recorded (`other`), no influence logic (✓); AC8 tenant+jurisdiction on every node/edge, tenant_b empty — **live: 0 bad nodes/edges, tenant_b `[]`** (✓); AC9 no raw neo4j in domain, fence holds, new Cypher asserts placeholders (✓ — AST + linter green, wrapper placeholder test); AC10 synthetic `met` cleared, German reads B1 — **live: cleared, recommendation now `hold`, target B1** (✓); AC11 migration idempotent across two runs under the D165 mechanism — **live: 2nd `make migrate` skipped 0003, German still B1** (✓); AC12 this entry records Step 0 + the reflections (✓).

- Reflection 1 — Once mode/target moved to the node, did the edge still want to carry something? German sits **perfectly clean**: the node holds every goal-level property, the edge holds nothing but the relationship (live: edge mode/target NULL). get-a-job revealed the edge **does** still want to carry something — but not goal-level state. A sequence's `step_order` and `step_state` describe *how a particular lever serves the outcome* (which step, in what state), which is genuinely a property of the relationship, not of the goal. So the edge went from carrying goal-level state at S62 (the wrong strain the reflection named) to carrying relationship-level state at S63 (correct). That meant the D163 clarification's "the edge carries only that a lever serves the outcome" was slightly too absolute; I refined it in-build to name the relationship-level step attributes. The honest result: moving goal-level props to the node was right and German proves it clean, and the edge's residual cargo is not the old strain returning — it is the edge owning its own relationship data, which is where it belongs.

- Reflection 2 — Did the schema generalise to a non-cadence goal, or did it need reshaping? The two-threshold verdict, plainly: **the abstraction held; the first-instance's data shapes were too narrow and had to widen — additively, not a rebuild.** The three-axis model, the `:Outcome` + `:Lever` + `LEVER_FOR` shape, the `GoalGraphPort` + apps-bridge consumer seam, the wrapper-as-only-Cypher-surface — all reused unchanged in structure. What had to change was the *single-lever assumption* baked into the carriers: `OutcomeGraphRecord` carried one `commitment_id` and `_LIST_OUTCOMES` returned one row per outcome, and `Goal.lever_commitment_id` was singular — all of which had to become many-lever (a `levers` tuple, wrapper-side aggregation of N rows into one record, `Goal.steps`), plus the node gained a terminal and the domain gained `Terminal`/`LeverStep`. None of it touched German's progressive path (strict superset). So: the taxonomy generalised — it did not get rebuilt — but S62 under-generalised the data shapes to its single instance, and S63 widened them. That is the expected shape of a healthy two-threshold result: the model survives the second instance, the first instance's conveniences don't.

- Reflection 3 — Did unblock-or-drop stay distinct from raise-or-hold? Yes, genuinely. Separate enums (`RaiseOrHold` vs `UnblockOrDrop`), separate reading types (`GoalReading` vs `ChainReading`), separate pure functions (`build_goal_reading` vs `build_chain_reading`), and `list_goals` forks at `_read_goal` on mode — the remedy *logic* shares no path, so a cadence goal cannot receive a sequence remedy or vice versa (the route test asserts both directions). The one place sharing tempted me was the **transport DTO**: both are "a goal card," and it would have been easy to let one mapping function fill both. I let the *container* be one `GoalReadingDTO` with a `remedy_kind` discriminator (a transport convenience — one HTTP type), but kept the two mapping functions (`_goal_reading_to_dto`, `_chain_reading_to_dto`) and the two renderers (`progressiveCard`, `chainCard`) fully forked, branching early on `remedy_kind`. The line I held: a shared transport type is fine; a shared recommendation enum or reading type is not, because that is where the wrong remedy would leak onto the wrong shape.

- Reflection 4 — What does the third instance need? The **influence probabilistic gap** (control=OTHER), because it is the one remaining mechanic with no machinery: get-a-job's terminal is already control=influence but its `terminal_state` is a bare `pending` — the "did my influence land?" reading is explicitly deferred. The homeostatic re-establish remedy is the milder candidate (nearest progressive — a cadence mode with a different behind-semantics) and would mostly re-prove mode dispatch. The richer, more valuable third instance is the influence gap, and the **lowest-coupling way to instance it is to deepen get-a-job's existing terminal** (one axis of genuinely new machinery, on a goal that already exists and is already control=influence) rather than standing up M's Esperanto first (which moves *two* axes — control and subject both to OTHER — at once). So: third = the influence probabilistic gap on get-a-job's terminal; then M's Esperanto (the subject=other axis); homeostatic re-establish and the avoidance variant after.

methodology: live verification this session was **confirmatory, not corrective** — the first P16 goal-graph session where the mock/live gap did not bite. The new sequence Cypher (step_order/step_state, terminal, the multi-lever aggregation) passed live on the first try, because the placeholder-supplied assertion added at `5735d06` (every `$placeholder` in the Cypher must be supplied) is now a standing unit test that catches the S55a-fix class at unit time. The dedicated structural fix for the class (the fifth recurrence) is still recommended as **S64** and scheduled; but the per-class assertion held, evidence that even an interim guard, once written as a test, stops the recurrence from reaching the live write.

- Live verification (run this session on the operator's stack, 2026-06-08; Docker reachable). Rebuilt the api image + recreated the container (baked-image discipline) before any seed. `make migrate` applied `0003`; **the migration alone moved German edge→node in place** (node mode=progressive/target=B1/ladder=A1..C2, edge mode/target NULL) before any re-seed — AC3 proven by the migration, not the seed. A second `make migrate` skipped `0003` and German stayed B1 (AC11 idempotent). `make seed-german` cleared the synthetic observation (AC10); `make seed-get-a-job` seeded the sequence. Graph query confirmed get-a-job: sequence/other/self, terminal "Offer accepted" pending, 3 lever steps ord 1/2/3 state done/blocked/blocked (AC4); tenancy audit returned 0 bad nodes + 0 bad edges (AC8). `GET /goals` (personal token) returned German as raise-or-hold (hold, target B1 — correctly holding on the clean slate, no `met` to flip it) and get-a-job as unblock-or-drop (recommendation `unblock`, active "Apply to target roles", reason offering both unblock and drop, terminal pending) — the remedy reads the shape, no crossing (AC5/AC6/AC7). `GET /goals` with a tenant_b token returned `[]` (AC8 isolation). `/app` serves 200 with the chain-rendering code present; the literal browser click-through is the operator's final confirmation.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level and live-verified on the operator's stack (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC10/AC11 all live-confirmed; the browser click-through operator-gated)**. The D163 clarification landed (goal-level props on the node, refined to note the edge's relationship-level step props); D164 + D165 ratify the thin reference and the migration mechanism. Two goal shapes wired (progressive + sequence); influence semantics, homeostatic re-establish, the avoidance variant, the balance layer, the capture UI, and German's second lever remain schema-present/deferred. **Next: the dogfooding week runs on these two goals; S64 is the recommended test-integrity slice (the mock-hidden Cypher-placeholder class structural fix + the clock-seam test red since S60c); the third goal instance is the influence probabilistic gap, lowest-coupling on get-a-job's existing terminal.**

## S65 — P17: task ingestion (Google Tasks), Wave 2 of Phase 2-A (D167)
roles: architect (the provider-identity-vs-enum call against D155, the third-instance + substrate-extraction disposition, the per-context cache shape), engineer (the tasks context, Nango adapter, store + migration, sync pipeline, daily-driver view, ops pull, live smoke), analyst (the Google Tasks API reconcile, the two-threshold substrate read), PM (the read-only/no-correlation restraint), technical writer (D167, the smoke, this entry)
mode: build session, executing the S65 prompt (the brief in-context)

S65 lands **task ingestion** (D167), the first package of Wave 2: Google Tasks pulled through the Nango-over-HTTP seam into a tenant-scoped, re-pullable, read-only cache, with tasks visible in the daily driver as their own list — **not** correlated to calendar or goals (correlation is P18). Realized as a `contexts/tasks/` external-cache context identified by `Connection.provider="google_tasks"`, the third instance of the calendar (D148) / email (D151) pattern. Four commits after the charter-first. 2383 unit+contract pass (**0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock calendar test, `log/captures.md` [S60c], carried forward; +20 S65 tests); 43 import-linter contracts kept (+`layers-tasks`); 9 AST enforcement green. **Docker reachable → migration + cache + read path + isolation live-verified this session; the live Google pull (AC7) is operator-gated** at `docs/smoke/p17_s65_task_ingestion.md` (needs a Nango `google-tasks` integration + `tasks.readonly` consent).

- Step 0 reconciliation (recorded; where it differed from the prompt — two stale-model catches): **F1 (numbering)** — S63 highest, **S64 (test-integrity) not yet run**, so this is **S65** (S64 reserved for the precondition per roadmap v8; the operator-gated live pull is this session's local guard against the mock-hidden class). D166 highest → **D167**. **F2 (the decisive divergence — `IntakeSource`)** — the prompt's "TASKS_READ in the IntakeSource enum, alongside CALENDAR_READ/EMAIL_READ" rests on a false premise: the enum holds **only** MANUAL_ENTRY + WHATSAPP_INBOUND; CALENDAR_READ/EMAIL_READ were never added (the docstring's P14 prediction; P15 built separate contexts). `IntakeSource` is **IntakeRecord provenance** (tenant-authored canonical state); a task is a **D155 external mutable cache scoped out of canonical state**, so a TASKS_READ enum value would **contradict D155**. Resolved in the charter *before* the first commit (amend D167, not commit-then-reconcile): source identity is `Connection.provider="google_tasks"`, no enum change; the "unified intake seam / CALENDAR_READ" framing is corrected as a stale-model specification, not a reversal. **F3 (substrate)** — calendar + email are **separate parallel instances** (each own `*_connections` + cache + source port + sync + Nango adapter, no shared substrate, and a per-context `connections`/`email_connections` table — confirmed not shared), so tasks is the **third** instance following the template (no embedding — tasks need no semantic search at P17). **F4 (Google Tasks API, reconciled live not memory)** — two-call `tasklists.list` → `tasks.list`; `pageToken`/`nextPageToken`, `maxResults` 20/100; scope `tasks.readonly`; `showCompleted`/`showHidden`/`showDeleted`; `status` ∈ {needsAction, completed}; **no recurrence in the API**. **F5 (migration)** — latest 0029 → **0030_tasks_substrate**. **F6 (tenancy)** — D12/D24/D32 tenant+jurisdiction on every row, bound-tenant defence-in-depth.

- Produced: Five commits. (1) `docs(charter): activate task ingestion (D167), realized provider-identity not enum` — D167 (index + full entry with the D155 reasoning + the seam/CALENDAR_READ correction + the substrate-extraction debt), current-package P17/S65 marker + Step 0. (2) `feat(tasks): add the Google Tasks domain, TaskSourcePort and Nango adapter` — Connection, Task (+ task_from_source/content_hash), SourceTask/SourceTaskList/TaskPage, TaskSyncTrigger, errors; TaskSourcePort (read-only), TaskRepository/TaskReader, ConnectionRepository; NangoProxyTaskAdapter; adapter + domain tests. (3) `feat(tasks): the read-only re-pullable tasks cache, migration, and sync_tasks` — `_tables.py` + `0030_tasks_substrate` (task_connections + tasks, content D21-encrypted, soft-delete, no embedding); PostgresTaskStore (upsert/tombstone/set-diff inputs); PostgresConnectionRepository; sync_tasks (two-call drain → upsert/tombstone → set-diff, idempotent); sync + structural isolation tests. (4) `feat(tasks): tasks view in the daily driver + the operator-gated pull` — TasksReaderAdapter + build_tasks_reader (main.py wiring), GET /tasks + TaskDTO, the /app Tasks panel, ops/pull_tasks.py + `make pull-tasks`, TasksSettings, the `layers-tasks` import-linter contract, route tests. (5) this docs commit (smoke + this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin).

- Decisions: D167 (task ingestion via Google Tasks, provider-identity not enum, the third external-cache instance; the substrate-extraction debt named for before Trello). Kano: performance tending to must-have for parity.

- Tests: 2383 unit+contract pass (12 skipped; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure carried forward). +20 this session: 5 Nango adapter (parse lists + tasks, Bearer + Provider-Config-Key + Connection-Id headers, showCompleted/Hidden/Deleted params, pagination, auth→config / 5xx→retryable), 5 domain (task_from_source mapping, completed→completed_at, unknown-status default, content-hash sensitivity, blank-id invariant), 5 sync (upsert live, tombstone deleted, set-diff vanished, idempotent re-pull, missing-connection raises), 3 structural tenant-isolation (store upsert/read + connection-repo cross-tenant reject), 2 route (/tasks returns ingested tasks; empty when unwired). 43 import-linter contracts kept (+`layers-tasks`); 9 AST enforcement green.

- Acceptance criteria: AC1 D167 logged, charter commit first (✓); AC2 **reconciled** — not the IntakeSource enum (would contradict D155); the tasks context exists with `provider="google_tasks"` as its source identity, literally met (✓); AC3 the adapter pulls via Nango behind the `TaskSourcePort`; no raw Google SDK/HTTP in domain — AST + `layers-tasks` + grep clean (✓); AC4 tasks land in a cache carrying tenant + jurisdiction on every row, re-pull idempotent (sync test + the set-diff), tenant_b reads empty — **live `[]`** (✓); AC5 tasks visible as their own view, not linked to calendar/goals, no correlation edge — **live `/tasks` + the /app Tasks panel** (✓); AC6 read-only — `TaskSourcePort` has no write method, nothing writes to Google (✓); AC7 the `tasks.readonly` live pull against real Google — **operator-gated** (the pull path is wired; the guard fires cleanly without provisioning) (✓ gated); AC8 this entry records Step 0 + the reflections (✓).

- Reflection 1 — Shared substrate, or third separate instance? **Third separate instance, and it is the crystallise point — answered decisively, not just asked.** Calendar and email are parallel contexts (each its own `*_connections` table, cache table, source port, sync pipeline, and Nango-proxy adapter; the `connections` table is per-context, confirmed not shared), and tasks followed the template exactly. That makes three near-identical external-cache ingestion contexts, past the two-threshold point and squarely in the structural-duplication cluster the P13 baseline named. The duplication is concrete: the `Connection` value object (near-identical three times), the connection repository (save/get on a `*_connections` table), the Nango-proxy adapter shape (Bearer + Provider-Config-Key + Connection-Id headers, the 200/4xx-config/5xx-retryable `_handle_response`), the re-pullable encrypted store (enc_* content + upsert-on-conflict + tombstone + the read), and the sync skeleton (drain → upsert/tombstone → set-diff). The genuine per-provider variation is only the wire-parse and the cache's structural columns. **Disposition (in D167): extract the shared ingestion substrate — a generic Connection + ConnectionRepository + a Nango-proxy client + a re-pullable encrypted-cache base + a sync skeleton, with per-provider adapters supplying parse + column mapping — as a named slice *before Trello*, the fourth adapter.** Three is tolerable; four is not — the same do-not-let-known-debt-compound discipline as the S64 test-integrity slice.

- Reflection 2 — Did the D155 read-only re-pullable cache model hold, or did Google Tasks' shape strain it? **It held, cleanly.** `google_task_id` is a stable key, so upsert is idempotent, deleted tasks tombstone, and a set-diff against the stored ids tombstones any that vanished beyond the `showDeleted` window — the same complete-refresh guarantee email uses. The three shape questions the prompt named all resolved without strain: the **tasklists** are a two-call N+1 (drain lists, then each list's tasks) — a shape difference from calendar's single `events.list`, but identical to email's N+1, so an inherited pattern, not new strain; **completed-task semantics** fit as structural fields (`status=completed` + `completed_at`); and **recurring tasks** turned out to be a non-problem because **the Google Tasks API exposes no recurrence at all** — a recurring task surfaces as individual instances, each a normal cache row, so there is nothing to model. The one real micro-decision was preferring set-diff over relying on `showDeleted` alone (a long-ago-deleted task simply vanishes from the response), which is the email precedent. Net: tasks are the *easiest* of the three caches (no embedding, no chunk store, no incremental-sync token dance), which is itself evidence the D155 model generalises down as well as across.

- Reflection 3 — What does P18 need from this cache that is not yet there? P18 correlates tasks ↔ calendar ↔ email into units of work by title + time proximity (D166). From this cache it has what it needs to *read*: the title (encrypted — P18's matcher must decrypt to compare, so correlation runs server-side with crypto access, noted), the `due_at` time anchor for proximity matching against calendar blocks, and a stable identity (`google_task_id` / the row id) to attach an edge to; and `list_tasks(include_completed=False)` already lets P18 take only open tasks as correlation candidates (completed tasks are history, not work to correlate). What is **not** here, by design: a place to record the correlation edge — that is P18's to add as a **Padhanam-native edge**, never written back into the tasks cache (D166 "not written back"; D167 read-only) — and any link to the goal facet, which is P19. So the cache is correlation-ready as a read source; P18 adds the edge store and the title/time matcher, touching neither this cache's write path nor Google. The one thing P18 will likely want that is absent is a normalized title for matching (the raw title is all we store); whether to add a derived match-key here or compute it in P18's matcher is a P18 call, flagged now.

methodology: the as-built-vs-prompt reconciliation landed in the charter **before** the first commit (amend D167, not commit-then-reconcile) — the operator's "fix it before it commits, so what lands is accurate" discipline, applied to AC2's false premise. This is the second consecutive session whose prompt inherited a stale model the build had already superseded (S63: the brief's edge-placement of mode/target; S65: the IntakeSource enum / unified-intake-seam framing) and Step 0 against live code was the catch both times — the pattern is that prompts written from the charter's *predictions* drift when a later session superseded the prediction, and reading live code at Step 0 is the standing corrective. Worth a methodology note at the next audit: the enum docstring's unfulfilled P14 prediction is itself a charter-vs-code drift that outlived its truth; predictive docstrings are a drift source.

- Live verification (run this session on the operator's stack, 2026-06-08; Docker reachable). Rebuilt the api image + recreated the container before migrate (baked-image discipline). `make migrate` applied `0030_tasks_substrate` to all three tenant DBs; `tasks` + `task_connections` confirmed present on the personal tenant (0 rows). `GET /tasks` (personal token) returned `[]` — the route, `TasksReaderAdapter`, `PostgresTaskStore`, and the table all execute live (an absent table errors, not returns `[]`); `GET /tasks` (tenant_b token) returned `[]` (isolation, AC4/AC8). `GET /app` serves 200 with the Tasks panel. `make pull-tasks` without provisioning exits with the clear `TASKS_CONNECTION_REF is empty` guard, not a stack trace — the pull path is wired and operator-gated. The live Google pull against real tasks (AC7) is the operator's final step (Nango `google-tasks` integration + `tasks.readonly` consent + `TASKS_CONNECTION_REF`), per the smoke; the mock tests verify parse + pipeline, not what Google emits (the S55a lesson).

- Close state: **clean at code+test level and live-verified on the operator's stack (migration, cache, read path, isolation, the /app panel all live; the real Google pull operator-gated)**. D167 lands task ingestion as the third external-cache context with provider-identity (no enum, honest with D155); the shared-substrate extraction is named as owed before Trello. Read-only, no correlation edge created (P18), no goal link (P19). **Next: S64 test-integrity (the reserved precondition, still owed — the clock-seam test red since S60c and the mock-blindness structural fix); then P18 unit-of-work correlation, which reads this cache and adds the Padhanam-native edge; the shared ingestion substrate extracted before Trello.**

## S66 — P18: unit-of-work correlation, Wave 2 of Phase 2-A (D168)
roles: architect (the graph model mirroring :Lever/:Outcome, the daily_driver-owns-units placement against a new context, the at-most-one-facet-per-type correctness call), engineer (the matcher, the unit-graph capability on the wrapper, the bridges, the route + panel, the ops trigger, live verification), analyst (the live-data-distribution falsification + fix), PM (the read-only/no-write-back + candidate-not-auto-link restraint), technical writer (D168, schema, the smoke, this entry)
mode: build session, executing the Wave 2 continuous-build brief (P18 leg, in-context)

S66 lands **unit-of-work correlation** (D168), the second Wave-2 package: Padhanam correlates the read-only ingested caches (task D167, calendar block D148, email-origin D151) into a *unit of work* (D166) by a title-and-time inference and records the correlation as the Padhanam-native **same-work edge** in the shared graph — never written back to any source tool. Units show in the daily driver as units rather than separate rows. Five commits after the charter-first. 2404 unit+contract pass (**0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock calendar test, `log/captures.md` [S60c], carried forward; +21 S66 tests); 43 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — a daily_driver extension); 9 AST enforcement green. **Docker reachable → migration + correlate path + read path + isolation + the no-mega-unit fix all live-verified this session**; the cross-tool correlation proof (a task ⊕ meeting unit) is unit-tested and operator-gated on the task/email pulls (only calendar is ingested for the personal tenant) at `docs/smoke/p18_s66_unit_correlation.md`.

- Step 0 reconciliation (recorded; where it shaped the build): **F1 (numbering)** — S65 highest, S64 still reserved-and-unrun (the test-integrity precondition), so this is **S66** (the operator-gated live verification is the local guard until S64 lands). D167 highest → **D168** (the brief's expected number). **F2 (no Alembic)** — the same-work edge is a graph edge (D166), so no relational migration; the schema lands as Neo4j `0004_work_unit.cypher` (latest `0003`), the S62 graph-node-no-Alembic call. **F3 (the graph model, reconcile-and-proceed not a fork)** — mirrors the `:Lever`/`:Outcome` sibling: a `:Unit` anchor + thin `:Facet {facet_type, facet_id}` reference nodes (the D164 thin-reference rule, never a copy of the cache row) + a `(:Facet)-[:SAME_WORK {confidence, status, basis}]->(:Unit)` edge. **F4 (placement)** — the graph capability (`UnitGraphPort`) lands on ingestion's `TenantScopedNeo4jSession` wrapper (the only Cypher home, the D163 F1 precedent), and daily_driver owns the unit concept (matcher + consumer ports + use cases + apps bridges, the D163 F2 goal-layer shape) — no new context, no new context-independence contract. **F5 (idempotency + P19-stability)** — correlation is derived state recomputed from the caches (D155); unit identity is deterministic (`uuid5(tenant + anchor facet)`, anchor priority task > meeting > email) so re-correlation is idempotent and ids stay stable for P19's goal facet; each run replaces the facet links and prunes stale units.

- Produced: Five commits after the charter-first (`docs(charter): activate unit-of-work correlation (D168)` — D168 index/entry, current-package P18/S66 marker + Step 0, schema.md `:Unit`/`:Facet`/`SAME_WORK` section, `0004_work_unit.cypher`). (1) `feat(units): the work-unit domain + the title-and-time correlation matcher` — `work_unit.py` (WorkFacet/WorkUnit/FacetLink/UnitRecord/UnitFacetRef + `correlate_facets`), the FacetSource + UnitGraphPort consumer ports, matcher tests. (2) `feat(units): the unit-graph capability on the shared Neo4j wrapper` — ingestion `UnitGraphPort` + the Cypher templates (`_DELETE_FACETS`/`_PRUNE_UNITS`/`_MERGE_UNIT`/`_MERGE_FACET_LINK`/`_LIST_UNITS`) + wrapper `replace_units`/`list_units` + the `Neo4jGraphRepository` methods, wrapper tests (incl. the every-$placeholder-supplied contract). (3) `feat(units): correlate use case, units reader, the daily-driver units view` — `correlate_units`/`list_units` use cases, `unit_view.py` (build_unit_views), the apps `FacetSourceAdapter` + `UnitGraphAdapter` + main wiring, `GET /units` + UnitDTO, the `/app` Units panel, `ops/correlate_units.py` + `make correlate-units`, the `DAILY_DRIVER_UNITS_READ`/`_CORRELATE` permissions, route tests. (4) `test(p18/s66): … units perms` — the two exact-permission-set assertions. (5) this docs commit (smoke + captures + this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin).

- Decisions: D168 (unit-of-work correlation as a Padhanam-native graph layer, references D166; the same-work edge, never written back; derived-state idempotency with deterministic unit identity). Kano: performance (the cross-tool unit is the assess-not-replace differentiator's first concrete read).

- Tests: 2404 unit+contract pass (12 skipped; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure carried forward, 0 new). +21 this session: 12 matcher (normalise; title+time → confirmed; title-only → candidate; missing-time → candidate; anchor self-link; distinct titles; blank titles; deterministic id; anchor priority; tenant-scoped id; **same-type duplicates do not collapse**; **cross-type pairs nearest-in-time**), 3 unit-graph wrapper (replace deletes+prunes+merges with bound tenant + the $placeholder contract; empty-still-clears; list aggregates), 6 unit application+view (correlate matches+replaces; correlate authz; list enriches; list authz; build marks candidate+removed; build orders correlated-first), 2 route (/units returns a correlated unit; empty when unwired). 43 import-linter contracts kept; 9 AST enforcement green.

- Acceptance criteria (P18 leg of the brief): correlated units in the graph linking task/calendar/email via the native same-work edge (✓ — `correlate_units` writes the subgraph, live-verified 979 units); units shown in the daily driver as units not separate rows (✓ — `GET /units` + the Units panel, facets grouped); D168 referencing D166, number+text reconciled (✓); the linking inference by title and time, high-precision, confirm-not-assume (✓ — at-most-one-facet-per-type, nearest-time cross-type pairing, candidate below floor); the edge is native and never written back (✓ — graph-only, caches read-only, AST/lint clean); a low-confidence match is a candidate not auto-linked (✓ — `status=candidate` surfaced as suggestion-to-confirm); a wrong link is reversible (✓ — derived state, re-correlation corrects; manual pin/unlink named deferred); tenant-scoped (✓ — wrapper binds tenant_id, live tenant_b `[]`); idempotent (✓ — deterministic ids + replace).

- Reflection 1 — Did correlation hold across three sources, or did the no-shared-identifier inference need a confidence floor? Both, and the floor earned itself. The inference holds: facets sharing a normalised title correlate, a corroborating time anchor confirms, a title-only match is a candidate — and the floor (0.8) is exactly what separates "auto-link the task to the meeting that share a title and a day" from "surface, for the operator to confirm, the task and the meeting that share a title but sit 40 days apart." The decisive lesson was a **live-data-distribution** one (captures [S66], the sixth live-substrate instance and a new face): the first matcher grouped purely by title and collapsed ~84 recurring calendar instances of one title into a single 84-facet mega-unit — internally correct, fully unit-tested on synthetic fixtures, and wrong on the real corpus. The fix is the genuinely-correct model D166 implies: **a unit binds at most one facet per type** (the cross-tool link is the differentiator, not same-type recurrence collapse), with same-type duplicates staying separate units and cross-type facets pairing one-to-one by nearest time. Without the live run this would have shipped green.

- Reflection 2 — What does P19 need from the unit that is not there yet? P19 reads orphan work (a unit pointing at no goal) and the neglected goal (a goal nothing points at), against the seeded goals. From this layer it has what it needs: a stable `:Unit` node (deterministic id, survives re-correlation) to attach a goal-facet edge to (the P19 `LEVER_FOR`-style edge from `:Unit` to `:Outcome`), and `list_units` to enumerate units for the orphan scan. Two things P19 must handle that S66 surfaced: (a) **recurrence noise** — 979 single-facet units, most of them recurring calendar instances, would each read as an "orphan" without dedup; P19's orphan read should fold recurrences (by `recurring_event_id` or title) so the neglected-goal/orphan-work signal is not drowned (the reverse-Kano restraint lesson, [S57], applied to a read rather than a push). (b) **the homeostatic/owed clause** (D166): a meeting that is pure maintenance is not "orphan work," so the orphan read must not flag every goal-less unit — the purpose-is-broader-than-goal-advancement clause is P19's to honour.

- Reflection 3 — Did the daily_driver-owns-units placement hold, or should this have been a new context? It held, and it was the right reconcile-and-proceed call. The goal-layer precedent (S62: graph capability in ingestion's wrapper, the concept owned by daily_driver, bridges in apps) transferred exactly — correlation added one domain module, two consumer ports, two use cases, two apps bridges, and a route, with no new context boundary and no new import-linter contract. The one hexagonal catch the linter found (the view projection in domain importing the read record from ports) was the right kind of catch: it forced the read records (`UnitRecord`/`UnitFacetRef`) into the domain where the GoalGraphPort-returns-domain precedent already puts them, leaving ports importing domain (legal) rather than the reverse. A separate `contexts/work_units/` would have been a new context boundary for a layer that is, structurally, a second instance of the goal-layer shape — over-engineering against the established sibling.

methodology: the live run was load-bearing in a new way — it caught a *pure-domain* bug (the matcher), not a substrate or vendor-contract bug, because the failure lived in the gap between the author's assumed data distribution (synthetic fixtures: distinct titles, one-of-each-type) and the real corpus (many same-title recurrences). The standing "verify on live substrate" discipline already covered substrate behaviour, vendor contracts, runtime state-churn, the browser boundary, and mock-blindness; this adds *real-data-distribution* as a sixth face, recorded as a new clause on the held live-substrate-verification-gate candidate. The corrective generalises: a heuristic over ingested data is not done when its unit tests are green; it is done when it has run against a representative real corpus.

- Live verification (run this session on the operator's stack, 2026-06-08; Docker reachable). Rebuilt the api image + recreated the container before migrate (baked-image discipline; new digest pinned in `compose.yaml`). `python -m ops.migrate_neo4j` applied `0004_work_unit`; `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` confirms `unit_unique_per_tenant` + `facet_unique_per_tenant`. `GET /units` (personal token) → `[]` before, **979 units** after `ops.correlate_units` — the route, `UnitGraphAdapter`, `Neo4jGraphRepository`, and the `list_units` Cypher all execute live (an absent graph errors, not returns `[]`). The no-mega-unit fix verified: **max 1 facet/unit, 0 duplicate-facet-type units**. `GET /units` (tenant_b, real provisioned tenant) → `[]` (isolation). `GET /app` serves 200 with the Units panel. The cross-tool correlation (a task ⊕ meeting unit) is unit-tested; live it is operator-gated on the task/email pulls (only calendar is ingested for the personal tenant), per the smoke.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level and live-verified on the operator's stack** (migration, correlate path, read path, isolation, the no-mega-unit fix all live; the cross-tool proof unit-tested + operator-gated). D168 lands correlation as the Padhanam-native same-work graph layer, derived state with deterministic unit identity, read-only and never written back. **Next in the Wave 2 runway: P19 (S67) — goal-aligned assessment, the moat (the dogfoodable threshold): orphan work + the neglected goal, recommendation-shaped, against the six seeded goals (seed before P19). S64 test-integrity still owed.**
