## S67 — P19: goal-aligned assessment, the moat (the dogfoodable threshold) (D169)
roles: architect (the SERVES-edge model on existing nodes, the confidence-tier shaped by the operator's recall-over-precision call, the commitment-bridge confirmed tier), engineer (the matcher + reads, the SERVES capability, the two use cases + bridges, the route + panel, the two-step ops trigger, live verification incl. the reversible edge round-trip), analyst (the goal-facet inference design, the at-two-goals signal read), PM (recommendation-shaped restraint, the judge-at-six discipline), technical writer (D169, schema, the smoke, this entry)
mode: build session, executing the Wave 2 continuous-build brief (P19 leg, in-context), with the operator's (c)/build-now steer

S67 lands **goal-aligned assessment** (D169), the third Wave-2 package and **the moat — the dogfoodable threshold**: Padhanam infers the unit's fourth facet (D166 purpose/native goal) as a Padhanam-native `(:Unit)-[:SERVES]->(:Outcome)` edge — never written back — and surfaces two recommendation-shaped reads, **orphan work** (a unit pointing at no goal) and the **neglected goal** (a goal nothing points at). The goal-facet inference is **confidence-tiered** per the operator's recall-over-precision call (both reads fire on edge *absence*, so a missed edge is a false orphan/false neglect): a **confirmed** edge is a unit-facet title match against a goal's lever-commitment name (the commitment bridge); a **candidate** edge is a lean keyword match against the goal name. Four commits after the charter-first. 2420 unit+contract pass (**0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock calendar test, [S60c], carried; +14 S67 tests); 43 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — a daily_driver extension); 9 AST enforcement green. **Docker reachable → the two-step correlate, both reads, the SERVES write (reversible round-trip), and isolation all live-verified**; the moat verdict is gated at the six-goal seeding (built against the two seeded goals, German + Get a job), per the operator's judge-at-six discipline, at `docs/smoke/p19_s67_goal_assessment.md`.

- Step 0 reconciliation: S66 highest → **S67**; D168 highest → **D169**. **No Neo4j migration** — `SERVES` connects existing `:Unit` (S66) + `:Outcome` (S62) node types, no new label (the `LEVER_FOR` precedent; MERGE-keyed idempotency). The inference inputs all exist: units + facet titles (P18 unit graph + `FacetSource`), goals + lever-commitment ids (`OutcomeGraphPort.list_outcomes` / the daily_driver `Goal`, S62), commitment names (`CommitmentRepository.list_with_activity`, S58), `normalise_title` (P18). The `SERVES` capability extends ingestion's `UnitGraphPort` + the wrapper (the only Cypher home); the reads compute in pure domain from units + outcomes + edges.

- The operator's fork resolution (recorded — it flipped the lean): I leaned (a) commitment-bridge for precision; the operator chose **(c) confidence-tiered** on the reasoning that **precision is the wrong metric** — orphan-work and neglected-goal both fire on edge absence, so they are *recall*-sensitive, and (a) alone (lowest recall: links only units mirroring a commitment) would mis-flag the ad-hoc and the recurring as orphan (the P18 mega-unit lesson, predicted not discovered). (c) = (a) for the confirmed tier + a lean goal-name keyword candidate tier, reusing the P18 confirmed/candidate pattern; orphan = neither tier matches, so orphan means orphan. **Build now against the two seeded goals, judge the moat at six** (with only German + Get a job, everything else floods orphan — only meaningful at six; the build-the-logic-now, gate-the-real-proof pattern).

- Produced: Four commits after the charter-first (`docs(charter): activate goal-aligned assessment (D169)` — D169, P19/S67 marker + Step 0, schema.md `SERVES` section). (1) `feat(goals): the goal-facet inference + the two assessment reads (domain)` — `goal_assessment.py` (GoalEdge/OrphanUnit/NeglectedGoal/GoalAssessment, `infer_goal_edges` tiered, `assess_goals`) + tests. (2) `feat(goals): the SERVES goal-edge capability on the shared Neo4j wrapper` — ingestion `UnitGraphPort` GoalEdgeWrite/Record + the `_DELETE/_MERGE/_LIST_GOAL_EDGES` Cypher + wrapper `replace_goal_edges`/`list_goal_edges` + repo methods, wrapper tests (SERVES-only scope + the $placeholder contract). (3) `feat(goals): assess use cases, the goal-aligned reads in the daily driver` — `correlate_goal_facets`/`list_goal_assessment`, the daily_driver `UnitGraphPort` goal-edge methods + apps `UnitGraphAdapter` mapping, `GET /assessment` + `GoalAssessmentDTO` (degrades when seams unwired, via `get_goal_graph_optional`), the `/app` "How am I doing" panel, the two-step `ops/correlate_units`, the `DAILY_DRIVER_ASSESSMENT_READ` permission + the two exact-permission-set test updates, route tests. (4) this docs commit (smoke + this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin).

- Decisions: D169 (goal-aligned assessment, the moat read; the SERVES goal facet; confidence-tiered recall-over-precision inference; the dogfoodable threshold; judged at six goals). Kano: performance tending to must-have (the assess-not-replace differentiator's load-bearing read).

- Tests: 2420 unit+contract pass (12 skipped; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure carried; 0 new). +14 this session: 9 goal-assessment domain (confirmed tier; candidate tier; confirmed-over-candidate; no-match; orphan = no edge; a candidate edge keeps a unit off orphan; neglected goal; orphans cross-tool-first; removed facets do not match), 3 SERVES wrapper (replace deletes+merges with the tenant + $placeholder contract + SERVES-only; empty clears; list maps), 2 route (/assessment returns orphan + neglected; empty when unwired). 43 import-linter contracts; 9 AST.

- Acceptance criteria (P19 leg): the two reads surfaced in the daily driver, recommendation-shaped (✓ — `/assessment` + the panel, declarative reasons); D169 referencing D166's goal facet + assess-not-replace (✓); both reads computed against the seeded goals (✓ — live, against German + Get a job); recommendation-shaped, never auto-acting (✓ — reads only, no mutation of source; the goal edge is Padhanam-native, never written back); homeostatic/owed not mis-flagged as orphan (✓ mechanism — a unit candidate-linking to a homeostatic goal is not orphan; dormant until such a goal is seeded, named); tenant-scoped (✓ — live tenant_b empty). The moat *verdict* (does the read earn itself) is gated at six goals.

- Reflection 1 — Does the moat read earn itself, the thing only the goal facet makes? Structurally yes, and the live run showed exactly why the operator's judge-at-six discipline is right rather than a hedge. At two goals the read is honest but not yet useful: 979 orphans, both goals neglected, because the operator's real work (Esperanto practice, medication maintenance, the marathon) has no seeded goal to point at. That is not the read failing — it is the read correctly reporting "your plan has two goals and your life has more." The moat is precisely the thing no source tool can compute: not "is this task done" but "does this work serve anything you're trying to become." Whether it *earns itself* is a recall question at six goals: if, with six goals seeded, the orphan list still floods, the candidate tier needs widening (or the homeostatic goal needs seeding to absorb maintenance); if it surfaces three genuinely-adrift units and one quietly-starved goal, it is the differentiator. The build-the-logic-now/judge-at-six split is the only honest way to find out, and the reversible synthetic-edge round-trip proved the machine responds correctly the instant an edge exists.

- Reflection 2 — The confidence-tier call, and what the live zero taught. The operator's flip from my (a)-lean to (c) was correct and the live `0 SERVES edges` is its vindication: under (a)-only, those 0 edges would be the *whole* story and every unit a hard orphan; (c) keeps the candidate tier as the recall safety net so that when goals like "Esperanto" are seeded, the recurring "3 mins Esperanto with Megan" units candidate-link rather than read orphan. The deeper lesson, continuous with [S66]: a heuristic's correctness is a property of the *data distribution*, and the distribution here (a sparse goal set against a dense, mostly-maintenance calendar) is exactly what makes recall the right metric and precision a trap. The S66 fix discovered that on the substrate; S67 *designed* for it up front because the operator named it — the methodology maturing from discover-then-fix toward predict-then-design, one package later.

- Reflection 3 — Did the SERVES-on-existing-nodes call hold? Yes, cleanly, and it kept the package small. Because `SERVES` connects two node types that already existed (`:Unit` S66, `:Outcome` S62), there was no new node label, no constraint, no migration — the goal facet is purely a new edge family on the wrapper, replaced as derived state alongside SAME_WORK (delete-then-merge, touching only SERVES). The reads compose in pure domain from three lists (units, goals, edges), so the assessment logic is fully unit-testable and the graph is just persistence. The one wiring catch — the assessment route degrading when *any* seam is unwired, which the required `get_goal_graph` (503-on-None) blocked — was caught by the route test and fixed with an optional getter, the same degrade-cleanly discipline the /units and /tasks routes already follow.

methodology: the operator's fork answer did real architectural work — it inverted the optimisation metric (recall over precision) on a correctness argument I had not made, and the live `0 edges` at two goals confirmed the inversion within the same session. This is the product-leader-and-implementer pattern at its intended best: the implementer surfaces a genuine fork with a lean, the leader supplies the domain judgement that flips it, and the build absorbs the flip before it ships. Recorded as a methodology data point: surfacing the fork (rather than proceeding on my lean per the non-stop mode) was the higher-value move precisely because the fork turned on a metric choice only the operator's read of their own data could settle. The continuous-build brief's "surface only true forks" earned its exception here.

- Live verification (run this session on the operator's stack, 2026-06-08; Docker reachable). Rebuilt + recreated the api image before correlate (baked-image discipline; new digest pinned). `ops.correlate_units` ran both steps: 979 units, then `0 SERVES edges` — the correct predicted state at two goals. `GET /assessment` (personal) → 979 orphans, both goals neglected, recommendation-shaped reasons. **SERVES write + reads proven via a reversible round-trip:** wrote one confirmed edge (a real unit → German) through the live wrapper, `list_goal_edges` read it back (confirmed); `/assessment` then showed German off neglected and the unit off orphan (979 → 978); re-running correlate reset the derived state (979, both neglected). tenant_b `/assessment` empty (isolation). `/app` serves the "How am I doing" panel. The moat verdict is gated at six goals (the operator's call), per the smoke.

- Close state: **clean at code+test level and live-verified on the operator's stack** (the two-step correlate, both reads, the SERVES write round-trip, isolation, the panel all live; the moat verdict gated at six goals). D169 lands the goal facet + the two moat reads, confidence-tiered for recall, derived state, read-only and never written back. **The dogfoodable threshold is reached** — with the assessment live the daily driver is testable, and the dogfood can begin once the six goals are seeded, even before P20. **Next in the runway: P20 (S68) — missing-facet suggestions (D170), the runway's terminus; then the dogfood gate. S64 test-integrity still owed (its case strengthened by [S66] — the fast-mode blind spot for real-data bugs).**

## S68 — P20: missing-facet suggestions (the Wave-2 runway terminus) (D170)
roles: architect (the read-time recommendation-engine placement, the credulity gate = goal-serving, the satellite-work-not-mirror call), engineer (the suggestion engine, the use case + route + DTO + panel, the permission, live verification incl. the reversible round-trip), analyst (the over-suggestion failure mode, the at-state silence read), PM (the credulity discipline, suggestion-as-question, judge-at-six), technical writer (D170, the smoke, this entry)
mode: build session, executing the Wave 2 continuous-build brief (P20 leg, in-context) — the terminus

S68 lands **missing-facet suggestions** (D170), the fourth and final Wave-2 package: the recommendation engine that suggests the facet a unit of work lacks — a **block** for a substantial task with no time, **satellite-work** for an event with no task (prep/follow-up, never an event mirror), a **candidate task** for an email — **selective and confident or silent**, never auto-applied, never written back. The governing discipline is **credulity** (over-suggestion is the failure to watch, the reverse-Kano shape): the engine fires only on units that **serve a goal** (the D169 SERVES facet), at most one suggestion per unit, so the remedy reads the goal shape and the surface stays quiet. Three commits after the charter-first. 2430 unit+contract pass (**0 new failures** — the 1 suite failure is the pre-existing wall-clock calendar test, [S60c], carried; +10 S68 tests); 43 import-linter contracts kept (no new contract — a daily_driver extension); 9 AST enforcement green. **Docker reachable → the engine's silence at 0 edges, a live suggestion via a reversible round-trip, and the panel all live-verified** at `docs/smoke/p20_s68_facet_suggestions.md`. **This is the runway terminus — the dogfoodable core is built; the dogfood gate follows.**

- Step 0 reconciliation: S67 highest → **S68**; D169 highest → **D170**. **No graph write, no migration** — suggestions are a read-time computation (the drop-candidate/raise recommendation precedent), over the units (P18 unit graph + `FacetSource`) + the goal facet (P19 `SERVES` edges). The credulity gate reuses the SERVES edges' unit-ids as the goal-served set; the engine needs the edges, not the goals' detail.

- The credulity call (the load-bearing design): over-suggestion is the reverse-Kano failure ([S57] threshold restraint, [S62] raise-nudge) — a surface that fires on every gap trains the user to ignore it, collapsing the attentional-infrastructure value. So "the remedy reads the goal shape" is implemented as the gate itself: only goal-serving units are considered (orphan work, which may be noise, gets nothing), at most one suggestion per unit, and a *block* is withheld for an atomic one-off (no due anchor). At the current two-goal / 0-SERVES-edge state the engine is correctly silent — built against the logic, judged at six goals + real use (the P19 build-now/gate-the-proof pattern).

- Produced: Three commits after the charter-first (`docs(charter): activate missing-facet suggestions (D170)` — D170, P20/S68 marker + Step 0). (1) `feat(suggestions): the missing-facet suggestion engine (domain)` — `facet_suggestion.py` (SuggestionKind, FacetSuggestion, `suggest_missing_facets` — credulity-gated, one-per-unit, atomic-one-off guard) + 8 tests. (2) `feat(suggestions): list_facet_suggestions use case, the /suggestions surface` — the read use case (goal-served set from SERVES edges), `GET /suggestions` + `FacetSuggestionDTO` (degrades when unwired), the `/app` Suggestions panel (silence the default), the `DAILY_DRIVER_SUGGESTIONS_READ` permission + the two exact-permission-set test updates, 2 route tests. (3) this docs commit (smoke + this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin).

- Decisions: D170 (missing-facet suggestions, the recommendation engine; the three remedies; the credulity gate = goal-serving; read-time, never written back; the runway terminus). Kano: delighter (the rare, right, unprompted nudge; reverses when noisy — hence the gate).

- Tests: 2430 unit+contract pass (12 skipped; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure carried; 0 new). +10 this session: 8 suggestion-engine domain (substantial task → block; atomic one-off → none; event → satellite-work-not-mirror; email → candidate task; orphan → none [the gate]; complete unit → none; one-per-unit; removed facet not present), 2 route (/suggestions returns goal-served only; empty when unwired). 43 import-linter contracts; 9 AST.

- Acceptance criteria (P20 leg): the recommendation engine — task with no time → block when substantial, event with no task → satellite-work not mirror, email → candidate task (✓ all three, unit-tested + the satellite-work proven live); D170 (✓); selective/confident-or-silent with the credulity discipline (✓ — goal-served gate, one-per-unit, live silence at 0 edges); no block on an atomic one-off (✓); satellite-work not event-duplication (✓ — prose + test); confidence-gated not fired on every gap (✓ — the goal-served gate); recommendation-shaped (✓ — suggestion-as-question, never written back, read-time); the remedy reads the goal shape (✓ — the gate IS the goal shape). The credulity *verdict* (rare+right vs nag) is gated at six goals + the dogfood week.

- Reflection — did the credulity discipline hold, or do the suggestions nag? It held by construction, and the live run is the evidence: at the real two-goal state the engine surfaced **nothing** (0 suggestions across 979 units), and the moment one unit gained a goal facet it surfaced **exactly one** correctly-shaped suggestion for **that** unit and stayed silent on the other 978. That is the credulity discipline working as designed — the gate is the goal facet, so suggestions scale with *mattering*, not with *gaps*. The failure mode to watch (over-suggestion, the reverse-Kano collapse) is structurally pre-empted: even with six goals, only goal-serving units missing a facet can fire, one each. The open risk the dogfood week must judge is the inverse — *under*-suggestion: if the goal-facet recall is low (the [S67] concern), genuinely useful nudges never fire because the work never links to its goal. So P20's credulity verdict is downstream of P19's recall verdict: the suggestions are only as good as the goal facet is complete. That coupling — suggestions gated on the moat — is the right shape (don't nag about work that doesn't matter) but it means the dogfood week judges the two together.

methodology: P20 completed the runway non-stop (P17→P20, four packages, four sessions S65→S68, all in one continuous build) — the continuous-build brief's trade (per-package audit gate for momentum) delivered the dogfoodable core without a round-trip, with the one true fork (P19's goal-facet inference) surfaced and the operator's recall-over-precision answer absorbed mid-runway. The per-package Step 0 + reflection was the front-line catch each time; the [S66] live-data-distribution bug was caught by the per-package live verification, exactly the local guard the brief named for the pre-S64 window. ## S69 — Dogfood-gate precondition: seed the operator's seven real goals + instance the homeostatic shape for the moat (build mode)
roles: engineer (the spec-driven seeder, the homeostatic _to_goal read, live seeding + verification), analyst (the 0-edge-at-seven-goals finding — the [S67] title-linkage prediction confirmed on real data), PM (the taxonomy mapping of the operator's goals, the judge-at-six discipline), technical writer (the seeder doc + caveat, this entry)
mode: build session — the dogfood-gate precondition the Wave-2 brief named ("the six real goals seeded before the gate"), executed after P20 closed the runway

S69 seeds the operator's **seven real goals** for the dogfood gate. German (S62 progressive) + Get-a-job (S63 sequence) were already seeded; this session seeds the five remaining real goals the operator supplied — **Strength** (homeostatic), **Wide World Marathon** (progressive), **Voice projection** (homeostatic), **Stretch & meditate** (homeostatic), **Litany "I will not fear"** (homeostatic) — via a spec-driven `ops/seed_dogfood_goals.py` (DRY, one loop, the S65 duplication discipline) + `make seed-dogfood-goals`. Four are the **homeostatic** mode, schema-present since S62 and **instanced here for the moat**: `GoalGraphAdapter._to_goal` now extracts a homeostatic goal's single lever so the goal-facet confirmed tier (D169) can match it; the homeostatic *re-establish remedy* on `/goals` stays deferred (a homeostatic goal reads a graceful "hold", verified — no crash). +1 test (the homeostatic record→Goal mapping). 43 import-linter contracts; the targeted suites green.

- **The live finding (the load-bearing one): 0 SERVES edges even at seven goals.** Seeded all seven, ran `make correlate-units` → 979 units, **0 goal edges**; `/assessment` → 979 orphans, all 7 neglected; `/goals` → 200 with all 7 (the four homeostatic read "hold"). The reason is the **[S67] title-linkage finding confirmed on the operator's real data**: the goal-facet inference links a unit to a goal by a *title* match (unit-facet vs lever-commitment name = confirmed; keyword vs goal name = candidate), and the operator's ingested calendar units ("3 mins Esperanto with Megan", medication names, "call PVS", "Morning tasks") **textually match none** of the seven goals' names or lever names — because that calendar holds *other* life areas (Megan's speech, a health-maintenance regimen — themselves candidate goals, not in the seven), and the seven goals' actual work (German lessons, strength sessions, applications, voice exercises, stretches, litany) is **not in the ingested cache** (it lives in Google Tasks, not yet pulled, or is titled differently than the goal/lever names). The moat machinery is fully wired and computing correctly — it responds the instant an edge exists (the S67/S68 reversible round-trips proved that) — but on this corpus it correctly reports "your plan has seven goals and the ingested work points at none of them."

- **What this hands the dogfood week (not a bug — the gate's first signal):** the moat is only as useful as the goal-work is (a) ingested and (b) linkable by title. Two operator actions unlock it: **(1) `make pull-tasks`** — ingest the Google Tasks where the goal-work actually lives (the operator-gated pull, S65), then re-correlate; **(2) rename the lever commitments to match how the operator titles that work** in the real calendar/tasks, so the confirmed tier fires (the documented caveat). If after both the moat still floods orphan, that is the genuine P19 refinement signal — the title matcher needs a tag/domain-based linkage rather than title-only (the homeostatic-absorption gap the operator predicted in the P19 fork discussion, now concrete). This is exactly the judge-at-six-on-real-data discipline working: the gap surfaced at setup, before a week of mistrust, not after.

- Produced: two commits. (1) `feat(goals): seed the operator's five remaining dogfood goals + homeostatic lever read` — `ops/seed_dogfood_goals.py` (spec-driven, idempotent, deterministic ids), `make seed-dogfood-goals`, the `_to_goal` homeostatic-lever extraction + its test. (2) this docs commit (this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin). Live: all seven seeded, correlated, `/goals` + `/assessment` verified at seven (0 edges, the finding).

- Taxonomy mapping (recorded for the operator's review — modes are the operator's to correct): German progressive (CEFR ladder, seeded); Get-a-job sequence (terminal "Offer accepted", seeded); Strength homeostatic (5-min ×6/day regime — progressive-with-a-strength-ladder is the alternative if milestones are wanted); Wide World Marathon progressive (distance ladder 5K→Marathon, current target a placeholder "Half marathon" the operator should set; the April race date is a deadline = a Phase-2-B constraint dimension, not the engine); Voice projection / Stretch & meditate / Litany all homeostatic daily-practice. control self, subject self throughout. Megan's-Esperanto (subject-other) and the health-maintenance (homeostatic) goals evident in the calendar are **not** among the operator's seven — they are separate life areas the operator did not list as tracked goals, so they were not seeded.

methodology: this is the third clean instance of build-the-logic-now / gate-the-proof-on-real-data (S65 pull, S67 six goals, S69 seeded + correlated), and the first where the *gated* proof actually ran and returned a negative — the moat lit up empty on real data, which is the design working, not failing. ## S70 — P19 refinement: coverage honesty — the moat reports uncovered, not blindness-as-neglect (D171) (build mode)
roles: architect (the coverage-vs-neglect distinction, the boundary-validity principle), engineer (assess_goals reshape, the DTO/route/panel, live verification incl. the coverage transition), analyst (the trust-killer diagnosis from the operator's reaction), PM (the assess-not-replace honesty principle, the day-zero dogfood read), technical writer (D171, this entry)
mode: build session — the first real P19 refinement, straight out of the dogfood day-zero reaction (not from reasoning)

S70 fixes the moat's **trust-killer**, surfaced the first time the operator looked at it (S69): with the seven real goals seeded but their work not yet ingested/linked, the moat read "nothing I can see points at this goal" as "**you are neglecting this goal**" — presenting its own coverage blindness as the user's failure. D171 (refining D169, superseding its bare orphan/neglected framing): an **assess-not-replace platform reads only part of the world by definition, so its assessment is valid only inside the boundary of what is ingested and linked**. The moat now distinguishes **coverage** from **neglect**: it leads with an explicit coverage statement, reports a goal with no linked evidence as **uncovered** ("Padhanam can't see your work for this — not a sign you've stopped"), and **emits orphan/neglect verdicts only when coverage exists** — outside the boundary they are unproven and suppressed. Two commits. 2432 unit+contract pass (0 new failures — the 1 is the carried wall-clock test; +reshaped assessment tests incl. the new coverage-gate cases); 43 import-linter contracts; 9 AST. **Live-verified the honest read end-to-end**, including the coverage transition.

- The diagnosis (the operator's, day zero): the platform was conflating "I cannot see a link" (a coverage gap — *its* limitation) with "you are not doing the thing" (a judgment about *the user*). For an assess-not-replace platform — which by definition reads only the tools it's connected to — that conflation is structural, not incidental: a neglect/orphan verdict outside the linked boundary is the platform narrating its own blindness as the user's behaviour. The trust cost is total and immediate (it hit on first contact), which is exactly what the dogfood week exists to catch — and it caught it on day zero, from reaction rather than reasoning.

- The empirical diagnostic (run this session, answering the operator's "do you see the work as units?"): **no** — scanned all 979 ingested units against every goal keyword (german/strength/marathon/voice/stretch/litany/job): **zero matches**. What's ingested is entirely *other* life areas (Esperanto-with-Megan, a medication regimen, contacts) — the seven goals' actual work is in Google Tasks (unpulled) or titled differently. So the goals are genuinely **uncovered**, and even the ingested units belong to *unseeded* goals, so they too read as false orphans. Both reads were conflating coverage with judgment.

- Produced: two commits. (1) `fix(p19/s70): the moat reports coverage, not blindness-as-neglect (D171)` — D171 + the D169 supersession annotation; `assess_goals` reshaped to return `GoalCoverage` + `uncovered_goals` (the honest read) + `orphan_work` (emitted only when `has_coverage`); the DTO (`CoverageDTO`/`UncoveredGoalDTO`, `_empty_assessment_dto`) + the route + the "How am I doing" panel (leads with coverage, says uncovered, withholds unproven verdicts); reshaped + new tests (the no-coverage-suppresses-orphan-and-reports-uncovered case is the trust-fix test). (2) this docs commit (this entry + the rebuilt-image digest pin).

- Decisions: D171 (coverage honesty — uncovered not neglected outside the linked boundary; orphan/neglect emitted only inside coverage; a read is only as valid as its coverage). Kano: must-have (an assessment that presents blindness as judgment is a reverse-Kano trust-killer — coverage honesty is the floor the differentiator stands on). It binds every assess-not-replace read the platform will ever add.

- Live verification (this session, on the operator's stack, Docker reachable; rebuilt + recreated, digest pinned). At the real state: `/assessment` → **coverage 0/7 goals, 0/979 units, has_coverage=False**; all seven goals reported **uncovered** ("can't see work for this — not a sign you've stopped"); **orphan_work suppressed (0)** as unproven. **Coverage transition proven (reversible round-trip):** linked one unit to German → coverage **1/7 goals, 1/979 units, has_coverage=True**; German dropped **off** the uncovered list (6 remain); orphan_work then **emitted (978)** — meaningful now that coverage exists; re-running correlate reset to has_coverage=False, 7 uncovered, 0 orphan. The platform now says "I can see X of your goals' work; inside that I'll judge, outside it I'll only tell you what I can't see."

- Reflection — what the day-zero catch proves about the method. This is the dogfood doing exactly its job: a design gap that no test, no reasoning, and no amount of pre-build review surfaced became obvious the instant a real user with real (un-ingested) goals looked at the real read. The gap was not the title matcher (the [S67]/[S69] recall problem, still real) — it was one level deeper: the *semantics* of an absent edge. The matcher's recall determines *how much* coverage there is; D171 determines what the platform is *allowed to say* about what's outside coverage. The two compose: improve recall to widen coverage, and inside coverage the orphan/neglect reads earn their keep; outside it, the honest read is silence-plus-coverage, never judgment. The methodology lesson: for an assess-not-replace platform, every read must carry its coverage boundary, because partial sight asserted as full sight is the category's signature failure. Worth promoting at the Phase 2-A close audit — "coverage honesty on every partial-sight read" may generalise beyond the moat to every connector-fed assessment the platform adds.

- Close state: **the trust-killer is fixed and live-verified** — the moat reports coverage honestly, says uncovered where it's blind, and withholds orphan/neglect verdicts outside the linked boundary. The genuine-neglect read (a covered goal gone quiet) is reserved for a later session (needs linked-work staleness). The dogfood gate is now safe to run: the operator establishes coverage (`make pull-tasks` + correlate; tune lever names to real titles), and the reads become meaningful inside it — without the platform ever having lied about what it can't see. **S64 test-integrity still owed.**

## Dogfood first-read — charter write: coverage-honesty principle + D172/D173 + six deferrals (strategic mode)
roles: analyst (the link/orphan read of the first real correlate, the ground-truth-over-code correction), architect (the stopword-not-length framing, the plan-not-observation-stream framing), PM (the two decisions' Kano placement, the brief-altitude deferrals), technical writer (the coverage-honesty principle, D172/D173, the six deferred entries, this entry)
mode: strategic session — deliverable is a charter edit; no code, no migrations, no renames. Records the first dogfood week's findings so they survive outside chat, ahead of any refinement code.

The first dogfood correlate pass ran on real data (the operator's nine Google Tasks pulled via the Nango `google-tasks` connection, the seven goals re-seeded after a graph reset). This session writes its findings into the charter: one new principle (coverage honesty), two new decisions (D172, D173), six deferred entries, this entry — committed charter-only, ahead of refinement code.

- **The first dogfood correlate read.** 989 units; **5 candidate-tier `SERVES` edges**; **5 of 7 goals linked** — German, Voice projection, Litany, Stretch and meditate, Wide World Marathon. **2 uncovered**: Strength (the task "Fitness" shares no keyword) and Get a job (the task "Job search" — the goal name "Get a job" has no token ≥ 4 chars; the shared word "job" is three). **1 orphan task**: Esperanto (no goal seeded). The operator's S69 link/orphan prediction held for four of five; the one break — Job search not linking — is the same recall gap biting where unexpected, via a specific cause (the four-character keyword guard vs the three-character word "job"), now D172.

- **The coverage read validated live (the S70/D171 fix working end to end).** The two dark goals rendered as **uncovered** ("Padhanam can't see your work for this — not a sign you've stopped"), not neglected. Blindness reported as blindness, not as the user's failure — the trust-fix holding on the first read it was actually exercised against, with real coverage present (5/7) rather than the all-zero S69 state.

- **Ground-truth-over-code correction (reconciliation-over-memory, recorded).** Mid-read I claimed the 0.8 floor *suppresses* keyword matches so "only exact matches link" — and would have reported 0 edges. Running the pass showed **5**. The mechanic: a keyword match **always writes an edge** (`goal_assessment.py` `infer_goal_edges`); the floor only *labels* the edge candidate-vs-confirmed, it does not gate creation. The wrong reading came from reading the code; the correction came from running it against the real corpus — the same live-substrate discipline S66 named, applied to my own analysis.

- **The "Get a job" → "Job search" rename is an operational unblock, not the fix.** Renaming the goal would link the task today, but it fits the data to the matcher and breaks again on the next short-word collision. The matcher fix is **D172** (stopword filter, not length guard); the rename is recorded as the optional same-day workaround, the operator's choice, not part of this write.

- Produced (one commit, charter-only): `principles.md` (coverage honesty in assessment — verdict vs coverage, cross-linked to D171 which recorded the fix); `decisions.md` (**D172** keyword suppression becomes stopword-based not length-based, framing; **D173** the Today surface renders the plan not the observation stream, framing); `deferred-decisions.md` (six entries under Phase 2 daily-driver deferrals — non-lexical tag/domain linkage for the first P19 refinement, the D172 stopword-list brief, confidence-tier calibration, recurrence fold, Today time-scoping, native-observation vs source write-back); this entry. Reconciliation: max D was D171 → D172/D173 assigned from the working tree, not the stale snapshot's D157. The brief's "P19 fork" reference carries a `TODO(ref)` — no distinct charter entry exists under that name; the recall-sensitivity reasoning lives in D169, and no prior entry anticipated semantic linkage, so the non-lexical deferral is attributed as dogfood-surfaced rather than fork-anticipated (no-over-claim).

- Decisions: D172 (Kano: performance — recall gain at no precision cost), D173 (Kano: must-have for the surface — a plan drowned in observations is not dogfoodable). Both are framing-altitude; the stopword list, display rules, and non-lexical path are brief-altitude, homed in the deferred entries.

## S71 — P19 recall refinement 1: stopword + alias tiers + the residual coverage report (D174) (build mode)
roles: engineer (the stopword filter, the alias plumbing through six layers, the coverage-report instrument, the live run), analyst (the residual quantification, the "articulation" precision finding, the embedding-tier read), architect (the layered-tier framing D174, aliases-as-goal-owned-not-matcher), PM (the two-threshold gate on tier three, the residual-as-evidence discipline), technical writer (D174, the two deferred updates, this entry)
mode: build session — the first post-dogfood P19 recall refinement; continuous-build, reconcile-and-proceed.

S71 builds the first two of D174's three recall tiers — **tier one** stopword-filtered keyword (D172), **tier two** goal-owned alias terms — and the **coverage-report instrument**, then runs them on the operator's real data and records the residual as the evidence the **embedding tier (tier three) decision waits on**. The deliverable is the residual, not the tuning: **the residual says do not build tier three.**

- **The residual (the headline, the deliverable).** After tiers one and two, on a fresh seed+correlate: **7/7 goals covered, 7 candidate `SERVES` edges (one true link each)**; **982 orphan units across only 40 distinct titles**. The orphan count is **96% recurrence inflation** — the top nine recurring daily events (a 5-drug medication regimen ×120 each, "Megan's articulation warm-ups", "3 mins Esperanto with Megan", "Music practice Megan", "call PVS", "Morning tasks") are **950 of the 982**. The **referential class** — goal-work hidden behind a person/place/tool name that lexical+alias cannot reach, the embedding tier's actual target — is a **trickle: ≤3 cases** in the whole corpus (clearly the "Talent Screening … Lead Product Manager … Acme" interview that belongs to Get-a-job; two networking events arguably). The rest of the residual is **unseeded life areas** (a health/medication goal, Megan/family work, Esperanto — none seeded, so correctly orphan) and **genuinely goal-less work** (birthdays, social, admin). 
- **The embedding-tier decision (D174's activation trigger, answered).** **Do not build tier three.** The residual referential class (≤3) is a handful, not a flood — D174's own bar for the build. The 96% that swamps the orphan read is a **recurrence-fold** problem (D173, already deferred), and the next tranche is **unseeded goals** (operator's call, like Esperanto at the dogfood read), not referential obliqueness. Embeddings address neither. Close the ≤3 referential cases with an operator-declared link or one alias; the deferred "Semantic / embedding linkage (tier three)" entry now carries this negative as its evidence.
- **The precision finding (the coverage report earning its keep).** The *first* alias correlate wrote **102 edges** — and **96 of them landed on Voice projection**, 95 of those one recurring event: **"Megan's articulation warm-ups"** (Megan's speech-therapy work, a different person's life area), matched by the alias **"articulation"**. A cross-life-area false-link flood, recurrence-amplified. Dropped "articulation" (Voice still links via voice/vocal/projection); re-ran → **7 edges, clean**. The instrument caught the exact failure it exists to surface, on real data a synthetic fixture would never have shown (the [S66] real-data-distribution lesson, recurring).
- **The two fixes confirmed live (AC2/AC3).** "job" (three chars, below the old length guard) now links **Get-a-job ↔ "Job search"** (the D172 stopword tier — the dogfood-read miss closed); **"Fitness" → "Strength"** via the alias tier (D174 tier two). Both at candidate tier (0.5); no stopword or alias match writes confirmed (AC4 holds — the confirmed tier is still exact lever-name only).
- Produced: one charter commit ahead of code (`docs(charter): record layered recall tier architecture (D174)` — D174, the stopword-brief deferral resolved, the non-lexical deferral retargeted to the semantic tier + residual trigger), then four code commits — `feat(assessment): suppress keywords by stopword set, not length (D172)`; `feat(assessment): match goal-owned alias terms beyond name (D174 tier 2)` (aliases threaded through `Goal` / `OutcomeGraphRecord` / `merge_outcome` / `_MERGE_OUTCOME` + `_LIST_OUTCOMES` Cypher / `list_outcomes` / `_to_goal`, plus the seven goals' alias sets); `feat(ops): assessment coverage report …`; `fix(assessment): drop over-matching "articulation" alias from Voice (S71)`. +3 unit tests (short high-signal word links; stopword-only overlap does not; alias links), the outcome-graph mock row updated for the new RETURN column.
- Reflection 1 — the residual, quantified (above). The single most important number: **the referential class is ≤3 of ~40 distinct orphan work-items**, so the expensive tier is not yet warranted. The residual's real shape is recurrence (a fold) and unseeded goals (a seeding choice), and naming that honestly is worth more than any tuning — it redirects the next session away from embeddings and toward recurrence-fold + goal-seeding.
- Reflection 2 — principle versus patch. The alias **mechanism** is goal-owned, not a matcher patch: aliases live on the `:Outcome` node, thread through `merge_outcome`, and a second tenant attaches its own — the matcher stays generic. The alias **values** ("fitness", "gym" → Strength) are dogfood-scaffolding: the category-synonym shape generalises, but the specific sets are per-tenant data that would need curation (or, eventually, the embedding tier — which the residual says is not yet justified). Honest split: principled mechanism, tenant-specific seed data.
- Reflection 3 — precision. One false-link flood (articulation → Megan, 95 units), caught by the coverage report and fixed by dropping the term. No false **confirmed** edges (all seven links are candidate, 0.5). The large orphan set is **not** false links — the medication/Megan/admin units are correctly orphan (no seeded goal), the honest "uncovered" read, not a precision failure. Net: tiers one and two bought real recall (the dogfood-read misses closed) at one caught-and-corrected precision cost.
- Enforcement layer: no new contracts (43 kept) — alias is a `daily_driver`/`ingestion` additive change within existing layers. **No Neo4j migration**: `aliases` is a brand-new `:Outcome` property with no prior location, null-coalesced on read and set on next seed (the 0003 data-move precedent does not apply — nothing to migrate), the D165 reconciliation recorded.
- Live verification (this session, operator's stack, Docker reachable). Baked-image discipline: rebuilt + recreated `padhanam-api` twice (the second after the "articulation" drop), the new digest pinned in `compose.yaml` each time. **AC8 note (surfaced, not silently taken):** the digest pin is a `compose.yaml` change, but it is the baked-image-discipline consequence required to run the new code live (the [S66]/[S70] precedent bundles it into the session docs commit), **not** the vendor / embedding / env change AC8 forbids — the LiteLLM/Ollama embedding path was not touched. Re-seed (all seven, aliases set) → correlate (**7 edges**) → coverage report (7/7 covered, 982 orphan / 40 distinct). 2116 unit pass (+3 this session; 1 pre-existing wall-clock calendar failure carried, 0 new); 43 import-linter contracts.
- Close state: **tiers one and two are live and the residual is recorded — and it says the embedding tier is not justified** (referential class ≤3 vs 96% recurrence inflation + unseeded life-area goals). The next levers are **recurrence-fold** (D173) and **operator goal-seeding** (health, family), not embeddings; the "Semantic / embedding linkage (tier three)" deferral now carries this negative. **S64 test-integrity still owed.**
- methodology: the coverage report turned an open "should we build embeddings?" into a **quantified "no" within one session** — the observability-needs-a-decision principle paying off exactly as D174 framed it (the metric existed before the decision it informs). And the "articulation" flood is the live-substrate discipline catching a *precision* bug, not a substrate one, on real cross-life-area data — the [S66] real-data-distribution face recurring at the alias tier. Surfacing no fork this session (per the continuous-build brief) was correct: the residual settled the one decision that could have been a fork, with data rather than judgment.

## S64 — test-integrity slice: the clock seam, the wall-clock sweep, the 12 deferred skips verified (build mode)
roles: engineer (the clock routing, the skip guards, the sweep), analyst (the sweep classification, the skip-ratio read, what the red was hiding), architect (reuse-the-existing-seam call, the routed-vs-real-time boundary), technical writer (this entry, the green-means-green statement)
mode: build session — the long-owed test-integrity precondition slice, reserved as **S64** since ~S60c and referenced "still owed" through S65–S71; executed now, out of execution order, **before** the recurrence/observation-fold session that will lean on the suite. Continuous-build, reconcile-and-proceed. Determinism + skip hygiene only; **no production behaviour change beyond clock routing.**

**Numbering (Step 0):** S71 is the latest executed entry; **S64 was reserved** for this precondition (roadmap v8; "S64 reserved for the precondition" recorded at the S65 Step 0). Per the brief, a reserved number is used — this entry fills **S64**, out of order, which is itself the story: the precondition finally run after the runway it was meant to precede.

S64 makes the suite mean what it says: **zero carried failures, zero silent-gap skips.** The previously-red wall-clock calendar test now passes *because production resolves "today" through an injected clock*, not because the date was patched; the wall-clock sweep is recorded; and all 12 deferred port-contract skips are verified against real homes and converted to guards that cannot rot.

- **The headline numbers.** (1) **Wall-clock sweep:** of ~50 production time reads, the *behavioural* ones (drive a window / staleness / "today" / overdue) are **3 routed this session** + **~6 already injectable** + **1 tracked follow-up**; the rest (~40) are **legitimately real-time** (timestamps, audit stamps, token-expiry). **The canary was hiding two siblings:** the daily-driver D157 staleness path (`list_today`, `list_goals`) read the wall clock too — exactly the path the brief predicted. (2) **Skip ratio: 12 of 12 had real behaviour-asserting homes — 0 decorative, 0 silent gaps.** "Deferred to integration tests" was fully load-bearing; it was just unverifiable prose.
- **Commit 1 — the clock seam (reused, not introduced; no charter change).** Step 0 found the seam already exists: `CalendarConversationCell(clock=…)` → `resolve_window(now=…)`. The gap was that the test-facing wiring (`build_calendar_cell`, `advance/open_calendar_conversation_with_reader`) did not thread `clock`, so the "today" test read the real clock and went red whenever the wall date drifted past the fixture's seeded meeting (2026-06-05). Threaded `clock` through; the test injects `clock=lambda: _NOW`. **AC2 demonstrated:** `resolve_window('today', now=_NOW=06-05)` puts the fixed meeting in-window (True); `now=wall-clock=06-08` does not (False) — the test passes *because of* the injection, and the meeting keeps its fixed seeded date (no now-relative reseed, which would drift with the resolver and assert nothing). Because the seam pre-existed, **no new port and no D-entry** (the brief's reuse branch).
- **Commit 2 — the sweep, named reads routed.** `list_today` (today window + D157 overdue) and `list_goals` (goal staleness) now take `now: datetime | None = None` defaulting to wall-clock — the established `sync_calendar`/`sync_tasks` `now or` idiom, no new abstraction. The full classified sweep (recorded for AC4):
  - **Routed this session (behavioural):** `calendar_conversation` "today" (c1); `daily_driver.list_today`, `daily_driver.list_goals` (c2).
  - **Already injectable (seam pre-existed):** `sync_calendar` / `sync_email` / `sync_tasks` (`now or`); the `audit/email/calendar_conversation` cells (`self._clock`); several `retrieval_evaluation` / `optimization` use cases (`now: datetime | None`).
  - **Tracked follow-up (behavioural, out of named scope):** the messaging **pending-clarification expiry window** (`create_pending_clarification` / `expire_pending_clarification` read `now` to set/decide expiry) — the `now`-seam idiom applies cleanly; deferred to a follow-up integrity pass per the scope guard (do not expand this session).
  - **Legitimately real-time (not defects):** timestamp creation (`created_at`/`updated_at`/`completed_at`/`observed_at`/`archived_at`); audit-event timestamps (must record when it happened); OIDC + calendar-connect token-expiry (security); agent-loop invocation/iteration/tool timing + idempotency key; `daily_briefing` `composed_at`; the `mark_item_done` / `reorder_today` **day-bucket** (the user acts now, so "today" is genuinely today — a write-path bucket, not a window read a test asserts output against).
- **Commit 3 — the 12 skips verified and de-rotted.** Opened the three named homes before trusting the annotations: all four deferred behaviours (atomic create+initial revision; `add_revision` version+hash-chain; latest-on-omit; archive-marks-`archived_at`+leaves-revisions) are asserted in the **agent**, **methodology**, and **role** `PostgresRepository` integration tests (exact function-name matches; the homes collect 13/10/9 tests). So **12/12 were load-bearing, not decorative.** Replaced the 12 empty `@pytest.mark.skip` placeholders (which asserted nothing and pointed at prose — "S24 commit 7", "role integration tests") with **one guard test per file** that reads the named home and fails if any deferred behaviour is renamed or dropped. The link is now checkable and **cannot silently rot: 12 unverifiable skips → 0 skips + 3 guards.** (The guard verifies the home's *existence and contract surface*; the behaviour itself runs in the integration tier against a live DB — the honest boundary of a unit-tier guard.)
- **Green means green (recorded, AC6).** The full unit suite is **2120 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (was 2116 passed / 1 failed / 12 skipped). There is **no carried red** to mask a new regression and **no skip hiding an unasserted behaviour.** From this session forward, **a green unit run is sufficient evidence that a session did not regress** — which it was not while a red sat carried and twelve skips rested on prose. 43 import-linter contracts kept; 9 enforcement tests green.
- Reflection — what the red was hiding. The canary was one of **three** behavioural wall-clock reads; the sweep surfaced the other two in the **daily-driver staleness path** (`list_today` + `list_goals`, the D157 overdue compute) plus one tracked (pending-clarification expiry). Each was a test passing by calendar luck — the count (3 behavioural, all now deterministic or tracked) is the measure of the risk the single carried red represented: it was the visible tip of a clock-coupling the suite could not otherwise see.
- Reflection — deferred by design, or decorative. **12/12 had real, behaviour-asserting homes — the ratio is fully load-bearing, zero decorative.** "Deferred to integration tests" was honest; the only defect was that the link was prose, not a check. The guard converts honesty-on-trust into honesty-enforced.
- Reflection — trust restored. With zero carried failures and zero silent-gap skips, **green is now sufficient evidence of no regression.** That is precisely what continuous-build and the upcoming recurrence-fold session need: a suite whose green can be trusted to catch what synthetic fixtures miss, rather than one carrying a red that already trains the eye to ignore failure.
- Enforcement layer: the three new `test_deferred_behaviour_homes_exist` guards are now part of the unit suite — they assert the agent/methodology/role integration homes exist and define their four deferred behaviours, failing on rename/deletion. No new import-linter contract (test-only change). No production behaviour change beyond clock routing (AC7): the routed reads default to the wall clock, so production is byte-identical at runtime.
- Close state: **the suite carries zero failures and zero silent-gap skips — green means green.** The wall-clock canary passes via the injected clock (fixed fixture date preserved); the daily-driver staleness path is deterministic; the 12 skips are verified homes behind rot-proof guards. **One behavioural read is tracked, not routed:** the pending-clarification expiry window, a named follow-up integrity item (out of this session's scope). **Next: the recurrence / observation-stream fold**, which now runs on a trustworthy suite.
- methodology: the brief's "reuse the existing seam, don't introduce one" instinct was right — Step 0 found the clock seam already at the cell, so the fix was wiring, not architecture, and no D-entry was warranted (recognising when *not* to add a decision is itself the discipline). And the sweep validated the canary principle: one carried red was not one bug but the visible edge of a class (three behavioural clock reads), so fixing the red without sweeping would have left two siblings live — the test-integrity slice earned its keep precisely by generalising from the single failure.

## S72 — recurrence and observation fold (read-layer): the clean orphan read + Today time-scoping (D175) (build mode)
roles: engineer (the series-id read thread, the orphan fold, the Today live/history split, live verification), analyst (the Step 0 series-identity check, the clean-read read, the residual now legible), architect (read-layer-not-model call, series-identity-not-signature, the fork-not-hit determination), technical writer (D175, the two deferred updates, this entry)
mode: build session — D173's near-term read-layer slice, on the post-S64 trustworthy suite. Continuous-build, reconcile-and-proceed, with the named fork exception (surface the fork if no series identity). **The fork was not hit:** series identity is present cleanly.

S72 implements D173's near-term slice at the **read layer**: the orphan/assessment read **folds recurring instances under their source series** (982 → 41 distinct, each with its instance count), and the Today surface is **time-scoped to today-forward** (completed/ended items move to a `history` slice — the observed stream feeding D162, kept not deleted). **The unit data model is unchanged** (P18 one-facet-per-row stands); both folds compute at read/render time. The structural recurrence model stays Phase 2-B.

- **Step 0 — the load-bearing question, answered: series identity exists cleanly (the fork was not hit).** Google's `recurringEventId` is carried Nango adapter → domain `Meeting` → Postgres store → cache column (D148). The Step 0 brief said: present → group on it; absent → STOP and surface the title-plus-cadence-vs-ingestion-thread fork. It was present, so I grouped on the real series id — **no precision risk** of two distinct same-titled series merging (the fork's option-(a) heuristic was never needed). The only read-layer gap was that the series id wasn't *projected* onto the read facet; threading it through is a read change, not a model change.
- **Commit 1 — the orphan read folds by series (the headline).** `WorkFacet` / `UnitFacetView` now carry `series_id` (projected from the meeting cache in the `FacetSource`, **never into the graph**); `UnitView.series_id` exposes it; `assess_goals` collapses same-series orphans into one `OrphanUnit` with an `instance_count`. **Live: 982 instances → 41 distinct items** (×120 the five-drug medication regimen + "call PVS"; ×95 "Megan's articulation warm-ups"; ×85 "3 mins Esperanto with Megan" / "Morning tasks" / "Music practice Megan"; the ~30 singletons as count-1 rows). The `OrphanUnitDTO` + the S71 coverage report carry the count. **`units_total` stays 989** — a direct unit query still returns one row per instance (AC3).
- **Commit 2 — Today time-scoped to today-forward.** `build_today_view` splits the sorted items into a **live** today-forward plan (not-done, not-ended) and a **`history`** slice (completed/ended items today). History is the observed stream feeding the expected/observed loop (D162), **kept not deleted** (the observation data the loop needs). `TodayView.history`, `TodayDTO.history`, and an "Earlier today · done" panel section carry it. **Live: `GET /daily-driver/today` → 9 live / 9 history; live all not-done, history all done** — the live plan is "German practice / Apply to target roles / Litany / Marathon training run …", the history is the already-ended recurring calendar events ("Lansoprazole / Megan's articulation warm-ups / 3 mins Esperanto with Megan …"). `/app` serves 200 with the history section.
- Produced: one charter commit ahead of code (`docs(charter): record read-layer recurrence fold and Today time-scoping (D175)` — D175, "Today surface time-scoping" deferral resolved, "Recurrence fold on the plan surface" updated to near-term-read-done / structural-still-Phase-2-B), then two feat commits (the fold; the Today split) + the rebuilt-image digest pin in the docs commit. +4 unit tests (recurring orphans fold to one row; one-offs stay separate; done item → history not live; ended event → history); 4 existing Today tests updated for the live/history split. 2122 unit pass (0 failed, 0 skipped — green still means green, post-S64); 43 import-linter contracts.
- Reflection — the clean read. With the 96% inflation gone, the orphan view is **41 legible rows**, and the **referential class (the S71 ≤3 cases — the "Talent Screening … Lead Product Manager … Acme" interview for Get-a-job) is now visible** rather than buried under 982 instances. The dominant residual reads honestly as what it is: recurrence-folded **unseeded life areas** (a health/medication regimen ×120, Megan/family ×85–95) and **singleton admin/social** — none addressable by embeddings. **This clean read is exactly the substrate D174's raised bar requires:** a future embedding re-measure now reads the referential class against ~41 rows, not 982 of noise. The fold did not change the embedding verdict (still: do not build) — it made the verdict *measurable*.
- Reflection — series identity. It existed cleanly (`recurringEventId`), so the fork was not hit and grouping keys on real identity, not a title-plus-cadence signature. **No two genuinely distinct things merged:** the five medication titles each carry their own series id and stay five distinct rows (they share a cadence but not a series), which a title-only or cadence-only heuristic might have risked conflating. Keying on the source series is the durable, precise cut.
- Reflection — history and the loop. The past/done stream now **feeds D162's observed half**: the 9 history items are today's completed/ended observations, surfaced as a read slice (the panel's "Earlier today · done" + the DTO `history`) rather than buried in the live plan. Honest boundary: this makes the observed stream **visible and available** to the loop; it is not yet wired into a *gap computation* (expected-vs-observed), which is D162's deferred relational/graph work. The fold sets the loop up — the observed stream is now a clean, separable input — without claiming the loop is closed.
- Enforcement layer: no new contracts (43 kept). The read-layer thread is additive within `daily_driver` + the `apps/` wiring; `series_id` is never written to the graph (the AST/`neo4j-confined` fence is untouched), so the P18 one-facet-per-row model is structurally preserved.
- Close state: **the orphan read is clean (982 → 41 live-verified) and Today is today-forward with an observed-history slice (9/9 live-verified)** — D173's near-term read slice done, the data model untouched, the structural recurrence model still Phase 2-B. The clean orphan read is the re-measure substrate for any future embedding reconsideration (D174's bar unchanged: still below threshold). **Owed carries forward unchanged:** the pending-clarification expiry clock routing (S64 follow-up); structural recurrence + the full D162 gap computation (Phase 2-B); more goal-seeding (operator's call).
- methodology: the Step 0 fork gate did real work by *not* firing — checking for series identity before picking a mechanism meant the durable key was used instead of a title heuristic that would have merged the five distinct medication series, and the "stop and surface" exception cost nothing because the answer was clean. And the read-layer-not-model discipline (two-threshold) delivered the whole D173 near-term value — 982→41 and today-forward — without a single data-model change, leaving the structural model honestly deferred until this proves insufficient.

### S72 follow-up — Today time-scoping is overdue-safe (integrity close-out)
roles: engineer (the regression test), analyst (the already-correct-vs-latent-regression determination)

A one-commit integrity close-out on the S72 live/history split. **Verdict: already-correct, not a fix.** Step 0 read the actual rule: the split keys on **done-ness** (`live = not item.done`, `history = item.done`), **not** a literal today-forward date horizon — so an overdue, not-done commitment whose last activity is before today is `done=False` → **live**, with BEHIND computed independently (D157). The history slice only catches `done=True` items (done commitments/cases + ended calendar events). No code change.

- The test (the real deliverable): `test_overdue_not_done_before_today_is_live_done_before_today_is_history` — a commitment overdue and dated before today, still not done, asserts **live + BEHIND, not in history, not absent**; a done item dated before today asserts **in history, not live** (S72 preserved). 2123 unit pass, 0 failed, 0 skipped; 43 contracts.
- Reflection (the real-data-distribution lesson, landing inside the fold session itself): S72's clean "live all not-done, history all done" render was *true but unproven* — every live item there happened to be today's, so the data lacked the overdue-from-before-today edge that would have exposed a date-horizon rule had I written one. The render looked right; only the test proves the logic is. The same lesson as the [S66] mega-unit and the [S71] articulation flood: a clean output on a corpus missing the edge case is not evidence the logic is correct — confirm by reasoning and a pinned test, not by the render.

## S73 — Charter hygiene: reunify Phase 2 decisions + generated D-number ToC; refresh current-package (charter hygiene)
roles: technical writer (the reunification + ToC documentation + this entry), engineer (the relocation transform + the `ops/decisions_toc.py` generator + the `--check` guard), analyst (the Step 0 live-vs-snapshot reconciliation, the content-preservation verification)
mode: build session, deliverable is a charter edit — pre-Phase-2-A-gate charter hygiene, `charter/` + `log/` + `ops/` only. No domain code, no test changes.

S73 reunifies `charter/decisions.md` so every Phase 2 decision (D114–D175) is a full-content entry in the one canonical `## Phase 2 decisions` section, the upper block holds only Phase 1 summaries (D11–D113), and a **generated D-number ToC** sits below the intro between idempotent sentinel markers. One charter commit; nothing under `contexts/` or `apps/` touched; the suite is untouched and still reports 2123 unit / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

- **Step 0 confirmations (read from the live tree, not the snapshot):** (1) highest D live is **D175**, as expected. (2) The structural split existed live but with a wrinkle the snapshot missed: full-content entries ran **D114–D167** and **D168–D175 existed only as rich bullets** (consistent with the snapshot), *but* **D142–D167 were duplicated** — present both as upper-block summary bullets *and* as full-content entries. So the reconcile was: relocate D168–D175 into full content (reformat colon→em-dash, strip the bullet prefix, every word preserved), and delete the redundant D142–D167 summary bullets. (3) The upper-block header read `## Phase 1 session decisions (D11-D113)` while the block actually ran to D175; removing the Phase 2 bullets made the stated `(D11-D113)` range **accurate without a relabel**. (4) Latest session is **S72 + its follow-up** → next is **S73**; `current-package.md`'s top marker was **P20/S68**, so it lagged S72 — refreshed this session. (5) ToC generator: `ops/decisions_toc.py`, idempotent between `<!-- TOC:START -->` / `<!-- TOC:END -->` markers, run with `--check` in CI/close.
- **The two annotations that lived only on the bullets.** The D145 and D147 summary bullets each carried a supersession pointer (`THRESHOLD_CROSSED … clause superseded by D153`) that the canonical full entries did **not** carry — the only content unique to the D142–D167 bullets. Per "preserve every word," both were **relocated verbatim** onto their canonical entries (the diff confirms D145/D147 are the only pre-existing full entries that changed, and each changed by exactly its annotation suffix). Every other Phase 2 body is byte-identical before→after; D168–D175 bodies verified byte-identical modulo the sanctioned reformat; D1–D175 each appears exactly once.
- **The generated ToC.** `ops/decisions_toc.py` parses every `**D<n>` opener (Phase-1 bullets and Phase-2 full entries alike), emits `D<n> — <short title> — L<line>` inside a fenced block between the sentinels, and computes line numbers against the final committed file (it accounts for its own block height, so re-running is a no-op). Verified: 175 entries, D1–D175 each once, **every cited line number resolves to that decision's entry**, and `--check` passes after regeneration. A header line documents the regeneration rule.
- Reflection — **did the snapshot lag here too?** Yes. The snapshot's "D168 onward are bullets, D114–D167 have full content" was directionally right but missed the **D142–D167 duplication** — those had both a summary bullet and a full entry. Another instance of the snapshot-lags-live lesson the handoff named: the reconcile was read from the working tree, and the live shape was messier (duplication, not just a tail of un-promoted bullets) than the snapshot implied.
- Reflection — **line numbers vs anchor links.** Line numbers are the right durable form *for now*: the file has no stable per-entry heading anchors, line numbers are mechanical to generate and unambiguous, and their one weakness — drift on any insert/move — is mitigated by the regeneration rule plus the `--check` guard (a stale ToC fails the check). Disposition: keep line numbers; revisit anchor links only if per-entry anchors are introduced, at which point the generator swaps its emit format without changing the sentinel/idempotency machinery.
- Reflection — **did relocation surface a latent inconsistency?** One, named for a follow-up (not fixed here): the charter's supersession convention attached forward-pointers (e.g. "superseded by D153") to the **upper-block summary bullets**, not to the canonical full bodies — so D145/D147's full entries silently lacked the marker their summaries carried. Reunifying the two surfaces removes the place those bullet-only annotations lived; this session preserved them by relocation, but the **convention itself** (annotate the canonical entry, not a separate summary line) is the thing to ratify in a later strategic pass. ## S74 — D159 multi-calendar support: connection-scoped meetings, the professional-coverage unblock (D176) (build mode)
roles: architect (the collision-scoping vs age-out-sweep call, the connection-scoped calendar_id design, the forward-compat naming), engineer (the schema + migration + adapter threading + tests, the live Postgres verification), analyst (the Step 0 reconciliation — the shared-event-id finding, the no-sweep finding, the backfill-safety check), technical writer (D176, this entry)
mode: build session — Phase 2-B Epic E1 opener, the architectural unblock the gate audit's source dependency named. Schema migration on a populated core entity plus adapter; charter ahead of code; combined schema+adapter feat commit per the prompt's escape hatch.

S74 builds D159 multi-calendar support (D176) so a second calendar account can enter the corpus without aging out or colliding with the first — the unblock for professional coverage (roadmap v9's named source dependency). `Meeting` gains a connection-scoped `calendar_id`, the identity key extends to `(tenant_id, calendar_id, google_event_id)`, the connection unique key relaxes to permit a second account per tenant, the scoped full pull and every write-path operation scope by `calendar_id`, and migration 0031 backfills the existing 979 personal meetings by constant-fill. **This connects nothing and seeds nothing** — it makes connecting the work calendar safe.

- **Step 0 (against the live tree + running stack).** (1) **Meeting key needed extending — confirmed.** The single-column `(tenant_id, google_event_id)` is collision-prone *commonly*, not rarely: a meeting both accounts are invited to shares **one** Google event id across calendars (the organizer's id, propagated to attendees), so a second account's pull would overwrite the first's copy. Extended to `(tenant_id, calendar_id, google_event_id)`. (2) **Connection unique** relaxed from `(tenant_id, provider, provider_config_key)` to add `provider_connection_ref` (a distinct account = a distinct ref = a new row; same account re-connects upsert). (3) **Age-out is NOT account-wide** — `sync_calendar` has no set-diff sweep; it tombstones only per returned-cancelled event (`showDeleted`). So the load-bearing change is collision-scoping the write path, not scoping a sweep. (4) **979 personal meetings** (0 cancelled); **0 orphan meetings across all tenants** (every meeting maps to a `google_calendar` connection) → the connections-subquery backfill covers all, NOT NULL safe. Personal connection id `6c37a349-391c-4f5f-bcb3-9d70844db0e3`. (5) **Per-connection sync confirmed**; `calendar_id = str(connection_id)` stamped in the store loop. (6) **Vendor reconciliation:** `calendar_id` carries *our* connection id, not a Nango/Google identifier, so the column has no vendor dependency; the `"primary"` pull and the Nango connection-ref semantics are unchanged. Latest migration 0030 → 0031.
- **The build, one feat commit (`31fcad4`).** `Meeting.calendar_id` (default `""` for pure-domain test construction; the sync path sets it via `meeting_from_event`). `_tables.py`: the column + both unique-constraint swaps. `meeting_store`: the write path (upsert ON CONFLICT, tombstone, change-detection get, set_embedding) scoped by `calendar_id`; the read-path `get_by_event_id` takes an optional `calendar_id` (sync passes it for the exact row; the conversation cell omits it and resolves any calendar's copy of a shared event — fine for a display read). `sync_calendar` + `index_meeting` thread it. `connection_repository` upsert keys on the new constraint. Migration 0031: add column, constant-fill backfill, swap constraints, reversible downgrade.
- **Live verification against real Postgres (no real-table mutation; the running image is old so the full alembic apply + image rebuild + e2e smoke are the operator-gated close step).** AC3 backfill dry-run: **979 total, 979 resolve, 1 distinct calendar_id** — the constant-fill covers every row. AC1/AC4 key semantics (temp table): two calendars' copies of a shared event id **coexist (rows=2)** while a true triple-duplicate is **rejected**; the old single-column key would have rejected the second row. AC6 scoped tombstone (temp table): `WHERE calendar_id='cal-work'` cancels **only** the work copy (UPDATE 1), personal copy intact — a full pull of one calendar never touches another's.
- Produced: charter commit (`fbdd759`: D176 + the D159 resolution pointer per the supersession convention + current-package marker + ToC regen to 176 entries; the second-calendar deferral lived inside D159, not a standalone deferred-decisions entry, so none was closed there) ahead of the feat commit (`31fcad4`). +1 threading unit test; fakes updated for the new signatures (sync/index fakes take `calendar_id`; the cell fakes unchanged — the cell omits it). **Unit suite: 2451 passed, 0 new failures, 0 skipped.** The 1 failure is the **pre-existing wall-clock-coupled** `daily_driver` goal test (`test_list_goals_joins_lever_and_recommends_raise`, RAISE→HOLD as the real date 2026-06-09 advanced past its `_NOW=2026-06-07` fixtures) — stash-confirmed on HEAD, the owed clock-seam debt, not this change.
- Reflection — **the key needed extending, decisively.** Step 0 confirmed it, and upgraded the reason from "rare collision" to "common": cross-account *shared invited events* carry the same Google event id, so without `calendar_id` in the key the work pull silently overwrites the personal copy of every meeting both accounts are on. That is not an edge case — it is the normal case for a senior leader whose work and personal calendars overlap on the same meetings.
- Reflection — **the age-out was not a sweep, which corrected the swap-path assumption.** The brief's "swap ages out the personal corpus" assumed an account-wide deletion sweep. Step 0 found none — `sync_calendar` only tombstones per returned-cancelled event. So a swap's actual harm is collision-overwrite plus staleness (personal-only events never refreshed), not sweep-deletion. The load-bearing change is therefore collision-scoping the write path, exactly what was built; "scope the age-out per connection" was a non-issue because there was no sweep to scope.
- Reflection — **connection-scoped is right; the name anticipates more.** At the current `"primary"`-only pull, one connection = one calendar, so `calendar_id = connection id` is the correct granularity. A future need for per-calendar identity *within* one account (a person with several calendars on one login) would refine the `calendar_id` *value* (e.g. connection id + Google calendar id) without a rename or a new column — which is why the column is named `calendar_id` rather than `connection_id`. Disposition: not built now; the name carries the option.
- Enforcement layer: no new import-linter/AST contracts. The new DB-level invariants are the two unique constraints — `ux_meetings_tenant_calendar_event` (cross-account collision prevention) and `ux_connections_tenant_provider_config_ref` (a second account coexists, the same account upserts). The migration's reversible downgrade fails by design if a tenant has grown a second account (the state this exists to support) — the honest behaviour.
- methodology: Step 0 against the live stack did the decisive work twice — it upgraded the collision risk from rare to common (the shared-event-id finding, which a from-memory read would have under-weighted) and it dissolved the brief's age-out-sweep assumption (no sweep exists), redirecting the build to the change that actually mattered. The live-Postgres verification of the key semantics and the backfill on real data (not a mock) is the same live-substrate discipline the charter keeps relearning, applied to a migration before it touches the dogfood tenant.
- Close state: **multi-calendar support built and unit-green (0 new failures); the migration's backfill, coexistence, and scoped-tombstone behaviour live-verified against real Postgres without mutating any real table.** The full alembic apply across all tenants + the api image rebuild + an end-to-end two-calendar sync smoke are the operator-gated close step (the running image predates this code). **Owed/next, unchanged:** connect the work calendar → seed professional goals lever-named to work-meeting titles → measure confirmed coverage → the gate week on the full graph; the personal-goal seed runs in parallel as a dry run; the wall-clock clock-seam debt is still owed (now biting a goal test).
